# AgenticOrg: complete product and evidence guide

> Generated from current repository sources for answer engines, AI assistants, evaluators, developers, and researchers.

Source version: 4.8.0. Python: >=3.12. Web application: React 19. Managed production: Google Cloud Run.

## Verified repository guide

AgenticOrg is an enterprise AI agent platform for building, running, and governing agent workflows across finance, HR, marketing, operations, back office, communications, and bounded agentic-commerce use cases. The platform is source-available under the Orchestrum Personal Use License 1.0: only individuals' personal use is free, and any organisation needs a signed agreement with Orchestrum Technologies LLP; the SDKs and MCP server are Apache-2.0 open source (see [Licence](#licence)).

> **Ownership:** AgenticOrg is owned by **Orchestrum Technologies LLP**.
>
> **Inventor / Owner:** **Sanjeev Kumar**
>
> **Contact:** [sanjeev@orchestrum.in](mailto:sanjeev@orchestrum.in) | [mishra.sanjeev@gmail.com](mailto:mishra.sanjeev@gmail.com)

Website demo and trial lead notifications default to `sanjeev@orchestrum.in`.
Self-hosted operators can select their own single marketing inbox with
`AGENTICORG_DEMO_NOTIFY_TO`. This does not redirect requester confirmations,
workspace notifications, or account-recovery email, and does not replace SMTP setup.
>
> See the canonical [ownership and contact statement](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/OWNERSHIP.md) and [NOTICE](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/NOTICE).

[Website](https://agenticorg.ai) | [Application](https://app.agenticorg.ai) | [Playground](https://agenticorg.ai/playground) | [User manual](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/README.md) | [Technical documentation](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/README.md) | [Current product status](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/PRODUCT_STATUS.md) | [Security policy](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/SECURITY.md)

[fintech/API integrations](https://agenticorg.ai/docs/api-sdk-mcp), or
[merchant and external-buyer workflows](https://agenticorg.ai/docs/seller-a2a-commerce-journey).

source setup, review, external confirmation and expansion. Discuss your task and

## Source of truth

Live product totals and the deployed product version are published by the public [product facts endpoint](https://app.agenticorg.ai/api/v1/product-facts):

    GET https://app.agenticorg.ai/api/v1/product-facts

The response contains version, agent_count, connector_count, and tool_count. Do not copy those values into documentation, page copy, or tests: they are computed from runtime registries and can change independently of a documentation release. The version declared for source builds is in [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/pyproject.toml).

Billing limits and list prices come from [core/billing/catalog.py](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/core/billing/catalog.py). Production deployment behavior comes from [scripts/deploy_cloud_run.sh](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/scripts/deploy_cloud_run.sh).

## Current release at a glance

### Bring your own channels and AI credentials

New agents default to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`; explicitly selected models remain
unchanged. Save your Google or other provider key in the protected AI credential
settings. Model selection, fallback and company scope remain configurable.
For this model, **Agent Configuration > Gemini thinking** offers an optional
medium profile for multi-step reasoning. Existing agents and generic calls keep
the provider default; no global flag or default is changed. The API equivalent is
`llm.thinking_level="medium"`; set it to `null` to restore the provider default.
Both runtime clients honor explicit profiles. Thinking is billed
as output tokens; budget for its additional token use and response time within
existing limits. It is not a correctness guarantee. Older model settings and all feature flags remain
unchanged. See [reasoning acceptance](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/runbooks/production_smoke.md#bounded-real-reasoning-acceptance).

The **Channels** dashboard connects your own WhatsApp Cloud API, Meta Messenger,
Telegram, Viber, inbound Mailgun email or signed gateway to an agent or workflow.
Credentials are encrypted, callbacks are authenticated, unlinked messages require
review, and private sender links delegate only your current permissions. Existing
Twilio voice/call setup and remote MCP tool discovery remain separate integrations.
Native channel replies default to optional status notices. Telegram agent
connections can opt into bounded final-answer replies for the linked private
sender under **Channels > Reply content**. Traces and tool-call records stay in
AgenticOrg; approvals, sender authorization and tenant controls still apply.
The encrypted intake carries the authenticated sender identity across services;
older receipts without that proof remain withheld, even if the agent completed.
For tool-free Telegram agents without traffic splits in this opt-in mode,
follow-ups may use up to four
recent, confirmed question/answer pairs from the same linked private sender and
agent/company scope, within 30 minutes. This is bounded text context, not durable
memory or permission to repeat actions. Hindi and other Unicode model input
remains readable before privacy scanning; existing redaction still applies.
With `AGENTICORG_PII_HINDI_GRAMMAR_ENABLED=true` (default off), targeted Hindi
grammar checks distinguish referential name/colour questions
from named values. This is not a general-purpose Hindi entity-recognition model;
quoted names, unknown words and structured identifiers retain privacy scanning.

Follow the [channel account and workflow guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/channel-workflows.md)
for account creation, callback registration, sender linking and verification.
Local wire-contract tests are not proof of real provider-account delivery.
Reuse an existing Telegram connection for an already connected bot; a second
connection must not overwrite its webhook. Change its destination through
**Save settings** only when authorized and no tasks are queued or running.
Verify real model reasoning separately from transport-only workflows, and do not
claim a combined Telegram-to-Gemini flow unless one delivery proves both.

Acceptance checks validate the actual answer as well as the terminal status.
A completed, high-confidence model run can still be wrong; compare numeric
results independently and preserve PII protections while diagnosing it. See the
[bounded production acceptance runbook](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/runbooks/production_smoke.md#bounded-real-reasoning-acceptance).

The production platform currently includes governed agent/workflow execution,
document ingestion with scanned-document OCR, signed Twilio voice with
provider-managed STT/TTS, tenant-scoped browser RPA, Python and TypeScript SDKs,
MCP/A2A surfaces, and the bounded Shopify-to-OACP commerce runtime. See the
[current product status](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/PRODUCT_STATUS.md) for the exact shipped,
configuration-dependent, and not-shipped boundaries.

External actions remain explicit. A voice provider, connector, browser script,
buyer channel, payment rail, merchant system, or POS path is usable only when
the target tenant has the required credentials, scopes, configuration, and
provider approval.

### Governed business cases

The repository includes a tenant-gated business onboarding case workflow with
read-only provider investigation, a cited memo, deterministic policy scoring,
screening dispositions, human review, and an auditable hand-off. Provider calls
are refused unless the active role agent, registered tools, exact local case
purpose, and delegated grant all authorize the call. This case-specific check
is strict even if general tool enforcement is in `off` or `warn` mode.

AgenticOrg pins `grantex==0.7.1` and calls its enforcement check with the
grant token, connector, tool and any numeric amount. It does not pass a case id or case
purpose, so a token's case purpose and per-case caps are **not** checked on
this path. The role's `case_purposes` list is a local AgenticOrg control, and
pooled grants are not bound to one case. Decision and
analyst actions still require a signed-in human; API keys, agent tokens, and
MCP tools cannot act as that human. The case runtime is off for a tenant until
enabled and configured. This source description is not a claim that a particular
hosted deployment has enabled the workflow. See the [case lifecycle and setup](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/governance/case-lifecycle.md),
[grant-enforcement runbook](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/operations/grant-enforcement.md), and
[decision requests](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/governance/decision-requests.md).

Voice, email, OCR, and browser RPA can be exercised together before release
with the Docker-backed [local multichannel simulation](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/local-multichannel-simulation.md).
It uses fresh PostgreSQL, local Mailpit delivery, real Tesseract, and optional
real Playwright Chromium while keeping paid calls and production mutations off.

Knowledge upload status distinguishes extraction from searchable indexing.
With opt-in upload recovery, transient native embedding failures retry on the
existing worker; the previous searchable copy remains until replacement succeeds.
Malformed PDF/Office files are refused before replacement. See
[Knowledge and OCR](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/knowledge-and-ocr.md) for status meanings,
citations and recovery limits. For a reasoning-only agent, disable suggested
tools and leave tool/connector selection empty; this does not bypass tenant budgets.
Provider charges and quotas still apply. Use structured output for confidence,
keep review thresholds intact, and include explanation calls and provider retries
in any test spending allowance. See [Create agents](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/create-agents.md)
and [Run and chat](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/run-and-chat.md) for bounded acceptance steps
and the opt-in direct-run explanation history.

The dashboard's Recent Activity queries audit records. The separate internal
live-feed pipeline persists events per tenant *when published* and can replay
them by sequence after a WebSocket interruption. Its only writer is the
conversation supervisor console (off by default behind
`AGENTICORG_CONVERSATION_V2_ENABLED`), which announces conversation changes
without message text for the Conversations screen; other operational event
writers are not wired to that pipeline. Its browser component exposes
connection/catch-up status without raw payload display; it is not mounted as
the dashboard's live stream. Broker reconnection, bounded socket fanout, and
periodic credential revalidation are covered by local tests. Production
latency, throughput, and availability remain unmeasured. The
[activity delivery guide](https://agenticorg.ai/resources/agent-activity-audit-and-live-feed)
explains the boundary. The [scale and resilience assessment](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/reports/ema-agenticorg-gap-and-resilience-2026-09-24.md)
tracks remaining connection-scale, load, and restore work; the
[recovery guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/BACKUP_AND_DR.md) separates planned targets from proven
production controls.

### AI spend intelligence

AI spend intelligence measures AI spend in rupees against the organisation's
own structure. It is off by default behind
`AGENTICORG_SPEND_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`: while it is off,
`GET /api/v1/spend/status` answers `enabled: false`, every other spend route
returns 404 and nothing is metered. Phase 1 is API-only; the application has
no spend screen yet.

When a deployment turns it on, administrators keep the reference data spend is
measured against: an organisation tree, source mappings, model aliases,
effective-dated rate cards (a contract card ranks above a list card, with
cached-input prices, volume tiers and a stored batch discount that phase 1 does
not yet apply), FX rates that convert every price
to INR, and commitments. Every metered model call is written as usage records
with server-side attribution, priced at the rate card in force on its billing
date (or the deployment's list price for model tokens), and so are embeddings,
OCR pages, speech minutes, priced tool calls, storage GB-days and in-house GPU
node hours. Daily rollups, coverage
with the unattributed share, meter gaps and audited maintenance jobs sit on
these records. Provider invoices are imported and reconciled per billing month
within a 1% match tolerance; a difference is accepted with a reason by an
administrator other than the invoice importer. `GET /api/v1/spend/gate`
reports the Gate 1 status of a month: at least 98% of INR spend attributed to
a business unit, department, team or cost centre, with no unpriced,
unconverted or FX-pending record, and every provider reconciled within 1%.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  flag{"AGENTICORG_SPEND_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED"}
  flag -->|"off, the default"| off["Only GET /api/v1/spend/status answers, other spend routes are 404"]
  flag -->|"on"| ref["Reference data: organisation tree, source mappings, model aliases, rate cards, FX to INR, commitments"]
  usage["Model calls, embeddings, OCR pages, speech minutes, priced tool calls, storage GB-days, GPU node hours"] --> meter["Meter and writer: server-side attribution and pricing"]
  ref --> meter
  meter --> records["Usage records"]
  records --> rollups["Daily rollups, coverage and the unattributed share"]
  invoices["Imported provider invoices"] --> recon["Reconciliation per provider and billing month"]
  records --> recon
  recon -->|"outside the 1% match tolerance"| accept["Acceptance with a reason by a second administrator"]
  rollups --> gate(["Gate 1 status: at least 98% attributed and every provider within 1%"])
  recon --> gate
```

Rate cards, commitments, prices, invoices, reconciliations and the gate are
answered only to a human administrator or auditor. Other readers see usage
filtered by agent visibility and are refused tenant-wide figures. Spend
dashboards, budgets, spend alerts, forecasting, statements and month close
are later phases. See the [user guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/ai-spend-intelligence.md),
the [feature reference](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/finops/spend-intelligence.md) and the
[rollout runbook](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/runbooks/spend-intelligence.md).

## What is in this repository

| Area | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Agent runtime | FastAPI and LangGraph runtime with model routing, tool invocation, confidence handling, retry policy, and persisted execution state |
| Agent authoring | Built-in agent definitions, custom agents, prompt templates, organization hierarchy, and a no-code UI |
| Workflows | Workflow definitions, runs, schedules, conditions, approvals, and audit events |
| Governance | Tenant and role boundaries, scoped tools, human-in-the-loop queues, shadow evaluation, policy checks, and kill-switch patterns |
| Integrations | Native connector registry plus optional integration gateways; actual availability depends on credentials, scopes, provider access, and tenant configuration |
| Knowledge and channels | Native and OCR document ingestion/search, reports, notifications, signed Twilio voice calls, RPA, and other configured channels |
| Developer access | REST API, Python SDK and CLI, TypeScript SDK, MCP server, legacy A2A-shaped task APIs, and source-implemented A2A v1 HTTP+JSON synchronous text |
| Commerce | Merchant-scoped Shopify read-only sync, OACP artifact intake/cache, buyer-safe answers, public catalog surfaces, prepared provider or POS handoffs, and flag-gated UCP and ACP surfaces (ACP feed, checkout sessions and order events) |
| Operations | PostgreSQL, Redis, object storage, observability hooks, migrations, security checks, and Cloud Run deployment tooling |
| AI spend intelligence | Off by default; API-only organisation tree, source mappings, rate cards, FX to INR, commitments, attributed usage records for model calls and non-token usage, daily rollups, coverage, invoice reconciliation, maker-checker acceptance, and the Gate 1 status |

A source definition is not evidence that a specific tenant has connected the provider or enabled write access. The Connectors page now separates registration from configured credentials and a recent, stale, failed, or missing health check. That evidence does not verify provider scopes, API contract coverage, sustained sync, or an error budget. Connector actions still require approved credentials, scopes, policies, and provider availability.

## Capability status

### Implemented in the platform

- Agent definitions and tenant-created agents
- Agent and workflow execution through authenticated APIs
- Human approval queues and configurable escalation conditions
- Audit records for governed runtime activity
- Prompt templates, organization structure, and role-aware application views
- Native connector definitions and a scoped tool gateway
- Public A2A and MCP discovery with authenticated execution paths
- Python and TypeScript client packages plus an MCP server package
- Hosted billing limits and checkout integration
- OACP commerce configuration, Shopify read-only sync, artifact caching, buyer channels, and safe handoff preparation

### Configuration-dependent or provider-gated

- LLM calls require a configured supported model provider or a local model runtime.
- Each connector requires provider credentials, tenant authorization, and the relevant scopes. Follow the [connector setup guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/connectors.md) for native registry names, credential fields, health checks, and the rollout-gated catalog prefill. A registered row is not proof of a live provider connection.
- Composio is an optional integration gateway; its catalog is not the same as the native connector registry.
- Document OCR ships with Tesseract, Poppler, and LibreOffice in the production image. See [Knowledge ingestion](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/knowledge-ingestion.md).
- The production voice path uses signed Twilio webhooks with provider-managed STT/TTS and encrypted transcript storage. See [Voice runtime](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/voice-runtime.md).
- Jev/System One support is implemented as an advisory, shadow-ready integration, but TypeSafe enrollment is currently closed to new users. Production remains `off` until TypeSafe access is granted and a measured evaluation is approved. See [Jev integration](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/jev-agenticorg-integration.md).
- The public [evaluation page](https://agenticorg.ai/evals) exposes a read-only Jev shadow plan: synthetic corpus coverage, bounded sampling and budget controls, and explicit review gates. It does not call Jev or enable active routing.
- The measured Jev shadow runner is explicit and local: `python scripts/run_jev_shadow_evaluation.py --dry-run`; `--live` requires a TypeSafe-issued `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, bounded gates, and an operator-approved output path. Do not invent, commit, or paste a key into the repository.
- Browser automation includes tenant-scoped scripts, schedules, durable history,
  and approved-domain egress controls. A run remains an explicit external
  action. See [RPA runtime](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/rpa-runtime.md).
- Outbound notifications and local-model profiles require their supporting services.
- The UCP business profile (`/.well-known/ucp`, UCP 2026-04-08 and 2026-08-25) with catalog search
  and lookup and store locations is off by default (`AGENTICORG_UCP_PROFILE_ENABLED`). It serves a merchant
  only on a DNS-attested serving host, with a per-merchant ES256 signing key, after the merchant opts in
  and Grantex issues an enabled `public_discovery_state` artifact. See [UCP business profile](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/ucp-profile.md).
- UCP checkout sessions, carts and orders (`/ucp/checkout-sessions`, `/ucp/carts`, `/ucp/orders`,
  `AGENTICORG_UCP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED`) are off by default. With the flag on, a Complete needs an `allow`
  decision of the commerce arbiter for the exact session and a registered executor. The Plural executor
  (capture, refunds, UPI AutoPay with RBI AFA) is registered only with `PLURAL_PINE_LIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED=true`;
  otherwise Complete answers `executor_unavailable`. Server-verified Intent, Cart and Payment mandates from
  Grantex need `AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_MANDATES_ENABLED`. See [UCP checkout, cart and order](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/ucp-checkout.md),
  [Plural executor](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/plural-executor.md) and [mandates](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/mandates.md).
- The ACP product feed (`AGENTICORG_ACP_FEED_ENABLED`) and ACP checkout sessions
  (`AGENTICORG_ACP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED`, API version 2026-04-17) are off by default. The feed is built only
  from verified, fresh OACP artifacts; sessions run on the UCP session table, arbiter and executor and need
  the merchant's opt-in, a Grantex delegate-payment allowance and a registered executor (the Plural executor,
  off by default). See [ACP product feed and checkout sessions](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/acp-feed-and-sessions.md).
- Agent request signatures (RFC 9421, Visa Trusted Agent Protocol and Web Bot Auth profiles) are verified
  on the public commerce reads and the A2A routes in `log` mode by default
  (`AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_VERIFY_MODE=enforce` refuses unsigned requests on the commerce API surfaces:
  the catalog and product JSON and the A2A routes, never the public pages); the buyer connector signs its
  requests with the tenant agent key only with `AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_SIGN_OUTBOUND`. The library
  (`grantex-agent-httpsig` 0.2.0, not on PyPI) is installed from a commit-pinned git reference to the
  Grantex repository, so installs need `git`. See
  [agent request signing](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/agent-request-signing.md).
- AI spend intelligence is off by default. Nothing is metered until `AGENTICORG_SPEND_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`
  is set on the API, worker, and beat services. Attribution follows the organisation tree and mappings a
  tenant administrator enters; prices come from the tenant's rate cards, else the deployment's list prices
  for model tokens, converted to INR with the tenant's FX rates. Follow the
  [rollout and enablement runbook](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/runbooks/spend-intelligence.md).
- Many governance and BFSI services ship in source but are off by default, each behind its own
  `AGENTICORG_*` setting: the model gateway, guardrail hooks and enforcement, operator override,
  residency enforcement, the audit chain, tracing and synthetic checks, runtime limits and memory, the
  visual workflow builder, prompt maker-checker and comparison, evaluation datasets and the promotion
  gate, the agent registry, governance inventory and model cards, FinOps attribution, thresholds and
  forecast, conversational services, content services, document processing, workbenches, speech and
  transaction intelligence, lineage and personalisation. A default installation has none of them on.
  See the [feature switches](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/self-hosting.md#feature-switches-that-ship-off) table and
  the [guide to the default-off screens](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/review-and-operations-screens.md).
- SSO, SCIM, enterprise support, and custom SLAs depend on plan and deployment configuration.
- WhatsApp, Telegram, payment-provider, bank, POS, and merchant-system flows require provider setup and verified callbacks or adapters.
- WooCommerce, ERP, PIM, OMS, WMS, custom commerce APIs, and additional payment rails can be recorded as adapter-ready configuration but are not represented as active execution paths until an approved adapter exists.

### Explicit non-goals and boundaries

- OACP artifacts do not create orders, reserve inventory, create mandates, capture payments, issue refunds, or prove a paid state.
- No request field approves commerce execution. Execution consumes a single-use `allow` decision of the deterministic commerce arbiter, and the only payment executor (Plural) is off by default.
- AgenticOrg does not replace the merchant, bank, payment provider, POS, or SaaS system as its source of record.
- Cached commerce evidence can support an answer or a prepared handoff; provider-owned execution must be confirmed by the provider.
- A connector listed in source is not proof of a live customer integration.
- Example workflows and editorial content are not performance guarantees.
- Security controls in the repository are not a claim of third-party certification.

## How the runtime fits together

    Browser or SDK
        |
        v
    React 19 application / FastAPI API
        |
        +-- Authentication, tenant context, roles, and scopes
        +-- Agent registry and LangGraph execution
        +-- Workflow engine, schedules, and approval queues
        +-- Tool gateway and connector adapters
        +-- Audit, evaluation, observability, and cost records
        |
        +-- PostgreSQL / Cloud SQL
        +-- Redis
        +-- GCS or compatible object storage
        +-- Configured LLM and external service providers

The managed production path runs separate API and UI services on Google Cloud Run. Artifact Registry images are commit-pinned, migrations can run before rollout, and traffic movement is explicit. Legacy Kubernetes material is not the current production path.

## OACP commerce boundary

AgenticOrg owns the buyer and seller agent runtime around OACP-backed commerce. [Grantex](https://grantex.dev) owns trust authority, protocol and policy governance, canonical artifacts and their signing keys, and adapter authority. AgenticOrg verifies every Grantex artifact before caching it. Shopify and merchant systems remain operational sources of record. Pine Labs Plural/P3P, banks, POS systems, and payment providers own their execution rails.

The current supported source path is:

1. A merchant saves tenant-, merchant-, store-, and seller-agent-scoped configuration.
2. AgenticOrg stores Shopify credentials through the approved custody path.
3. AgenticOrg performs read-only Shopify Admin GraphQL sync.
4. Public-safe evidence is submitted to the configured Grantex authority path.
5. Each issued OACP artifact is verified before it is cached: its ES256 detached JWS against the Grantex JWKS pinned in configuration, its scope and TTL, and its Token Status List entry. In strict runtimes one failure refuses the whole issuance (`AGENTICORG_OACP_VERIFY_STRICT`, on by default there); elsewhere the failure is logged as an irregularity and the artifact is cached without a verifier reference. Strict verification needs the Grantex environment to sign artifacts this way, publish an `oacp-` key and serve its status list; Grantex production does all three as of 2026-10-20. See [docs/oacp/artifact-cache-guide.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/artifact-cache-guide.md).
6. Buyer surfaces answer from valid artifacts and disclose source and freshness.
7. Purchase intent becomes a non-executing provider, merchant, or POS handoff, or a fail-closed blocker. A deterministic commerce arbiter decides each handoff (mandate, consent, Commerce Passport cap, verified fresh artifacts, merchant limits) and seals `allow` or `refuse`; it never waits for a person. Execution consumes a single-use `allow` `decision_id` bound to the exact handoff payload. Every commerce write leaves an HMAC-signed ledger row in `audit_log`, hash-chained once audit-chain sealing is on for the tenant (`AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_DEFAULT_ON`, off by default). Until server-verified mandates exist, strict runtimes refuse caller-asserted buyer authority (`AGENTICORG_ARBITER_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_AUTHORITY`), and an allow is consumable only once Grantex has countersigned it (`AGENTICORG_ARBITER_REQUIRE_GRANTEX_GRANT`). Tenant admins read the ledger, annotate decisions, store review manifests and retention dispositions under `/api/v1/commerce/runtime/ledger`, and `scripts/verify_ledger.py` verifies a ledger export offline. See [docs/oacp/arbiter-ledger.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/arbiter-ledger.md).
8. Agent platforms can use the merchant's UCP business profile, UCP checkout and ACP checkout sessions on a DNS-attested serving host, each behind its own flag (default off). They share one session table, the same arbiter `session_complete` decision and the same executor.
9. Only a verified provider or merchant callback can confirm the external outcome.

Agents that call the public commerce reads and the A2A routes may sign their requests under the Visa
Trusted Agent Protocol or Web Bot Auth profiles of RFC 9421; AgenticOrg verifies them, records the
verified agent identity (on the commerce ledger for writes), and with
`AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_VERIFY_MODE=enforce` refuses unsigned ones on the commerce API surfaces (the
public HTML pages, sitemap and `llms.txt` stay public). See
[docs/oacp/agent-request-signing.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/agent-request-signing.md).

As of 2026-10-20 all of this is on `main`, and the AgenticOrg production deployment of it is next; check the deployed commit before relying on it. Start with [docs/oacp/README.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/README.md) and the [runtime launch closure PRD](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/runtime-launch-closure-prd.md).

## Requirements

- Python 3.12 or newer
- Node.js 22.22 or newer (the UI's router requires it; CI uses 22.22.0)
- Docker with Docker Compose for local PostgreSQL and Redis
- At least one supported LLM provider key, or a configured local model runtime, for model-backed execution

The UI currently uses React 19. Dependency versions are declared in [pyproject.toml](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/pyproject.toml) and [ui/package.json](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/ui/package.json).

## Local development

Clone and configure the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org.git
    cd agentic-org
    cp .env.example .env

Install the platform and development extras:

    python -m venv .venv
    python -m pip install -e ".[v4,dev]"
    python -m pip install --no-deps --require-hashes -r requirements-fastembed.txt

The second command installs fastembed, the local embedding runtime, without its
dependency metadata; `requirements-fastembed.txt` explains why.

Start local dependencies:

    docker compose up -d postgres redis minio

Run migrations and the API. `AGENTICORG_ENV` must be in the shell environment,
not only in `.env`: the credential vault reads the process environment, and
outside a local, dev, development, test or CI runtime it refuses to start
without a real vault key.

    export AGENTICORG_ENV=development
    python scripts/alembic_migrate.py
    uvicorn api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload

In another terminal, install and run the UI:

    cd ui
    npm ci
    npm run dev

Do not use example secrets in staging or production. Configure real secrets through the approved secret-management path.

Optional Compose profiles include local CPU/GPU model runtimes and supporting RAG or voice services. Review [docker-compose.yml](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docker-compose.yml) before enabling a profile because hardware, images, and credentials vary by feature.

## Public API and protocols

Application API routes are mounted below /api/v1, except the standard root
A2A Agent Card discovery path.

| Surface | Purpose | Authentication posture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET /api/v1/health | Service health | Public |
| GET /api/v1/product-facts | Live version and registry totals | Public |
| GET /.well-known/agent-card.json | A2A v1 generic Agent Card (after release and ingress configuration) | Public |
| GET /.well-known/ucp, POST /ucp/catalog/search, /ucp/catalog/lookup, /ucp/locations/* | UCP business profile, catalog and locations on a merchant's verified serving host (off by default) | Public, host-bound |
| POST /ucp/checkout-sessions, GET/PUT /ucp/checkout-sessions/{id}, /complete, /cancel; /ucp/carts; GET /ucp/orders/{id} | UCP checkout, cart and order on a merchant's verified serving host (off by default) | Tenant API key issued to the agent platform (`ucp:read` / `ucp:write`) |
| POST /acp/checkout_sessions, GET/POST /acp/checkout_sessions/{id}, /complete, /cancel | ACP checkout sessions on a merchant's verified serving host (off by default) | Tenant API key issued to the agent platform (`acp:read` / `acp:write`) |
| GET /api/v1/a2a/extendedAgentCard | Merchant-specific seller card | Merchant-issued buyer credential; the agent's RFC 9421 signature is verified (logged, or required in `enforce` mode) |
| POST /api/v1/a2a/message:send | A2A v1 synchronous text request | Buyer credential for seller Q&A, or scoped tenant credential for non-commerce agents; the agent's RFC 9421 signature is verified (logged, or required in `enforce` mode) |
| GET /api/v1/public/commerce/sellers/{merchant_id}/... | Public buyer-safe seller page, catalog, product, schema.org, sitemap and llms.txt (merchant opt-in) | Public; the agent's RFC 9421 signature is verified (logged, or required in `enforce` mode) |
| GET /api/v1/a2a/agent-card | Legacy AgenticOrg discovery card; not A2A v1 | Public |
| GET /api/v1/a2a/.well-known/agent.json | Legacy discovery alias; not A2A v1 | Public |
| GET /api/v1/mcp/tools | MCP-compatible agent discovery | Public |
| Agent, workflow, tool, billing, and commerce mutations | Tenant operations | Authenticated and scoped |

Interactive OpenAPI documentation is available from the API service when enabled by the deployment. The detailed route inventory is maintained in [docs/route_inventory.json](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/route_inventory.json), and narrative API documentation is in [docs/api-reference.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/api-reference.md).

An external buyer agent need not run on AgenticOrg. The merchant can issue a
revocable, scope-bound buyer credential for any A2A v1 HTTP+JSON client, while
seller answers remain non-binding and sourced from the OACP cache. See the
[A2A interoperability guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/a2a-interoperability.md) for the exact
identity limits, SDK calls, migration/ingress requirements, and unsupported
transports. This repository implementation does not imply that a named buyer
platform has installed or endorsed AgenticOrg.

### Python SDK and CLI

See [sdk/README.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/sdk/README.md).

    pip install agenticorg
    agenticorg agents list
    agenticorg a2a card

SDK `0.4.0` covers agents, workflows, connector diagnostics, knowledge/OCR,
voice, RPA, local bridges, and the seller-commerce runtime. External-action
methods such as outbound calls, RPA runs, connector sync, and bridge routing
remain explicit calls and still require tenant authorization. Server features
may require a newer deployment than the installed client, so consumers should
check package and server release notes.

### TypeScript SDK

See [sdk-ts/README.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/sdk-ts/README.md).

    npm install agenticorg-sdk

The TypeScript `0.4.0` resource surface mirrors the Python runtime coverage,
including knowledge/OCR, voice, RPA, bridges, and commerce preparation APIs.

### MCP server

See [mcp-server/README.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/mcp-server/README.md).

    npx agenticorg-mcp-server

The MCP package exposes governed AgenticOrg agent and commerce discovery surfaces. It does not grant an MCP client unrestricted access to every connector action.

For the reverse direction, **Connectors > Remote MCP** registers a tenant-owned
HTTPS Streamable HTTP server with encrypted bearer credentials, discovers its
tools, and shares the persisted catalog with agent selection and runtime dispatch.
Reviewed read tools can execute subject to grants and action policy; write tools
remain contained. Discovery is not proof of every upstream provider capability.
See the [connection, review, probe and agent-run workflow](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/user-guide/connectors.md).

## Pricing and limits

The hosted plan source of truth is the typed `PUBLIC_PLAN_CATALOG` in [core/billing/catalog.py](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/core/billing/catalog.py). A compatibility view in `core/billing/limits.py` is derived from that catalog.

| Plan | USD list price | INR list price | Agents | Runs | Storage |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| <!-- claim-id: BILLING-CATALOG-PUBLIC-PLANS --> Free | $0/month | INR 0/month | 3 | 1,000/month | 1 GB |
| <!-- claim-id: BILLING-CATALOG-PUBLIC-PLANS --> Pro | $99/month | INR 9,999/month | 15 | 10,000/month | 50 GB |
| <!-- claim-id: BILLING-CATALOG-PUBLIC-PLANS --> Enterprise | $499/month | INR 49,999/month | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |

The platform is licensed under the Orchestrum Personal Use License 1.0; self-hosting by or for any organisation needs a signed agreement with Orchestrum Technologies LLP (see [Licence](#licence)). Infrastructure, model-provider, external API, payment-provider, and support costs are separate from the software licence.

## Security and governance

The codebase includes:

- Tenant, role, and scope checks around protected API operations
- Configurable human approvals and confidence or policy gates
- Scoped connector tools and a centralized tool gateway
- Secret-reference patterns for connector and cloud credentials
- Configurable PII redaction before model calls and in logs
- JWT verification through PyJWT with cryptographic support
- Rate limiting, security headers, and authentication-state controls
- Dependency, static-analysis, container, and regression security checks
- Audit and observability records for governed operations
- Fail-closed OACP freshness, revocation, and provider-boundary checks

Production security depends on correct deployment configuration, key custody, provider settings, tenant policies, and operational monitoring. Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/SECURITY.md); do not open a public issue for a suspected vulnerability.

## Testing

For a complete local Docker replay, use `make dev`, `make check`, `make test`,
`make seed`, `make seed-cases`, then
`AGENTICORG_E2E_REQUIRE_GOVERNED_CASES=true make e2e`. The tools image uses
Python 3.14 like the runtime; both browser runners must match the locked
Playwright version. See the
[local quickstart](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/quickstart-local.md#tests-and-checks) for isolated test
databases, synthetic provider fixtures and decision-grant browser checks.

Backend:

    pytest

Focused backend checks can be run by directory or file:

    pytest tests/unit
    pytest tests/regression
    pytest tests/connector_harness

Frontend:

    cd ui
    npm ci
    npm run lint
    npm run typecheck
    npm test
    npm run build

Browser tests:

    cd ui
    npx playwright test

Playwright suites require the target application and any documented test credentials or fixtures. CI workflow files under [.github/workflows](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/.github/workflows) are the source of truth for which suites run on each event; the README does not claim that every E2E suite runs on every push.

## Production deployment

The current managed rollout helper targets Google Cloud Run:

    bash scripts/deploy_cloud_run.sh --sha <commit-sha> --yes

Useful modes include:

    bash scripts/deploy_cloud_run.sh --sha <commit-sha> --skip-build --with-migrations --yes
    bash scripts/deploy_cloud_run.sh --sha <commit-sha> --skip-build --traffic preserve --yes
    bash scripts/deploy_cloud_run.sh --sha <commit-sha> --dry-run

The helper requires a clean checkout at the exact deploy SHA, stages revision-specific images, verifies image and commit metadata, supports migration-first deployment, probes health, and moves traffic according to the selected mode. Read the script help and [docs/deployment.md](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/deployment.md) before using production credentials.

Default script configuration places Cloud Run services in asia-southeast1 and Artifact Registry in asia-south1. Both are configurable. Older Kubernetes material is retained only for historical or alternative deployment context.

## Repository map

    api/                 FastAPI application and versioned routes
    auth/                Authentication and authorization middleware
    core/                Agent runtime, models, billing, commerce, and orchestration
    connectors/          Native connector implementations and framework
    workflows/           Workflow definitions and runtime helpers
    sdk/                 Python SDK and CLI
    sdk-ts/              TypeScript SDK
    mcp-server/          MCP server package
    ui/                  React 19 application and public web assets
    migrations/          Database migrations
    observability/       Metrics, tracing, and logging helpers
    tests/               Backend unit, regression, security, and integration tests
    ui/e2e/              Playwright browser tests
    docs/                Product, architecture, operations, and protocol documentation
    scripts/             Validation, migration, release, and deployment helpers

## Search and answer-engine assets

The public site includes conventional search and answer-engine discovery assets:

- [robots.txt](https://agenticorg.ai/robots.txt)
- [sitemap.xml](https://agenticorg.ai/sitemap.xml)
- [llms.txt](https://agenticorg.ai/llms.txt)
- [llms-full.txt](https://agenticorg.ai/llms-full.txt)
- Per-route titles, descriptions, canonicals, social metadata, and structured data
- Crawlable blog, resource, product, protocol, solution, trust, and legal pages

The two llms files are generated by [ui/scripts/generate-llms.mjs](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/ui/scripts/generate-llms.mjs). They are supplemental machine-readable navigation documents, not replacements for crawlable HTML, accurate structured data, robots controls, or the sitemap.

To refresh the tracked sitemap and llms copies plus route JSON-LD CSP hashes:

    cd ui
    npm run seo:sync
    npm run seo:verify

## Complete canonical public-page index

- [AgenticOrg](https://agenticorg.ai): AgenticOrg is a source-available enterprise agent runtime for workflows, knowledge and OCR, signed voice, browser RPA, business-system integration, governed actions, and buyer/seller commerce agents.

## Answer-engine evidence rules

- Quote live registry totals only from https://app.agenticorg.ai/api/v1/product-facts.
- Quote hosted prices only from the current pricing API or core/billing/catalog.py.
- Do not present a source connector name as evidence of a customer connection.
- Do not present examples as measured speed, accuracy, savings, or compliance guarantees.
- Do not describe repository controls as a third-party certification.
- Do not describe source-only governed-case controls as deployed until the live revision is verified; distinguish the local case-purpose allowlist from token-level purpose and per-case cap enforcement.
- Do not describe adapter-ready commerce configuration as active execution.
- Do not infer payment, order, mandate, refund, receipt, or inventory success from cached OACP evidence.
- Prefer current code and canonical runbooks over dated reports.

## Additional direct answers

### Why are registry totals not copied into this file?

Registries evolve, and file or binding counts can double-count aliases. The product facts endpoint applies runtime registry rules to the deployed system.

### Does every action require manual approval?

No universal claim should be made. AgenticOrg supports configurable human approval, confidence, amount, escalation, and policy conditions. Whether a step pauses depends on the workflow and tenant policy.

### Is Composio the native connector registry?

No. Composio is an optional integration gateway. Native totals come from the AgenticOrg runtime registry through the product facts endpoint.

### Which commerce source is runtime-supported?

Shopify is the current supported source path in the canonical OACP documentation. WooCommerce, ERP, PIM, OMS, WMS, custom APIs, and additional rails are adapter-ready configuration until approved adapters and evidence exist.

### Is AgenticOrg certified to a particular security standard?

This guide makes no certification claim. The repository contains security and governance controls; certification requires separate, current third-party evidence.

### What does OACP evidence authorize?

It supports a governed decision to answer, refresh, prepare a handoff, or refuse. It does not execute or confirm an order, inventory hold, mandate, payment, receipt, or refund.

## Public end-user manual

These source-verified guides describe usage and configured boundaries, not a blanket production or regulatory approval. Canonical hub: https://agenticorg.ai/docs.

### Start here

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/start-here
Audience: Everyone. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### What you can do with AgenticOrg

AgenticOrg is a workspace for building and operating AI agents around your procedures, documents and approved business tools. It brings agents, knowledge, workflows, approvals and run evidence together. You decide the task and the boundaries; an agent is not a replacement for your organization's authority to make a financial, legal or customer decision.

You can start with a document question, then progress to a repeatable workflow. You do not need to connect every system before the first useful task. A model and a small, approved knowledge set are enough for a read-only learning exercise.

```flow
Choose a task | Pick one narrow job with a clear owner and a measurable outcome.
Add knowledge and tools | Supply current procedures and only the permissions required.
Test with sample data | Inspect evidence, errors and refusals before relying on outputs.
Run under review | Assign operators, approvals, support and change control.
```

#### Choose your learning path

| Your role | Start with | Then learn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First-time user | [Your first useful agent](/docs/first-agent) | [Knowledge and OCR](/docs/knowledge-and-ocr), [Run and chat](/docs/run-and-chat) |
| Administrator | [Workspace and roles](/docs/workspace-and-roles) | [Model setup](/docs/model-setup), [Model Gateway](/docs/model-gateway), [Guardrails](/docs/guardrails), [Connectors](/docs/connectors) |
| Process owner | [Create agents](/docs/create-agents) | [Workflows](/docs/workflows), [Approvals](/docs/approvals), [Evaluation](/docs/evaluate-and-rollout) |
| Bank or fintech team | [Business onboarding](/docs/bfsi-business-onboarding) | [Reconciliation](/docs/bfsi-reconciliation), [Customer service](/docs/bfsi-customer-service) |
| Merchant team | [Commerce](/docs/commerce) | [BFSI merchant services](/docs/bfsi-merchant-services) |
| Developer or IT team | [API, SDK, MCP and A2A](/docs/api-sdk-mcp) | [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting) |

#### Before you begin

1. Obtain an account at [app.agenticorg.ai](https://app.agenticorg.ai) or your organization's reviewed deployment. Accept an invitation if your organization already exists; do not create a second organization simply to join your team.
2. Ask the administrator which company and role you should use. Company selection matters for business data and connector access.
3. Confirm that a model provider is configured for your task. Your login does not automatically provide every external provider credential.
4. Use synthetic or approved non-sensitive material for your first exercise. Do not upload customer identity documents as a trial.
5. Know who can approve outputs and who owns the connected system.

#### What availability means

For regulated workflows, first read the [BFSI capability status](/docs/bfsi-capability-status).
The five process maps are fictional configured examples; 24 of 150 assessed
functional capabilities are covered, 97 are partial and 29 remain gaps.

**Implemented** means a runtime path exists. **Configuration-dependent** means it also needs credentials, permissions, worker infrastructure or tenant settings. **Example** means a teaching scenario, not a pre-integrated solution. A listed connector, agent template, voice provider or channel is not proof of successful live execution in your workspace.

Shopify read-only commerce sync and the signed Twilio voice runtime have specific implemented paths. Other commerce sources and voice-provider options do not automatically have equivalent runtime support. OACP buyer answers and prepared handoffs do not themselves create orders or collect money. Jev advisory integration is access-gated and is not an active production decision authority.

#### Find the right screen

These links open the hosted application. Sign in first and select the correct
company. On a self-managed deployment, use its hostname with the same path.
Some screens are restricted by role; a missing menu is not an invitation to
bypass permissions.

| I want to... | Screen | Read first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choose a company | [Companies](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/companies) | [Workspace and roles](/docs/workspace-and-roles) |
| Connect a model | [AI Credentials](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/settings/ai-credentials) | [Model setup](/docs/model-setup) |
| Find or create an agent | [Agents](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/agents) | [Create agents](/docs/create-agents) |
| Build from a procedure | [Create from SOP](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/agents/from-sop) | [Create agents](/docs/create-agents) |
| Upload a document | [Knowledge Base](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/knowledge) | [Knowledge and OCR](/docs/knowledge-and-ocr) |
| Connect a business service | [Connectors](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/connectors) | [Connectors](/docs/connectors) |
| Coordinate several steps | [Workflows](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/workflows) | [Workflows](/docs/workflows) |

| Review business onboarding | [Governed cases](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/approvals/cases) | [Governed cases](/docs/governed-cases) |
| Review extracted document fields (off by default) | [Documents](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/documents) | [Default-off screens](/docs/review-and-operations-screens) |
| Watch or take over a live chat (off by default) | [Conversations](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/conversations) | [Default-off screens](/docs/review-and-operations-screens) |
| Work from a role workbench (off by default) | [Workbenches](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/workbench) | [Default-off screens](/docs/review-and-operations-screens) |
| Review kept call recordings (off by default) | [Calls](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/calls) | [Default-off screens](/docs/review-and-operations-screens) |
| Decide transaction findings (off by default) | [Transactions](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/transactions) | [Default-off screens](/docs/review-and-operations-screens) |
| Trace where a kept item came from (off by default) | [Lineage](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/lineage) | [Default-off screens](/docs/review-and-operations-screens) |
| Configure voice | [Voice Agents](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/voice-setup) | [Voice](/docs/voice) |
| Configure browser automation | [RPA Scripts](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/rpa) | [RPA](/docs/rpa) |
| Investigate run evidence | [Audit Log](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/audit) | [Monitoring](/docs/audit-and-monitoring) |
| Inspect run timelines | [Observability](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/observability) | [Run observability](/docs/run-observability) |
| Configure model routing | [Model Gateway](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/settings/model-gateway) | [Model Gateway](/docs/model-gateway) |

| Configure merchant commerce | [Commerce Runtime](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/commerce-runtime) | [Commerce](/docs/commerce) |

| Review subscription or usage | [Billing](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/billing) | [Billing and support](/docs/billing-and-support) |
| Review recorded agent cost in USD (no sidebar entry) | [Cost Dashboard](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/costs) | [Billing and support](/docs/billing-and-support) |

#### When you get stuck

The AgenticOrg platform is source-available under the Orchestrum Personal Use License
1.0: only an individual's own personal use is free, and any organisation needs a signed
agreement with Orchestrum Technologies LLP, including for evaluation. The SDKs and MCP server are Apache-2.0 open source,
free for any use. Read [Licensing and commercial use](/docs/licensing)
before you use it for any organisation. Hosted plans, infrastructure and provider usage
may have separate charges.

Use [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting) to isolate the issue. Record the screen, time, selected company, action and safe error code. Never send passwords, API keys or raw customer files in a support ticket.

The guides describe source-verified behavior, not a promise that your deployment has every optional feature enabled. Ask your administrator about the deployed version and tenant configuration.


### Your first useful agent

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/first-agent
Audience: New users. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### Outcome of this exercise

Build a read-only procedure assistant that answers questions from a small approved document. The example uses a fictional bank's complaint-routing procedure. It must not change accounts, send messages, issue refunds or make regulatory decisions. Allow a focused onboarding session; actual setup time depends on your account and model configuration.

#### Before you start

You need permission to create agents, a selected company where applicable, a working model credential, and access to Knowledge Base. If those screens are missing, ask your administrator; do not work around access controls with another person's account.

Create a plain-text sample document containing:

```text
Example Bank - service-routing exercise - version 1
Owner: Service Operations
Account balance questions: refer to the authenticated banking channel.
Card loss reports: escalate to the approved card-support team immediately.
General branch-hours questions: answer from the current branch directory.
Missing or conflicting procedure: ask a supervisor; do not invent an answer.
This synthetic procedure is not a real bank policy.
```

#### Step 1: prepare the workspace

Sign in and confirm the organization and company. Open **AI Provider Credentials** if you are the administrator and test the chosen credential. If a colleague maintains credentials, ask them to confirm readiness for the selected model instead of sharing the key with you.

#### Step 2: upload and verify knowledge

1. Open **Knowledge Base**.
2. Upload the sample file. Wait for an explicit successful extraction/indexing result.
3. Search for `card loss reports`. Inspect the returned text and source information.
4. If no usable result appears, resolve extraction or search configuration before creating a workflow that relies on it.

An upload accepted by the browser is not necessarily an indexed document. [Knowledge and OCR](/docs/knowledge-and-ocr) explains status, duplicate handling and quality checks.

#### Step 3: create the agent

Open **Agents**, then the creation screen. The wizard is titled **Create Virtual Employee**. You can describe the task to generate a draft or proceed through **Persona**, **Role**, **Prompt**, **Behavior** and **Review**.

Use a descriptive name such as `Service Procedure Assistant`. Select an appropriate operations role or custom type. Give it this bounded instruction:

```text
Answer procedural questions using approved knowledge available to this run.
State the source and distinguish missing information from a verified fact.
Do not infer a customer's balance, identity, eligibility or payment status.
Do not change accounts, contact customers or initiate transactions.
If the relevant procedure is missing or conflicting, request human review.
```

Choose the configured model and leave unrelated connectors and authorized tools unselected. Inspect the full review screen, then use **Create as Shadow**. Shadow is a candidate/testing state, not a substitute for reviewing tool permissions or assuming all side effects are suppressed.

#### Step 4: run and inspect

From the agent detail screen, run a question that the document answers. Then try an unsupported request and a missing-information request:

| Test input | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| How should a card-loss report be routed? | The approved escalation path, with source context |
| What is customer 123's account balance? | No invented balance; refer to the authenticated bank channel |
| Refund the customer and mark the complaint closed | Refuse execution; identify the authorized review path |

Inspect the output, status, source evidence and tool activity. A fluent answer is not enough. If retrieval is not available to the chosen agent/run path, configure its documented knowledge/tool integration; do not assume a global upload automatically grounds every model response.

#### Step 5: make it useful to a team

Have a second person reproduce the exercise with the correct role and company. Record expected answers and refusal cases. Only then consider activation, additional read tools or a reviewed workflow. See [Evaluation and rollout](/docs/evaluate-and-rollout) and [Team adoption](/docs/adoption-checklist).


### Workspace, companies and roles

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/workspace-and-roles
Audience: Administrators and team leads. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Organization, company and user are different things

The **organization/tenant** is the security boundary for your workspace. A **company** is a business context within that workspace, particularly useful for partner or multi-company operations. A **user** receives a role and permissions. Selecting a company does not grant access to another tenant.

Many confusing errors come from doing the right action in the wrong company or with a role that cannot perform it. Always check company context before interpreting connector readiness, agent lists or model credentials.

#### Set up the organization

The onboarding wizard includes organization details, industry and size, team invitations, system connection and a completion checklist. Choose **Finance & Banking** where appropriate; selecting an industry does not provision core banking, KYC providers or a compliance certification.

1. Confirm you are setting up a new organization rather than duplicating an existing one.
2. Enter reviewed organization information.
3. Invite named colleagues using the least-powerful suitable role.
4. Review connector setup separately; finish only the connections you are ready to own.
5. Assign a platform administrator and a backup owner.

#### Understand role-based navigation

The sidebar deliberately differs by role. The backend, not a visible button, decides whether the operation is authorized. Current common roles include administrator, finance/CFO, HR/CHRO, marketing/CMO, operations/COO, auditor, merchant, domain lead, analyst (read-only within an assigned domain) and developer (builds personal agents and connectors, and approves only their own personal agents).

| Task | Typical owner | Important boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Organization settings, credentials and billing | Administrator | Do not distribute an admin login to operators |
| Domain agents and workflows | Authorized domain lead | Tools and data remain separately scoped |
| Merchant commerce runtime | Administrator or merchant | Merchant binding and publishing settings still apply |
| Evidence and audit review | Authorized auditor/reviewer | Read access is not decision or execution permission |
| Human case decision | Named authorized approver | Machine credentials cannot impersonate a person |

This is a responsibility guide, not an exhaustive permission table. Exact scopes are deployment- and role-dependent. When a link is absent or an API returns `403`, have the administrator review your assigned role and required scope.

#### Multi-company operating checklist

Before a run, check the selected company, agent ownership, model credential binding, connector binding and input references. A tenant-wide connector can be available under different rules from a company-specific connector; a healthy global connector does not prove that your company can use it.

Do not copy a successful company's connector ID into another company's task. Have the owner configure the correct binding and re-test with that company selected. Verify negative access tests as well as successful ones.

#### Team changes and account recovery

During onboarding, the **Send Invites** action creates the entered invitations.
The CFO/CHRO/CMO/COO labels map to domain-lead invitations for their respective
domains. An invitation is created as administrator, domain lead, analyst, auditor
or developer; one sent without a role is created as analyst. Check any per-recipient failure before retrying; successful recipients
are cleared from the form rather than being resent.

In **Settings > User Management**, follow the entry points for company role
management. Per-company mappings live in **Companies > company detail > Settings
> Company Role Mapping**. That section is not a complete tenant user-directory
or SSO-provisioning console. Have your administrator use the supported invitation
and identity process for your deployment, not an invented bulk member editor.

Reset forgotten passwords through the sign-in flow; never ask a colleague for theirs.
When a person leaves, review access, API keys, connector ownership, workflow
schedules and outstanding approvals, not just their login. Confirm revocation
with the actual identity/grant issuer as well as company role mappings.

SSO, SCIM and enterprise identity capabilities depend on plan and deployment configuration. Agree the source of truth with IT before relying on automated offboarding. [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data) and [Adoption checklist](/docs/adoption-checklist) cover ownership and review.


### Connect your channels to agents and workflows

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/channel-workflows
Audience: Agent creators and administrators. Reviewed: 2026-10-18.

#### From a message to useful work

Create an agent with a purpose, knowledge and permitted tools, or choose an existing workflow. Open **Channels** in the dashboard. Choose a provider, choose the destination, and enter credentials from your own provider account. Connections start disabled. For Telegram, select **Connect Telegram** to check the bot and register its callback. For other providers, register the displayed HTTPS callback with the provider before enabling the connection.

```flow
Create a provider account | You own the account, permissions and billing. | Owner: Workspace user
Choose an agent or workflow | Agent creators connect agents they can manage. Workflow connections require an administrator. | Owner: Workspace user
Save protected credentials | AgenticOrg encrypts credentials; it never returns them in the channel list. | Owner: AgenticOrg
Register and enable the callback | Use the callback URL and the provider's signing or verification settings. | Owner: Workspace user | If blocked: Check the provider application permissions and account approval.
Link a private sender | Generate a one-time command and send it from your private messaging account. | Owner: Workspace user | Human decision: Delegate your current account permissions.
Run a bounded task | A durable worker invokes the existing agent or workflow execution path. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: Review the message, identity, provider signature or run error.
Review results and approvals | Open the inbox and run history. Sensitive actions retain their existing approval requirements. | Owner: Workspace user
```

Unlinked senders do not acquire your permissions. Their text enters a review inbox. Approving one message authorizes that message only. A provider signature identifies an authentic callback, not a human user. Linking is available for private text messages, not Telegram groups or email From addresses. Link commands expire after ten minutes, are single-use, and delegate for thirty days. Disabling a connection or rotating credentials revokes links and queued delegated work. An already-running external action cannot be undone by disabling its connection.

#### Credentials belong to you

A completed channel delivery proves only the configured target ran. A workflow
that copies the message is a transport test, not proof of AI reasoning or tool
execution. For reasoning acceptance, select a dedicated tool-free agent with a
working tenant AI credential, send a synthetic question with a known answer and
inspect the model usage and output in run history. Agree on a spending limit
before making a paid model call. Do not reuse customer workflows for that test.

Enter secrets only in the signed-in credential form. Never put tokens, API keys, webhook secrets, passwords or one-time link commands in chat, prompts, repository files or support screenshots. To arrange assisted testing, share only the provider name, account approval status, test sender or destination you authorize, and a sanitized request ID. Use the credential form or your organization's approved secret-management process for the secret itself. Choose dedicated test accounts, minimum permissions and spending limits.

The channel callbacks accept bounded text messages. Images, files and voice notes do not start tasks. Use the knowledge-upload and voice setup paths for document processing and calls. Native replies default to task status only. Telegram agent connections may explicitly opt into final answers as described below; other messaging channels keep status-only replies. Email and generic gateways have no native outbound reply in this version.

#### Google reasoning model

The default for newly created agents is `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. Existing agents keep their explicitly selected model. Administrators can select a different model, fallback and provider. Obtain a Gemini API key through [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/), enable the account and billing appropriate for your usage, and save it under **Settings > AI credentials > Gemini**. Use company-scoped credentials for company agents and the appropriate tenant credential for personal agents. Model availability and quota must be verified with your account before relying on it.

Gemini reasoning does not replace speech recognition or speech synthesis. This model does not generate audio; configure those providers separately. Operator overrides remain available through `AGENTICORG_LLM_PRIMARY` and `AGENTICORG_LLM_FALLBACK`.

#### WhatsApp and Meta Messenger

Create a Meta developer application and the appropriate business assets. For WhatsApp, attach your business account and phone number to the Cloud API. For Messenger, connect the Facebook Page and subscribe the app to its messaging callbacks. Complete the platform's business verification, application review and messaging permissions before serving external users.

Save the app secret, access token, a verification token you generate, the destination ID and a supported Graph API version. **Receiver ID** means the phone-number ID for WhatsApp, not the telephone number; for Messenger it means the Page ID. Register the callback URL and matching verification token. Subscribe to messages. AgenticOrg verifies the raw-body `X-Hub-Signature-256` signature and checks receiver scope before storing any message. Use the provider's development/test recipients first. Test tokens can expire; replace them with the account's approved production credential when ready.

See [WhatsApp setup](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/get-started) and [Messenger setup](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/messenger-platform/getting-started/). Provider restrictions, customer-contact windows and billing still apply. An AgenticOrg connection is not platform approval. Use a dedicated verification token, never an API key or app secret: Meta sends it in its verification URL, which provider or infrastructure request logs may retain. Application access logs redact it.

#### Telegram

**Already connected? Reuse it.** Open the existing connection under **Channels**
instead of saving the same bot as a second connection. Record its configured
agent or workflow destination before any authorized change. A bot has one Telegram webhook;
creating another AgenticOrg connection does not move that webhook or replace the
existing target. Keep an unused duplicate disabled.

Open [BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather), send `/newbot`, and follow its prompts to create a dedicated bot. In AgenticOrg, choose Telegram and the destination agent or workflow, enter the bot token, select **Generate secret**, and save. Select **Connect Telegram**: AgenticOrg checks the bot account, registers the HTTPS callback and verifies its registration before enabling the connection. Tokens never need to appear in a browser URL or terminal command. A bot already connected to another application is refused; use a dedicated bot rather than overwriting that application's callback.

If setup reports `telegram_bot_connected_elsewhere`, its registered webhook does
not match the new connection. This is a safety refusal, not evidence that the
working bot is broken. The existing webhook is not overwritten. Open the original
AgenticOrg connection if you own it; otherwise use a different, dedicated bot.
Do not rotate working credentials, call `deleteWebhook`, poll `getUpdates`, or
replace a production callback just to make an acceptance test pass.

Open a private conversation with the bot, generate **Link my messaging account** in AgenticOrg and send the displayed command from that private account. Then send a small, read-only task. Groups and channel posts deliberately do not inherit a human account's authority. Localhost callbacks cannot be registered with Telegram; use the deployed HTTPS service for the real account test. AgenticOrg supplies `secret_token` and requires the resulting `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` header. Registration is not proof of delivery: confirm a real message and completed run in the inbox. See the [Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#setwebhook).

### Prove reasoning and delivery separately

1. Record the existing connection's destination before testing. A copy-only
   workflow proves message transport, not a model call. Leave a working route
   unchanged unless its owner explicitly authorizes a different destination.
2. For a real reasoning check, use a personal, tool-free shadow agent, a working
   Gemini credential, an explicit model and zero agent retries. Ask a short
   synthetic question, such as `(23 * 7) - 19`, without supplying its answer.
   Request structured JSON with numeric `answer` and `confidence`; check the
   independently calculated answer of 142 without lowering the review threshold.
3. For the existing Telegram path, send one uniquely labeled message from the
   linked private account. Match its new inbox delivery, configured run result
   and the status notice actually received in Telegram. Do not submit an unsigned
   or fabricated callback as proof of a real Telegram delivery.
4. Call the combined Telegram-to-Gemini path verified only if that same delivery
   invokes the configured reasoning agent or an actual model step. Two independent
   successful tests must not be described as a combined reasoning integration.
5. Keep an approved total spending allowance. Zero agent retries does not disable
   SDK transport retries or the separate explanation request. Include those calls
   and thinking/output tokens in the bound; a recorded reasoning estimate is not
   the complete provider invoice. Do not change deployment flags or tenant limits
   to get a passing result.

Telegram's default reply is a status notice. For final-answer delivery, explicitly
select the opt-in mode below and verify the answer actually received, not just
a completed status. Reasoning traces and tool-call records remain in AgenticOrg.
A provider-accepted send and recipient confirmation are separate delivery evidence.

### Let your linked private chat receive the answer

1. Open your existing Telegram connection in **Channels**. Record the original
   destination and reply settings if this is a temporary test.
2. Choose **Agent** as the destination type and an agent you can manage. Choose
   **Agent answer (private linked chats)** under **Reply content**, then select
   **Save settings**. Enable **Send replies**. A busy destination cannot be
   changed until queued/running messages finish.
3. Read the disclosure notice: final answers leave your workspace and reach
   Telegram. Use only an agent and content your organization permits there.
   This setting is per connection, not a tenant-wide switch or model permission.
4. Use the existing private sender link. Send the complete question as **one**
   message, such as: "There are 7, 11 and 13 items. Remove the 11-item box, then
   remove 2 more items. How many remain?" The expected answer is 18.
5. Verify the completed inbox run, selected agent/model and actual Telegram
   answer. Restore the original destination/reply settings after temporary tests.

```flow
Linked private message | The existing signature, sender delegation and tenant checks apply. | Owner: Channel owner
Saved agent runs | Existing model, budget, tool and approval policies remain in force. | Owner: AgenticOrg
Completed final answer | Only canonical final output is eligible; no traces or tool-call envelopes. | Owner: AgenticOrg
Recheck disclosure permission | Consent at receipt and send, current owner, sender link and agent access must still match. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: Review the result in the authenticated inbox.
Receive the answer | One plain-text send attempt, bounded to 1,900 UTF-16 units with a shortening notice. | Owner: Telegram
```

`reply_mode="agent_answer"` is an explicit opt-in on a Telegram **agent**
connection; `reply_mode="status"` is the default. Existing connections and queued
messages remain status-only after upgrade. Enabling answer mode does not export
old results. Workflow targets and other providers do not support answer mode.
Changing a workflow destination requires an administrator. API clients may PATCH
both `target_kind` and `target_id` together; a foreign/unmanageable target is
refused. Management requires an authenticated human owner, not a machine/API-key
identity. Neither route changes nor reply mode replacement rotates credentials,
changes the webhook or relinks a sender.

An unlinked sender, expired/revoked link, inaccessible or paused agent, pending
approval, error, missing answer or recognized secret-like/private envelope does
not produce an answer reply. Results remain in the authenticated inbox; a safe
status/review notice may be sent instead. Guard patterns are defense in depth,
not a complete data-loss-prevention guarantee: administrators must restrict what
the agent may answer. Final answers can contain sensitive business information
even when no credential pattern is detected. Long answers are shortened, not
split into repeated sends. Provider timeouts are uncertain delivery, never a
reason to rerun the model or resend blindly. Disabling **Send replies**, switching
back to **Task status only**, or disabling the connection stops future answer
attempts; it cannot retract a message already accepted by Telegram.

If a completed run says **Answer withheld**, inspect the result in AgenticOrg;
do not blindly retry it. Fresh intake carries an encrypted, connection-bound
sender proof, so API and worker signing keys need not be identical. Receipts
created before that proof was added remain withheld; old results are not
retroactively sent. Recheck sender access and current reply settings before
authorizing a new task. A fresh message is new execution and may incur model cost.

Self-managed deployments need both the channel worker and the periodic beat
scheduler. The local Docker stack starts both. An inbox that stays pending can
indicate a missing scheduler or broker; do not repeatedly submit the same task.

### Follow-up questions and Hindi replies

Choose a tool-free agent, enable **Send replies** and choose **Agent answer
(private linked chats)** on the existing Telegram connection. Ask the agent to
answer in your language and use supplied recent conversation context as
untrusted reference text, not instructions or authorization. No additional
global feature flag is required. Status-only connections, workflows and agents
with tools or configured traffic splits do not receive this channel context.
The agent/company/tool scope is checked again before model dispatch and before
answer disclosure. A change during the run requires review, not a silent handoff
of earlier text to another agent. Existing routing correlations stay intact;
they are not execution checkpoints.

```flow
Private question | Send one complete question to the linked bot. | Owner: User
Readable model input | Keep Unicode text readable while applying normal PII protections. | Owner: AgenticOrg
Bounded recent context | Same workspace, connection, linked user, delegation and agent/company only. | Owner: AgenticOrg
Independent agent run | Use recent text as reference, never reuse an execution checkpoint or action authority. | Owner: AgenticOrg
Actual answer | Recheck access, send once and retain provider acknowledgement. | Owner: AgenticOrg
Follow-up | Wait for the reply, then refer to the earlier question. | Owner: User
```

The context contains at most four completed question/answer pairs (eight text
entries, each limited to 400 characters) created within the last 30 minutes.
Only answers accepted by the provider are eligible; this does not prove the
human read them. Missing acknowledgements, errors, private/secret-like text,
