Items ingested while lineage was off have no recorded chain, so "No provenance kept yet" can mean the item predates the switch.

Next: [Approvals](/docs/approvals), [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data), [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting), [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting).


### Audit, monitoring and run history

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/audit-and-monitoring
Audience: Operators and auditors. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### What evidence you should inspect

Run evidence helps answer who requested a task, which company/agent handled it, which tools were attempted, what failed, what required review and what outcome was reported. Use **Audit Log**, **Observability**, agent history and workflow run detail according to your role. The separate administrator [run timeline and workload view](/docs/run-observability) is opt-in and has a bounded time window; it is not an exhaustive audit stream.

![Illustrative audit workspace](/screenshots/audit.webp)

This screenshot illustrates an existing product view. It is not evidence of your tenant's current activity or a measured delivery guarantee.

#### Investigate a task end to end

1. Find the run/case reference and timestamp.
2. Confirm the tenant/company context and initiating identity.
3. Inspect the agent and prompt/model version where recorded.
4. Read tool outcomes and safe failure/refusal reasons.
5. Verify citations, provider timestamps and missing evidence.
6. Inspect approval or case-decision authority separately.
7. Check the system-of-record outcome for any external action.

Do not infer that an absent event means no action occurred. Confirm the view's scope and whether the event writer for that path is implemented.

#### Understand screen limits

Dashboard Recent Activity and Observatory read audit history. Observatory polls the newest 20 rows every five seconds and labels that scope. This is not an exhaustive live stream or a full-day activity total. An internal resilient feed exists in the repository. Its only writer is the conversation supervisor console (off by default behind `AGENTICORG_CONVERSATION_V2_ENABLED`), which announces conversation changes, never message text, for the Conversations screen; no other operational event is published to it, so do not represent it as universal real-time monitoring.

In a tenant that keeps spend rate cards, commitments, invoices, reconciliations or spend jobs, the Audit Log hides those audit rows from every reader who is not a human administrator or auditor, including domain roles and machine credentials, even after spend intelligence is turned off. This is `AGENTICORG_SPEND_AUDIT_COMMERCIAL_FILTER`, on by default; `false` shows them to every reader as before. Where the deployment turns on the tamper-evident audit chain (`AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED`, off by default), audit rows are linked into a hash chain, and a reader with audit access can read the chain status and verify the links through `GET /api/v1/audit/chain` and `GET /api/v1/audit/chain/verify`.

For governed cases, inspect transitions, memo citations, policy inputs/version, analyst reviews, decision-grant evidence and signed handoff delivery history. The case record can retain stronger lineage than a general activity summary.

#### Establish operational measures

Choose metrics tied to your task: successful and refused runs, correct answers, missing-source rate, approval age, connector error/latency, OCR review rate, workflow retries and actual downstream outcomes. Record the time window, sample size and workload. Do not turn a sample result into a platform-wide accuracy claim.

#### Incident workflow

Stop the affected external-action schedule or agent path through supported controls. Preserve safe references, isolate the provider/configuration issue, and ask the accountable operator to investigate. Never paste secrets or full customer records into ordinary issue reports.

Check [Service Status](https://agenticorg.ai/status) and your own deployment health separately. A public service status page cannot certify the health of every tenant connector or self-hosted bank environment.

Next: [Run observability](/docs/run-observability), [Guardrails](/docs/guardrails), [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting), [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data), [Evaluation](/docs/evaluate-and-rollout).


### Guardrail rules, dry runs and enforcement

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/guardrails
Audience: Tenant administrators and security owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Configure and test guardrails

Tenant-scoped rules evaluate text at the input, retrieved-evidence, model-output and tool-action stages. A rule names a detector, threshold, optional agent/use-case/risk-tier scope, priority and response. Detector identifiers are `sensitive_data`, `toxicity`, `pattern`, `injection`, `output_policy` and `grounding`. Action values are `flag`, `mask`, `redact`, `tokenise` and `block`; API validation enforces detector/action compatibility.

Tenant administrators manage rules on the [Guardrails](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/settings/guardrails) page. It shows the mode in effect (hooks off, flag-only or enforcing), lists the rules with what each applies to, adds, changes, enables, disables and deletes a rule, and dry-runs a stage over a text. Detector options are edited as JSON, starting from an example for the chosen detector. The page changes rules only; hooks and tenant enforcement are switched on through their own approved controls.

The same operations are available under `/api/v1/guardrails` to an approved client acting as a tenant administrator and holding `governance.guardrails.sensitive.read` or `.write`: `GET /status`, `GET/POST /rules`, `PATCH/DELETE /rules/{rule_id}`, `POST /evaluate`, `GET /adversarial` and `POST /adversarial/run`. Do not copy a privileged key into a browser console or commit it to a script.

```flow
Check effective status | Open the Guardrails page and read the banner: hooks off, flag-only or enforcing.
Create a narrow rule | Choose one stage, detector, threshold, response and explicit scope.
Dry-run examples | Use the dry run with synthetic allowed and flagged text; inspect the outcomes and the text after the rules.
Review detector limits | Check false positives, missed cases, latency and failure behavior with the domain owner.
Enable only through approved controls | Confirm hooks and tenant enforcement configuration before relying on blocking or transforms.
Monitor and revise | Correlate rule outcomes with run evidence; keep a rollback owner and test after edits.
```

#### Understand the modes

Rules can be stored while platform hooks or enforcement are off. Hooks are disabled by default. With hooks enabled but tenant enforcement off, evaluations are flag-only: the request continues unchanged while findings are recorded for observation. The `/evaluate` endpoint is a dry run: it returns the result the rules would produce, including transformed text or `allowed: false`, but does not enforce that result on a live call and does not write an audit outcome. A dry run is therefore not evidence that production traffic is protected.

Enforcement is a separate setting. When active, a matching transform changes the text before it continues, and a blocking rule refuses that stage. A strict runtime may refuse a stage if it cannot safely load rules or a detector fails; behavior depends on the deployed strictness configuration. Confirm the effective status, hook configuration and runtime logs with your platform owner rather than inferring enforcement from the existence of a rule.

#### Scope and detector behavior

Rules match one of four stages: `input`, `retrieval`, `output` or `action`. Optional `agent_id`, `use_case` and `risk_tier` fields narrow a rule. Without those fields, the rule can apply to every call at that stage. Rules run in priority order, and a block takes precedence over a transform. Pattern rules are bounded and reject known unsafe regular-expression shapes; keep patterns short, specific and reviewed.

Sensitive-data recognition includes configured patterns for common identifiers such as payment cards, Aadhaar, PAN, GSTIN, email, UPI and phone. Recognition quality depends on the active analyzer and fallback recognizers. Toxicity and prompt-injection detection are signals, not proof of intent or a complete security boundary. A `grounding` rule (output stage; flag or block) compares each sentence of an answer with what the run retrieved and reports claims, and figures, that the retrieved text does not carry. It is a word-level check, not a judgement of meaning: it catches answers written without the retrieved material, and it can flag a faithful paraphrase. In the dry run, paste the retrieved text as the context. Test representative languages, formats, OCR noise and adversarial inputs. Retain a human review path for high-impact decisions.

#### Operational checklist

- Start in flag-only mode with synthetic cases and inspect false positives and misses.
- Run the adversarial set on the Guardrails page against your rules. It reports, per category, the synthetic attacks your rules detect, the ones they miss and the benign texts they wrongly catch. Some attacks are included because pattern-based detectors miss them, so a score below 100% is expected; the result describes that corpus only.
- Verify exact tenant, agent, use-case and risk-tier matching, including missing-context behavior.
- Test each action separately; ensure masks/redactions do not destroy required business context.
- Verify that blocked input, retrieval, output and tool-action cases stop at the intended boundary.
- Confirm audit permissions, correlation IDs, retention and incident ownership.
- Keep a rollback rule/configuration and rerun regression cases after every detector or policy change.

Guardrails do not replace access control, data minimization, provider contracts, connector permissions, human approvals or institution policy. They are one control in a layered system.

Next: [Model Gateway](/docs/model-gateway), [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data), [Audit and monitoring](/docs/audit-and-monitoring), [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting).


### Run timelines and workload observability

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/run-observability
Audience: Administrators and operators. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Inspect run timelines and workload

The administrator-only **Observability** screen (`/dashboard/observability`) has Traces, which lists recent instrumented runs and a span waterfall for one run, and Workload, which summarizes review deadlines and selected tenant outcomes. Traces and Workload are read-only views. Where the deployment turns on synthetic checks (`AGENTICORG_SYNTHETIC_CHECKS_ENABLED`, off by default), a third **Checks** tab lists the tenant's scheduled probes with their latest results and lets an administrator add or run one. Where the debugging console is on (`AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_DEBUG_CONSOLE_ENABLED`, off by default), a run recorded while it was on offers **Step through** to read its checkpoints one step at a time. They help an operator investigate; they do not replace the audit log, provider billing, a system-of-record check or an incident process.

```flow
Open Observability | Sign in as an authorized administrator and select the intended company.
Check recording state | Read the tracing/timeline status before interpreting an empty run list.
Find a run | Filter recent runs by agent, then open one run to inspect parent/child spans and events.
Compare workload | Review pending/overdue reviews and the one-hour run, model-call and guardrail summaries.
Follow the correlation | Use run/correlation identifiers to inspect audit details and the downstream system separately.
```

#### Traces and timelines

The list requests up to 50 recent stored runs and can filter by agent ID. A run detail displays its stored spans in relative time order, including duration, parent relationship, status and available attributes/events such as model decisions, tool outcomes, guardrail outcomes and exceptions. Data is limited to what that deployment records; missing spans do not prove that no work occurred.

Before a platform owner changes `AGENTICORG_TRACING_ENABLED` or `AGENTICORG_TRACING_TIMELINE_ENABLED`, agree on an approved OTLP endpoint and protocol, sampling, data classification, storage and retention. Both controls default to off; strict production-like environments require a valid exporter endpoint when tracing is enabled. Confirm the effective retention setting with the platform owner before relying on historical timelines. Never send sensitive payloads to an unapproved telemetry collector.

#### Workload view

Workload refreshes about every 15 seconds. Its run, model-call and guardrail summaries cover the most recent hour. Review counts and deadlines come from the tenant's pending human-review queue. Each panel can report unavailable data independently; a dash or an error means unknown/unavailable, not zero. Model-call summaries depend on model-gateway record capture, and guardrail block/transform counts depend on persisted guardrail audit outcomes.

Use the panel's stated time window and generated time when comparing it with another report. This is not a durable event stream, full audit export, cross-tenant dashboard or service-level guarantee. Do not use it as the sole evidence for a financial, compliance or customer-impact decision.

#### A practical investigation

1. Capture the run ID, correlation ID, company, agent and approximate time.
2. Check whether tracing and timeline storage were enabled during that interval.
3. Follow span status, duration and error events; identify the earliest failing dependency.
4. Compare guardrail and model-gateway decisions with the audit view.
5. Confirm any external action with its authoritative system (for example, the provider or connected business application).
6. Record the safe error code, deployed commit and remediation owner; do not attach credentials or full customer payloads.

If the view is empty, first verify permissions, selected company, feature configuration, retention window and whether the run path emits timeline spans. See [Audit and monitoring](/docs/audit-and-monitoring), [Model Gateway](/docs/model-gateway), [Guardrails](/docs/guardrails) and [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data).


### Evaluate and roll out safely

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/evaluate-and-rollout
Audience: Product owners and administrators. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Define success before running tests

Choose the task, owner, expected output, permitted tools, prohibited actions and escalation behavior. Use representative examples, not only a single easy prompt. A confidence percentage, template name or passed unit test does not establish business accuracy.

#### Build a small reviewed test set

Include normal inputs, incomplete files, conflicting procedures, stale evidence, incorrect company references, provider failures and attempts to request forbidden actions. For OCR, include realistic scans; for voice, include accent/noise and silence; for RPA, include expired sessions and changed selectors.

| Dimension | Example acceptance question |
| --- | --- |
| Grounding | Is each material fact supported by an authorized source? |
| Correctness | Does the result match the reviewed answer? |
| Permissions | Are cross-company and ungranted requests refused? |
| Human control | Does consequential work stop at the intended review boundary? |
| Recovery | Are retries bounded and duplicate effects prevented? |
| Usability | Can a second operator reproduce the task without the builder? |
| Operations | Are latency, cost, volume and failure handling acceptable for this workload? |

#### Run candidates in a bounded environment

Create candidates in shadow and restrict tools to reads where possible. Shadow is an evaluation state, not proof of universal side-effect suppression. Inspect actual tool activity. Compare versions with the same test inputs and source content. Record provider/model, prompt and configuration so results are reproducible.

The public **Evaluations** page describes methodology; use the task's actual evaluation/run evidence for promotion. Jev advisory shadow work has its own access and cost/latency gate and does not replace human authority.

#### Prompt templates, datasets and the agent catalogue

Administrators manage prompt templates on **Prompt Templates**. Three panels on that screen appear only where the deployment turns them on, and each is off by default:

| Panel | Setting | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changes waiting for approval | `AGENTICORG_PROMPTS_MAKER_CHECKER`, or the tenant flag `prompts.maker_checker` | A template create, change, rollback or delete waits for a second person's approval |
| Evaluation datasets | `AGENTICORG_EVALS_V2_ENABLED` | Versioned tenant datasets that can be run and compared run by run |
| Compare models | `AGENTICORG_PROMPT_COMPARE_ENABLED` | One prompt run against several models side by side; these are real, billed model calls |

With `AGENTICORG_EVAL_PROMOTION_GATE_ENABLED` on (off by default), an agent that declares an evaluation gate is not promoted or resumed to active until its prompt has a stored run on the gate's dataset version that meets the gate's pass rate without regressing beyond its allowance. The **Agent Catalogue** screen lists each agent's registry card and lifecycle state when the agent registry is on (`AGENTICORG_AGENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED`, off by default); otherwise it says the registry is off in this deployment.

#### Move to a limited pilot

Agree users, volume, allowed data, hours, review coverage and rollback triggers. Choose a narrow population and a named support owner. Train operators and reviewers separately. Verify that a non-admin user can complete the documented flow with their own account.

Do not enable a provider/payment/channel action simply because read-only Q&A works. Each external action needs its own account, contract, authority, failure tests and operational evidence.

#### Expand deliberately

Measure actual results and reopened errors. Correct the shared cause when a bug affects multiple paths, then add regression cases that replay the failing user steps. Re-evaluate after changes to model, prompt, policy, document, connector or target site.

For a bank, the institution's risk, security, privacy and business owners approve rollout under their own process. AgenticOrg does not make a regulatory approval, certification or guaranteed service-level claim on the basis of this checklist.

Next: [Team adoption checklist](/docs/adoption-checklist), [BFSI onboarding](/docs/bfsi-business-onboarding).


### Security, privacy and data handling

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/security-and-data
Audience: Security teams and data owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Start with approved data

Use synthetic records when learning. Before real data, identify the data owner, classification, purpose, allowed model/providers, retention and access. Minimize what each task receives. A document being useful to a model is not permission to upload it.

For BFSI, customer identity, financial, health and account information can require institution-specific controls. This guide explains product boundaries; it is not legal advice or proof of regulatory compliance.

#### Protect access and credentials

Use named accounts and least-powerful roles. Keep company context explicit. Store provider credentials through the approved protected form, secret manager or connector path; never in prompts, scripts, example files or screenshots.

Review API keys and delegated grants by scope, environment and owner. Rotate and revoke through the appropriate control. A machine credential is not a human session and cannot perform human-only case decisions.

#### Understand where information goes

| Path | Review requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Model and embedding calls | Provider endpoint, permitted data, retention and contractual terms |
| Knowledge extraction | File access, extracted chunks, OCR quality, replacement and deletion |
| Voice | Provider recording/retention, approved number and encrypted bounded text |
| Calls (speech intelligence, off by default) | Encrypted audio and transcript kept per tenant, the transcription engine and speech-provider credential used, spoken-data redaction, and how recordings are removed: the speech routes offer no deletion or retention setting |
| RPA | Approved domains, secret custody and screenshot/log content |
| Governed cases | Cited evidence, encrypted excerpts, decision authority and signed handoff |
| Commerce | Merchant scope, artifact freshness, public-safe projection and provider-owned execution |

AgenticOrg's controls do not automatically set the provider's retention or your bank's network configuration. Review those separately.

**Settings > Compliance & Data > Data Region** records the tenant's region (IN, EU or US). It does not move stored data or change where the hosted service runs. Residency enforcement is off by default. When a platform operator turns it on for the deployment (`AGENTICORG_RESIDENCY_ENFORCE=true`) or for one tenant (authority flag `residency.enforce`), any AI or integration provider without an active attestation for that region is refused; providers running inside the deployment need none. Administrators record attestations through `/api/v1/residency/attestations`. Confirm the deployment's actual regions with your platform owner.

#### Retention and deletion

Decide who can delete source documents, derived knowledge, retained excerpts and operational evidence. These are not identical resources. Governed-case excerpt deletion can remove retained passages while keeping references/digests and the memo. It does not silently erase every downstream copy or the institution's system-of-record obligation.

Ask the operator to verify backup/restore and erasure procedures in the actual environment. A backup configuration file is not proof that restoration works.

#### Respond to an incident

Stop affected schedules/actions, revoke compromised credentials, preserve safe references and notify the designated incident owner. Report security issues privately through [Support](https://agenticorg.ai/support) or the repository's security process. Do not open a public issue containing customer documents, tokens or exploitable tenant identifiers.

A useful incident record states time, version, resource/run reference, affected path, observed symptom and mitigation. Keep customer material in the institution's approved evidence system.

Next: [Workspace and roles](/docs/workspace-and-roles), [Audit and monitoring](/docs/audit-and-monitoring), [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting).


### Agent security deployment and evidence

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/cert-in-agent-security
Audience: Tenant administrators, security and deployment operators. Reviewed: 2026-10-17.

#### Agent Security Deployment And Evidence Guide

Use [CERT-In CIAD-2026-0049](https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?pageid=PUBVLNOTES02&VLCODE=CIAD-2026-0049)
and [CIAD-2026-0046](https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?pageid=PUBVLNOTES02&VLCODE=CIAD-2026-0046)
as primary references. If a detail page is unavailable, CERT-In's
[official 2026 advisory index](https://www.cert-in.org.in/s2cMainServlet?pageid=PUBADVLIST02&year=2026)
lists the titles and issue dates. Detail-page availability was intermittent when
checked on 17 October 2026. This guide does not confer certification, legal compliance,
bank approval or permission to conduct a live financial transaction.

#### Responsibility Boundaries

Tenants configure their own approved SSO/OIDC connections and group mappings;
they do not receive platform-operator privileges by controlling an IdP. Require
MFA in the tenant IdP's application policy, test non-admin and missing-factor
refusals, and record the exact issuer, audience, redirect URI and group mapping.
An endpoint-discovery test alone proves none of these. Keep machine credentials
and recovery access separately protected. This release does not switch any
tenant's MFA policy or platform IAM/IAP configuration on automatically.

AgenticOrg coordinates work, applies configured action/tenant policies and
records evidence. Grantex supplies delegated authorization primitives. The
operator owns deployment isolation, IAM, network policy, identity-provider MFA,
security-log storage and incident response. External systems still enforce
their own permissions and business rules. None of these boundaries is replaced
by a prompt or a model's confidence score.

Existing inventory records do not automatically discover every deployed agent,
API or third-party tool. Reconcile the runtime catalog with cloud assets, service
accounts, installed packages, scheduled jobs and external credentials. Record an
owner and decommission decision for dormant endpoints and identities.

#### Separate Run Authorization

The source adds an opt-in control; the compatibility default remains off:

```bash
AGENTICORG_GRANTS_ISOLATE_RUN_TOKENS=true
AGENTICORG_GRANTS_ENFORCE_CLOSED=deny
AGENTICORG_GRANTS_RUN_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS=900
```

When isolation is enabled, the run-grant resolver forces deny mode even if the
deployment supplied off or warn. It obtains a delegated grant for a server-created
run authorization context rather than sharing the same cache entry across
separate contexts. Refresh preserves the isolation key. Governed-case calls in
one authorizer share that context; another authorizer receives another key.

A legacy static token in agent configuration no longer substitutes for the run's
delegated grant. A supplied external token remains an additional restriction;
it does not become a shortcut around fresh run authority. Ambiguous supplied
and caller tokens are refused. Missing registration, scopes, root authority,
issuer availability or valid delegation prevents authorized tool dispatch.

The root credential must come from a secret manager and the configured registered
agent/scopes must be reviewed. Tokens expire; this setting does not automatically
revoke a grant the moment a run completes. It does not create a separate OS user,
container or cryptographic agent key per run. It also does not bind a JWT to one
case ID or enforce case-purpose/cap semantics that the SDK call does not receive.
Do not describe this as complete per-case authorization or complete advisory
coverage. See the [governed-case boundary](../user-guide/governed-cases.md).

#### Runtime And Network Isolation

Run evaluations with synthetic targets and credentials in disposable infrastructure.
Use a network-enforced default-deny policy and allow only reviewed destinations,
ports and protocols. Apply it to API workers, model/tool runtimes, browser or code
execution and remote-tool transports, not just the public API container.

The public-URL validator and DNS-pinned transport reject unsafe destinations on
the paths that use them. They are not a global firewall and do not prevent an
unrelated SDK, shell or connector from opening another socket. Cloud Run VPC
routing alone is not an allowlist. Use a reviewed firewall or authenticated
egress proxy, and test direct-connect bypass. Keep policy changes, cloud role
administration and workload restarts outside the agent's permissions.

Do not hand provider keys to the model or persist them in plaintext workflow
state. Use tenant-aware encrypted connector configuration or secret references.
If an agent encounters an unexpected credential, stop the run, quarantine that
credential through the operator's shared suppression/rotation process and
investigate. Do not try it against a real endpoint to establish validity. Masking
a secret in logs is not revocation or cross-run quarantine.

#### Human Authority And Containment

Sensitive actions need an approved policy and authenticated human authority at
the backend execution boundary. Separate preparation from approval and execution.
For financial work, the maker cannot approve their own action; a payment executor
must independently verify the approved record, beneficiary, amount, expiry,
replay state and cumulative ceilings. A case recommendation is not activation.

Configure independent operator override and upstream revocation. Verify their
effect on active workers, resumed work and cached grants. Do not let the same
agent change its scopes, remove its own audit trail or restore its root grant.
Human decisions, API-key access and service identities have different purposes;
an API key is not MFA. Protect privileged administration through private ingress
and an approved MFA-enforcing identity provider. Test the backend origin as well
as the public domain.

#### Monitoring, Retention And Evidence

Centralize security-relevant request and action logs. Retain the applicable
security logs for at least 180 days, or longer where another requirement applies.
Verify the actual bucket and sink, exclusions, access restrictions and legal
holds. A seven-year audit setting does not prove a separate cloud request-log
bucket has equivalent retention. Extending a bucket cannot restore expired logs.

Capture actor/run/grant references, tool, destination, port, protocol, timestamp
and result at the appropriate boundary; exclude tokens, raw credentials and
sensitive payloads. Configure per-second bursts, enumeration, bulk-read and
automated-registration alerts, and verify alert receipt. Process-local limits
are not a deployment-wide ceiling. Hash-linked evidence still needs protected
storage and independent verification; it is not proof that a privileged operator
cannot delete a database or bucket.

#### Operational Control Register

| Area | Required evidence before an enabled production rollout |
|---|---|
| Inventory | Reconciled agents, tools, APIs, workloads, accounts and owners |
| Secrets | Commit/history/build/config/cloud scan, issuer rotation records, credential suppression across future runs |
| IAM | Least-privilege roles, tenant isolation and anonymous read/write denial tests |
| Privileged access | Private ingress, MFA policy, authorized operator mapping and direct-origin bypass test |
| Runtime authority | Separate run grants, scope attenuation, online revocation and denial under issuer/cache failures |
| Network | Enforcing firewall/CNI/proxy, exact allowlist and denied socket test for every execution runtime |
| Monitoring | Live destination/action telemetry, burst/bulk-read alerts and on-call receipt |
| Retention | Bucket read-back, sink routing, exclusions, evidence integrity and custody |
| Patching | Deployed image digest, middleware/dependency scan and retest |
| Sensitive decisions | Human session, step-up and distinct approver tests; exact action binding |
| Financial execution | Approved references, beneficiaries, ceilings, sequence binding, velocity and reconciliation at the payment API |
| Response | Independent stop, evidence preservation, rotation, root-cause remediation, external retest and reporting assessment |

The operator must record verified configuration and test artifacts, not mark rows
complete because a feature exists in a repository. Unknown and disabled controls
remain open. Never call a sandbox merchant pilot a compliance-approved live release.

#### Incident And Recovery Procedure

Stop and isolate the affected run without destroying evidence. Preserve original
timestamps, relevant logs, image digests, authority identifiers and configuration;
restrict access and record custody. Revoke affected grants, rotate credentials
at every actual issuer and investigate adjacent accounts and persistence. Patch
root causes and replay the original failure plus sibling paths in isolation.
Retest externally through an authorized independent party before restoring access.
The incident commander and legal/security owners assess applicable reporting
obligations using the official CERT-In channels. Do not wait for a framework or
identity-verification provider to make that decision for the organization.

#### Safe Adoption Sequence

Start one synthetic workflow locally, set deny enforcement, register the smallest
tool set and test cross-tenant, revoked-grant, missing-approval and denied-egress
paths. Add run-token isolation after issuer registration/root permissions are
validated. Configure private MFA administration, network enforcement, retention
and alerts. Capture evidence and approve a staged rollout with rollback and
independent containment. Do not enable a sensitive or live onboarding flow while
any of its required gates are unresolved.


### Billing, limits and support

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/billing-and-support
Audience: Account owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-13.

#### Understand separate cost sources

Hosted platform plans and external provider usage are different. Models, embeddings, calls, messaging, merchant systems and payment providers can charge independently. Self-hosting adds your infrastructure and operating costs. Do not assume an economy label means the provider is free for your account.

The software licence is separate from these charges. The AgenticOrg platform is licensed under
the Orchestrum Personal Use License 1.0 (the SDKs and MCP server are Apache-2.0, free for any
use): only an individual's own personal use of the platform is free, and any organisation,
including for self-hosting, evaluation or a pilot, needs a signed agreement with Orchestrum
Technologies LLP. Existing and new users are treated the same for every version
published on or after 21 October 2026. See [Licensing and commercial use](/docs/licensing);
agreements: [sanjeev@orchestrum.in](mailto:sanjeev@orchestrum.in). Free personal
use of the software does not mean free hosting or providers.

Administrators and CFOs can open the **Cost Dashboard** at `/dashboard/costs` (it has no sidebar entry). It sums the platform's own recorded USD cost per task and agent; it is not a provider invoice.

The hosted pricing page is generated from the platform's plan catalog. Use [Pricing](https://agenticorg.ai/pricing) and **Billing** in your workspace for current plan information rather than relying on a hard-coded price in a guide.

#### Review a plan

Compare agent/run/storage allowances, required connector access, identity features, support and deployment needs. Ask the account owner to verify subscription status and currency. A plan upgrade does not configure provider keys or activate every optional feature.

Before a pilot, set a provider budget, expected workload, limits and an alert owner. Start with short tasks and read-only tools. For voice, approve destinations and calling windows; for RPA, avoid unnecessarily frequent schedules.

#### Billing-console procedure

1. Open **Billing** with the account-owner/admin role.
2. Inspect the current plan and supported subscription/usage controls.
3. Review the requested change and terms before checkout.
4. Return from the billing-provider flow and confirm the recorded status.
5. If status is unclear, check the provider reference and contact support; do not repeatedly submit payment.

Platform subscription billing is separate from OACP buyer payment and merchant mandate execution.

#### Send an actionable support request

Include the affected screen/flow, safe run/case reference, timestamp and timezone, selected company context, deployed version where available, expected versus actual behavior, and steps to reproduce. State whether the issue is hosted or self-managed and whether it blocks an external action.

Do not include passwords, raw API keys, full account numbers, identity documents or unredacted provider payloads. If evidence is sensitive, arrange the approved private support channel first.

Product contact: [sanjeev@orchestrum.in](mailto:sanjeev@orchestrum.in) or [mishra.sanjeev@gmail.com](mailto:mishra.sanjeev@gmail.com). ### AI spend intelligence and invoice reconciliation

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/ai-spend-intelligence
Audience: Administrators, finance teams and auditors. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### What it answers

AI spend intelligence keeps a priced, attributed record of the AI work a deployment does and checks it against what each provider invoices. This guide is for the administrators who set it up and reconcile the figures, and the auditors who read and check them. The CFO role and the other domain roles are not readers of tenant-wide or commercial figures (see [Who can read what](/docs/ai-spend-intelligence#who-can-read-what)).

| Question | Where the answer comes from |
| --- | --- |
| Which business unit, department, team or cost centre used which model, and what did it cost in rupees? | Usage records and daily rollups |
| How much of the month's spend is not attributed to the organisation, and why? | Coverage: the attributed share, the unattributed share and its reasons |
| Does each provider's invoice agree with what was metered, priced at the rates you agreed? | Invoice import and reconciliation within the 1% match tolerance |
| Does the month meet Gate 1: attributed, priced, converted to INR and reconciled? | The Gate 1 status, read together with the month's meter gaps |

The feature is off by default, and phase 1 is API-only: there is no spend screen in the app. Every request in this guide goes to `/api/v1/spend/...` with an authenticated session, and the values in the examples are illustrative. The figures are what was metered and priced with the rate cards you entered. They are not a provider's bill, a tax figure or an accounting entry. Usage records are a separate source: the existing cost ledgers, the model-call records and the screens that read them stay as they are, and `GET /spend/coverage/ledgers` sets the two side by side with the expected differences listed.

#### Turning it on

Spend intelligence is controlled by one deployment setting. While it is off, `GET /api/v1/spend/status` answers with `enabled: false`, every other spend address answers 404 `spend_disabled` before the request body is read, nothing is metered or written, and no existing behaviour changes.

| Setting | Default | What it controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_SPEND_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED` | off | The whole feature |
| `AGENTICORG_SPEND_REPORTING_TIMEZONE` | `Asia/Kolkata` | The reporting day: FX lookup, rollups, coverage and the Gate 1 attribution month |
| `AGENTICORG_SPEND_PROVIDER_BILLING_TIMEZONES_JSON` | empty | The zone each provider closes its billing day in; it dates rate cards, commitments and the reconciliation month |
| `AGENTICORG_SPEND_SWEEPS_ENABLED` | on | The scheduled spend jobs (partition check, FX settlement, commitment recompute, storage samples, GPU allocation, job sweep); no effect while the feature is off |
| `AGENTICORG_SPEND_GPU_POOLS_JSON` | empty | Standing in-house GPU pools whose node hours are shared out to the calls that used them |
| `AGENTICORG_SPEND_AUDIT_COMMERCIAL_FILTER` | on | `GET /audit` hides the audit rows of rate cards, commitments, invoices, reconciliations and spend jobs from readers other than an administrator or auditor, whether the feature is on or off (see "Who can read what" below); off restores the previous `GET /audit` for every reader |

The tables come from four migrations, `v6z79_spend_reference`, `v6z80_spend_usage`, `v6z81_spend_gpu` and `v6z82_spend_reconciliation`. Apply them before the release that turns the switch on; strict runtimes do not create tables at start-up (see [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting)). With the feature on, a deployment refuses to start when the reporting zone or a provider billing zone cannot be loaded, or when the GPU pool setting does not parse.

**Who can write.** Every change (reference data, imports, maintenance jobs, invoice imports, reconciliations and acceptances) needs a tenant administrator signed in as a person. The server checks the administrator scope and then confirms an active administrator of the tenant in the database. API keys and agent tokens are refused, and `approvals:write` alone, which developers and domain heads hold, is not enough. Each change is audited with the acting administrator's id in the same transaction. Metering can be paused for one tenant with the feature flag `spend.metering_paused`; paused usage is not written and is counted as a `paused` meter gap.

```flow
Apply the migrations | Run v6z79 to v6z82 in the release before the one that turns the switch on.
Turn on the switch | Turn on the spend switch from the settings table above and check that the reporting and billing zones load.
Confirm the status | GET /api/v1/spend/status answers enabled true and says whether this process's writer started.
Load reference data | Build the organisation tree, map sources, then enter rate cards, FX rates and commitments.
Watch coverage | Read coverage and meter gaps; add mappings and rate cards, then re-attribute and restate the records already written.
Reconcile the first month | Import each provider's invoice, reconcile the month and read the Gate 1 status.
```

#### Setting up the reference data

Reference data is what spend is measured against. Every kind can be written one row at a time, and the organisation tree, mappings, rate cards and FX rates can also be imported from a CSV or JSON file (`POST .../import`, at most 2 MiB and 5,000 rows). Add `dry_run=true` to an import to see exactly what it would create, update or reject without writing anything. The examples below omit the `Authorization` header that every request carries.

### Organisation tree

A node has your own code (such as `CC-4120`), a name, a kind, a parent and an optional owner. Only a group may be a root. A node is never deleted: setting `active` to false deactivates it, and its children keep rolling up through it.

| Kind | May sit under |
| --- | --- |
| `group` | nothing (a root) or a group |
| `business_unit` | a group or a business unit |
| `department` | a group, a business unit or a department |
| `team` | a department or a team |
| `cost_centre` | a group, a business unit, a department or a team |

```http
POST /api/v1/spend/org-nodes
Authorization: Bearer <administrator session token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"code":"CC-4120","name":"Card disputes","kind":"cost_centre","parent_code":"DEPT-CARDS"}
```

### Source mappings

A mapping ties a spend source to a node, a product line and a use case. Sources are an `agent`, a `workflow`, an `application` (such as `chat`, `voice`, `knowledge` or `documents`) or a legacy `cost_center` or `department` label that agents carry today. A mapping is turned off with `active: false`, never deleted.

```http
PUT /api/v1/spend/mappings
Content-Type: application/json

{"source_type":"agent","source_ref":"<agent id>","org_node_code":"CC-4120","product_line":"cards","use_case":"dispute-triage"}
```

Attribution is worked out on the server from the agent's configuration, these mappings and the tree. The department, cost-centre, business-unit and use-case labels a caller sends with a run are ignored, so a caller cannot charge its usage to someone else's cost centre.

### Rate cards in rupees or the provider's currency

A rate card prices one provider, usage type, model, unit and source (`contract` or `list`) from `effective_from` until `effective_to`, in the provider's billing dates. A rate change is a new card with a later start, so history keeps the rate of its day; two active cards of one key may never overlap.

```http
POST /api/v1/spend/rate-cards
Content-Type: application/json

{"provider":"openai","usage_type":"llm_tokens","model_sku":"example-chat-model","unit":"1m_input_tokens","unit_price":"212.50","cached_unit_price":"106.25","currency":"INR","effective_from":"2026-10-01","source":"contract","reference":"MSA-2026-17"}
```

- **Which card prices a call.** A model-specific card comes before a provider default; within one level, a cached-token price comes before the plain input price; then a contract card comes before a list card; then the latest start.
- **Cached and batch prices.** An input-token card may carry a cached-input price. Any card may carry a batch discount percentage, but phase 1 records carry no batch flag, so the discount is stored but not yet applied in metering, price quotes or reconciliation.
- **Volume tiers.** A card may carry up to 20 tiers, `graduated` or `all_units`. Usage is priced at the base price; the tiers are applied per contract and billing month in reconciliation.
- **Adding a card later.** A new card prices usage metered from then on. Records already written stay unpriced, or fallback-priced, until you run `POST /spend/usage/restate` for the provider and its billing days (at most 92 per job, with a reason); `include_unpriced` is on by default, so the job re-prices those records with the cards as known now.
- **No card.** Model tokens fall back to the deployment's list prices in USD and are marked as fallback-priced. In-house models, embeddings, OCR and Whisper price at zero unless you add a card; in-house model serving is charged through GPU node hours. Anything else with no price is **unpriced**: it has no amount, never zero, and is counted.
- **Corrections.** A card that has priced usage changes only through `POST /spend/rate-cards/{card_id}/correct` with a reason. The correction queues a restatement of the records the old card priced, in the same transaction.

`GET /api/v1/spend/price?provider=openai&usage_type=llm_tokens&unit=input_token&quantity=120000&model=example-chat-model&on=2026-10-15` prices a usage the way metering will, so you can check a card before usage arrives.

### FX rates to INR

Rates are kept per currency and date as the rate to INR. A record converts on its reporting date. With no rate that day (a holiday or a rate not yet published), the latest earlier rate converts and the record is marked `fx_estimated`; with no rate at all the record is `unconverted`. A new or changed rate queues an FX settlement that converts those records again with the rate of their day.

```http
PUT /api/v1/spend/fx-rates
Content-Type: application/json

{"rate_date":"2026-10-01","currency":"USD","rate_to_inr":"84.10","source":"reference"}
```

### Commitments

A **quantity** commitment names a provider, usage type, optional model, card unit and quantity, and may carry an overage price. A **money** commitment names a provider, an optional usage type and an amount in a currency. Drawdown is counted from usage records in time order by a recompute job; a record past the capacity is flagged as overage, and the overage price is applied in reconciliation, not on the record.

```http
POST /api/v1/spend/commitments
Content-Type: application/json

{"provider":"openai","kind":"quantity","usage_type":"llm_tokens","model_sku":"example-chat-model","unit":"1m_input_tokens","committed_quantity":"500","period_start":"2026-10-01","period_end":"2027-04-01","overage_unit_price":"240.00","overage_currency":"INR"}
```

#### What gets metered

Each billable quantity in one unit becomes one usage record, with the same pricing, attribution and daily rollups whatever produced it.

| Usage | Record unit | Where it is counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model calls | input, cached input and output tokens | Every model call through the router and the agent graph, plus four direct callers; one estimated `token` record when a provider does not split its count |
| Embeddings | embedding tokens, estimated from characters | Knowledge ingestion, re-indexing, search and RPA ingestion |
| OCR pages | pages | Document processing, knowledge uploads and ingestion that extracted a file itself |
| Speech minutes | audio minutes | Each transcription by the in-house Whisper engine or Deepgram, metered when the engine returns, so a later redaction, encryption or save failure does not lose minutes already transcribed |
| Priced tool calls | calls | A successful connector tool call, only when a rate card prices that tool |
| Storage | GB-days | A daily sample of each tenant's knowledge, document, document-processing and recording storage |
| In-house GPU | GPU node hours | Each closed pool hour, shared over the calls of the pool's models by tokens |

A record holds identifiers, counts and amounts only, never a prompt, a response, a document or customer data. It is append-only: its event fields never change, and only audited maintenance jobs revise its price, FX, attribution or commitment fields.

**The meter does no database work or waiting on the call path.** The hook builds the call's usage in memory and puts it on a bounded in-process queue. If metering fails, the failure is logged and counted and the call carries on unchanged. A writer thread in each process writes the queue in batches; a batch it cannot write is handed to a retry task with the same keys, so a retry never writes a record twice. Usage that still cannot be written is counted as a meter gap (`GET /spend/gaps`), and backfill can recreate model-call records from the model gateway's records while those exist.

**How attribution is chosen.** The first rule that matches wins and is stored on the record as its `attribution_path`:

| Situation | Order of rules |
| --- | --- |
| A call made by an agent | the agent's mapping; its legacy cost centre (mapping, then a node with the same code); the application's mapping |
| A workflow step with no agent | the workflow's mapping; the application's mapping; the initiating user's department |
| Anything else | the application's mapping; the initiating user's department |

A legacy label that names no node stops there: the record is kept and counted as unattributed with the reason `unknown_label`, never moved to a broader mapping. The business unit stored with a record is the nearest business unit at or above its node.

#### Reading spend

| Read | Window | What it returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /spend/usage` | up to 31 days | Records a page at a time, filtered by usage type, provider, node, agent, unattributed or unpriced |
| `GET /spend/rollups` | up to 366 days | Sums per day or per one dimension (node, business unit, use case, provider, model, agent and more), per currency and in INR |
| `GET /spend/coverage` | up to 366 days | Per day and for the period: the attributed and unattributed shares, unpriced and unconverted records, pending FX and gaps by reason |
| `GET /spend/gaps` | up to 92 days | Usage that could not be metered, by day, usage type and reason |
| `GET /spend/coverage/ledgers` | up to 31 days | Usage beside the existing cost ledgers and model-call records, with the expected differences |

The **attributed share** is the INR amount attributed to a business unit, department, team or cost centre over the whole INR amount. Attribution to a `group` node is reported separately as `group_share` and does not count. Records with no INR amount (unpriced or unconverted) count only in the record-count share and are listed beside it, so their volume stays visible. Shares are shown to six decimals and rounded so they never look better than they are.

| Unattributed reason | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no_mapping` | No rule matched | Add a mapping for the agent, workflow or application |
| `unknown_label` | A legacy cost-centre or department label names no node | Map the label or create a node with its code |
| `inactive_node` | The matched node is deactivated | Reactivate it or move the mapping |
| `no_source` | A system call with no user | Map the application |
| `resolver_failed` | A database failure during resolution | Check the logs; the record was still written |

After adding mappings or nodes, `POST /spend/usage/reattribute` resolves the still-unattributed records again. Long operations like this one are maintenance jobs: the request answers `202` with a job id, one job of a kind runs at a time per tenant, and `GET /spend/jobs/{job_id}` reports its status and result. The other jobs rebuild rollups, backfill model calls, restate prices, settle FX and recompute commitments.

#### Reconciling invoices

**Import the invoice.** `POST /spend/invoices/import` takes one provider's invoice or billing export for one billing month, in the provider's own billing zone. An invoice is stored whole or refused whole: one bad line refuses the file with 422 `invoice_rejected`, listing every refused line and its reason, because a partial invoice would reconcile against a wrong total.

```http
POST /api/v1/spend/invoices/import?provider=openai&period=2026-10&invoice_ref=INV-2026-10-0042&currency=USD&dry_run=true
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

file: invoice-2026-10.csv
```

```csv
line_kind,usage_type,model_sku,unit,quantity,amount
usage,llm_tokens,example-chat-model,1m_input_tokens,412.5,1031.25
usage,llm_tokens,example-chat-model,1m_output_tokens,96,960
tax,,,,,358.43
```

| Line kind | In the comparison |
| --- | --- |
| `usage` (the default) | Yes |
| `credit`, `tax`, `fee` | No, reported beside it |
| `commitment` (shortfall or prepaid charges) | No, reported beside it |

A second current invoice with the same reference is refused unless `replace=true`, which supersedes the earlier one; both are kept. Several references for one provider and month, such as two accounts, are summed. A month holds at most what a reconciliation can store: an import that would take the month's current invoices past that is refused with 413 (`too_many_rows`, `period_amount_too_large` or `period_quantity_too_large`), dry runs included.

**Run the reconciliation.** `POST /spend/reconciliations` with `{"provider":"openai","period":"2026-10"}` compares the provider's month with its current invoices and answers the run with its items. Only usage billed to the tenant's own key is compared (usage whose paying account could not be inferred is included and counted); usage on the platform's key is reported separately, and in-house serving, storage and GPU hours have no provider invoice. Each item carries two figures in the invoice currency:

- **stored**: the amounts as metered;
- **re-priced**: the same usage priced again with the cards in force on each billing day as known now.

The month's volume tiers and any commitment overage are worked out for each figure from its own base: the stored figure from the cards that priced the records, the re-priced figure from the cards in force now. The run reports both adjustment totals (`stored_adjustments_amount`, `repriced_adjustments_amount`).

An item is within tolerance only when both figures are known and each is within 1% of the invoice. Otherwise it needs review. So a card entered or corrected after metering leaves its items needing review until a restatement brings the records to the contracted rates. A run goes `stale` when anything it read would now read differently: late records, a card, an alias, an FX row or the month's invoices.

**Accept a difference.** An item that needs review can be accepted with a reason of 10 to 500 characters (`POST /spend/reconciliations/{reconciliation_id}/items/{item_id}/accept`). The acceptor must be an active tenant administrator other than whoever imported one of the run's invoices (409 `same_actor`); this is the maker-checker rule, and a tenant with a single administrator cannot accept anything. Every acceptance is audited with the reason, both variances and the actor. An accepted difference is recorded, but it does not meet Gate 1.

```flow
Check the month's reference data | Confirm the month's rate cards, commitments and FX rates are entered and settled. | Owner: Spend administrator | Human decision: Decide whether any contract change dated inside the month needs a correction and restatement first. | If blocked: Unpriced records stay listed in coverage until a card covers them and a restatement re-prices them; unconverted records convert when the settlement a new FX rate queues has run.
Review coverage | Read the month's coverage and meter gaps and clear unattributed spend with mappings and re-attribution. | Owner: Spend administrator, reviewed by an auditor | Human decision: Agree which unattributed reasons are fixed now and which are explained. | If blocked: A share below 0.98 or any unpriced record keeps attribution unmet.
Import the provider invoice | Dry-run the invoice file, then import it for the provider's billing month. | Owner: Administrator A, the importer | Human decision: Confirm the invoice reference, currency and billing month against the provider document. | If blocked: 422 invoice_rejected lists every refused line; nothing is stored until the file is corrected.
Run the reconciliation | Reconcile the provider's month and read each item's stored and re-priced variance. | Owner: Spend administrator | Human decision: Decide whether a difference is a metering, pricing or invoice question. | If blocked: 409 invoice_missing when the month has no current invoice; 422 currency_mismatch when its invoices differ in currency.
Resolve or accept differences | Correct cards and restate, or accept an explained difference with a written reason. | Owner: Administrator B, not the importer | Human decision: Accept only a difference that is explained and evidenced outside the system. | If blocked: 409 same_actor when the importer tries to accept; the item stays open.
Read the Gate 1 status | Request the month's gate and meter gaps and keep both responses with the month's evidence. | Owner: Auditor or administrator | Human decision: Treat the month as reconciled only when gate_met is true and the meter gaps are explained. | If blocked: Missing, stale or accepted reconciliations are listed by provider and keep the gate unmet.
```

#### The Gate 1 status

`GET /api/v1/spend/gate?period=2026-10` answers whether a month meets Gate 1. It is met only when both halves are met.

| Half | Met when | Reasons or lists when not met |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attribution (the reporting month) | The attributed share is at least 0.98, and no record is unpriced, unconverted or waiting for an FX rate | `below_target`, `no_priced_usage`, `unpriced_usage`, `unconverted_usage`, `fx_pending` |
| Reconciliation (each provider's billing month) | Every provider with a current invoice or tenant-billed priced usage has a current, fresh run within tolerance | `missing_reconciliations`, `stale_reconciliations`, `accepted_exceptions` |

```json
{
  "period": "2026-10",
  "gate_met": false,
  "attribution": {"attributed_share": "0.991204", "target": "0.98", "met": true, "reasons": []},
  "reconciliation": {"met": false, "missing_reconciliations": ["anthropic"], "stale_reconciliations": [], "accepted_exceptions": [], "tolerance_pct": "1.00"},
  "backfill_source": "model_gateway_records"
}
```

The rules are deliberately strict: no unpriced record is allowed, group attribution does not count, an accepted difference does not meet the gate, and an item needs both figures within 1%. Shares are shown rounded toward zero and variances away from it, while the verdicts use the exact values, so a share of 0.979996 is shown as `0.979996` and is not met. An invoiced provider with no metered records is listed too, because it can point to a broken hook, a provider-name mismatch or usage on a key the tenant did not pay for. The response repeats `backfill_source`, so you know whether lost model-call writes can still be recreated before you trust the month.

Gate 1 does not check everything. Meter gaps are reported beside the attribution figures but do not fail the gate: usage that could not be written or was lost at shutdown, tool calls that no card prices, and usage paused for the tenant with `spend.metering_paused`, which is not in the share at all. Storage, in-house GPU hours and in-house model serving have no provider invoice, so they are never reconciled. Read `GET /spend/gaps` for the month before you treat its figures as complete.

```flow
Read the reasons | Start from attribution.reasons and the three reconciliation lists in the gate response.
Fix attribution | Add mappings or nodes, then run re-attribution for the month.
Fix prices and rates | After adding a card, run POST /spend/usage/restate for the provider's billing days (at most 92). A correction queues its own restatement, and a new FX rate queues its settlement.
Re-run reconciliation | Reconcile every missing or stale provider again after the records change.
Read the gate again | Request the gate for the same month and compare it with the earlier response.
```

#### Who can read what

Reads need the `audit:read` scope. Beyond that, one rule decides what each reader sees.

| Read | Administrator (a person) | Auditor (a person with unrestricted domains) | Anyone else |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Usage records and rollups | Every record and row | Every record and row | Only records of agents they may see, and records with no agent; contract terms and user ids hidden; no rate-card or commitment grouping |
| Coverage, meter gaps, jobs and GPU allocations | The whole tenant | The whole tenant | Refused, 403 `tenant_wide_read_refused` |
| Rate cards, commitments and price quotes | Yes | Yes | Refused, 403 `commercial_read_refused` |
| Invoices, reconciliations and the Gate 1 status | Yes | Yes | Refused, 403 `commercial_read_refused` |
| Changes, imports, jobs and acceptance | Yes, signed in as a person | No | No |

"Anyone else" includes the CFO role and every other domain role, and machine credentials without the administrator scope. A finance team reads coverage, reconciliations and the gate through a person with the auditor or administrator role. Under the agent visibility rule a reader sees records with no agent, records of shared agents in their domains (every shared agent, for a machine credential) and records of their own personal agents. Tenant-wide figures are refused rather than filtered, because a filtered total would let a reader work out other agents' spend by comparing two views. Rate cards, commitments, prices, invoices, reconciliations and the gate are for a human administrator or auditor only: an API key or agent token is refused them whatever scopes it holds, since machine credentials can hold `audit:read` through agent grants. The audit rows of those writes and of spend jobs carry the same figures, so `GET /audit` hides them from the same readers, also after the feature is turned off, since audit rows are kept. A deployment can opt out with `AGENTICORG_SPEND_AUDIT_COMMERCIAL_FILTER=false`, which shows those rows to every audit reader again, as before.

#### What is not in phase 1

- **No spend screen.** Phase 1 is API-only. The app's existing cost views, such as the Cost Dashboard at `/dashboard/costs` (administrators and CFOs; it has no sidebar entry), read the existing cost ledgers, not these usage records.
- **No spend dashboards, budgets, alerts, forecasts, statements or month close.** These belong to later phases; freezing closed months and statements belong to phase 2. Spend intelligence does not block or throttle a call because of its spend.
- **Some usage is not metered:** the embedding backfill command and seed data, the voice runtime's own speech-to-text and text-to-speech outside the speech store, and the tool gateway's own completion path.
- **No batch flag on records.** Reconciliation re-prices every group as non-batch usage.
- **No HTTP write for GPU hours.** Standing pools come from the deployment setting and metered hours from an operator command, because a tenant administrator must not set a cost shared by every tenant.

For the full behaviour, error codes and limits, read the [spend intelligence reference](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/finops/spend-intelligence.md).

Next: [Model Gateway](/docs/model-gateway), [Audit and monitoring](/docs/audit-and-monitoring), [Workspace and roles](/docs/workspace-and-roles), [API, SDK and MCP](/docs/api-sdk-mcp).


### Troubleshooting by symptom

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/troubleshooting
Audience: Everyone. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Start with the smallest failing layer

Record the exact screen, timestamp, company, safe run reference and error code. Separate sign-in, permissions, model, knowledge, connector, workflow and provider issues. Changing all configuration at once makes the cause harder to find.

#### Symptom checklist

| Symptom | First checks | Safe recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cannot sign in | Correct deployment, email/invitation, expired session | Use password recovery or administrator identity support |
| Menu missing / `403` | Assigned role and route/tool scope | Have the owner grant the required permission; no shared admin login |
| Data missing after company switch | Selected company, resource ownership, binding | Return to authorized context and re-test; do not copy another company's IDs |
| Model credential missing | Provider/kind, tenant/company, model ID | Configure the correct credential and test a short task |
| Overload / rate limit | Provider incident, quota, concurrency | Bounded retry/backoff or approved model routing |
| Connector appears configured but fails | Upstream scope, secret binding, API contract, health age | Perform a bounded read test and correct configuration |
| Document upload fails | Supported type/limits, corruption, extractable text | Use the original supported file or a cleaner scan |
| OCR text is wrong | Orientation, language, scan quality, reading order | Compare against original; correct source or request manual review |
| Search has no result | Extraction/indexing, embedding availability, scope | Test a known phrase and the retrieval service separately |
| Workflow waits | Approval/event/wait step, worker availability | Review the waiting condition; do not bypass required approval |
| Workflow runs twice | Trigger/retry history, idempotency | Confirm external effects before retrying |
| Voice call has no reply | Callbacks, signature, mapped active agent, model | Inspect provider status and runtime health; no unsigned fallback |
| RPA times out | Target changes, session, selectors, approved domain | Pause schedules and revalidate the script in a test environment |
| Commerce answer is stale | Source sync, artifact TTL, revocation and merchant state | Refresh through the supported path; do not promise final inventory/price |
| Case decision refused | Current version, issuer configuration, distinct approvals | Resolve the exact reason and request a current decision |
| A screen says a service is off, or `idp_disabled`, `conversation_disabled` or `spend_disabled` | The service's deployment setting is off (the default) | Ask the platform owner whether it should be on; this is configuration, not an empty result |
| Run refused with `guardrail_blocked` / `E1016` | A guardrail rule at that stage blocked it | Review the rule with its owner on the Guardrails page; do not reword input to get past it |
| `423` or a tool result with `operator_override` / `E1013` | An operator halt or throttle covers the model, agent, workflow or tool pipeline | Ask the administrator who placed it; do not work around it |
| `409` "Agent is paused" | The agent is paused and the deployment refuses paused agents (`AGENTICORG_PAUSED_AGENTS_REFUSED`, off by default) | Have the owner resume the agent, or use another active agent |
| Run stopped with a `limit` block | The agent's own step, duration or tool-call limit, or its loop rule, applied while `AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_LIMITS_ENABLED` is on (off by default) | Review the limits and the repeated tool calls before running it again |
| Approval decision returns `409` | You already voted on the item, or its policy changed while it waited | See [multi-person approval rules](/docs/approvals#multi-person-approval-rules) |
| `403` `human_session_required` | An API key or agent token tried a governed-case action reserved for a person | Sign in as the named person |

#### Distinguish refused, failed and unavailable

Refused means a boundary prevented the action. Failed means the attempted path did not complete. Unavailable can mean a provider capability is absent or a tenant feature is disabled. None should be turned into a fabricated success.

`governed_cases_disabled` is feature configuration; `decision_service_not_configured` is an issuer dependency; `case_changed` means existing decision evidence is no longer current. Do not edit an underlying record to bypass these conditions.

#### Reproduce safely

Use a synthetic record with the same role, company, source version and input shape. First verify the standalone provider/model/knowledge path, then the agent, then the workflow/channel. A successful admin test does not validate an operator's permissions.

If production customer data is required to diagnose the problem, use the organization's approved private evidence channel. Screenshots can contain sensitive fields; redact before sharing.

#### Escalate with useful evidence

Send expected versus actual behavior, reproduction steps, safe references, environment/version and attempted recovery. State whether a payment, email, account change or other external action may already have happened. Never send raw tokens or credentials.

When an external effect is ambiguous, pause and confirm with the system of record. A retry that makes the UI green but duplicates a customer action is not a fix.


### Seller and buyer commerce with OACP

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/commerce
Audience: Merchants and bank merchant-service teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### The end-to-end ownership model

AgenticOrg runs seller/buyer agents and their skills, knowledge and approved integration paths. Grantex supplies trust, policy and canonical artifact authority. Shopify, another merchant system or a catalog file the merchant uploads remains the operational source of truth. Buyers pay on the merchant's own payment page, its Shopify checkout or its own Plural account; AgenticOrg never collects the money. Banks, fintechs, providers and POS systems own payment, mandate and fulfillment execution.

For a bank-led pilot with explicit owners, human decisions and blocked paths,
see the [merchant-services process map](/docs/bfsi-merchant-services#process-map).

```flow
Merchant setup | Create the shop on Sell Everywhere, or configure the Seller Commerce Agent and merchant-scoped sources/channels on Commerce Runtime.
Catalog read | Read real products, variants, images, price and inventory snapshots from Shopify with the merchant's own read-only token, or take them from a CSV or JSON upload.
Grantex authority | Send the bounded authority request and obtain validated artifacts. Turning on Sell everywhere does this once by itself.
AgenticOrg cache | Check each artifact's Grantex signature, scope, expiry and revocation status, then persist it with source and freshness.
Buyer conversation | Answer through configured web/agent/channel bridges from supported evidence.
Payment link or prepared handoff | A ready checkout gives the buyer a link to the merchant's own payment page after an allow decision; other paths ask the authoritative provider, merchant or POS to confirm its own action.
```

#### Merchant setup checklist

A merchant sets up a real shop on **Sell Everywhere** (`/dashboard/sell-everywhere`): create or pick the shop, add a catalog, write the returns, shipping and pickup policies (and a flat shipping fee without Shopify), set order limits, choose where buyers pay, then turn it on. Going live enrols the tenant with Grantex, gives the shop an address, publishes its profile and refreshes its artifacts. See [Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere) and the [merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup).

**Commerce Runtime** is the operator console for the same runtime. Open it with an administrator or merchant role. Prepare the merchant identity/reference, source system, owner, catalog scope, approved channels, publishing state and provider/POS references. Review the available form and onboarding packet before requesting authority.

For Shopify, the merchant creates a custom app in its own store with the `read_products` and `read_inventory` Admin API scopes and enters its token; AgenticOrg checks it with one read and stores it encrypted. Every sync uses the merchant's own stored token. A deployment-wide Shopify store is read only for the one operator tenant named in `AGENTICORG_SHOPIFY_ENV_OPERATOR_TENANT_ID`. Product webhooks go to the merchant's own webhook address and are checked with the merchant's own signing secret. No scraping is needed for the supported Shopify path.

A shop without Shopify uploads a CSV or JSON catalog: one product per row, one currency, up to 2,000 products. It is recorded as uploaded by the merchant, never as coming from a store system.

Synchronize a bounded catalog and compare SKU/variant, image, amount/currency and inventory timestamp with Shopify. Confirm a signed webhook is rejected when invalid and accepted only under the configured binding. Webhook receipt alone does not prove catalog freshness; inspect the resulting source snapshot.

#### Ask useful buyer questions

For merchant setup through a third-party buyer app and the Plural payment
boundary, follow the [guided seller A2A journey](/docs/seller-a2a-commerce-journey).
To watch a buyer agent that is **not** hosted on AgenticOrg talk to a
synthetic seller over real A2A HTTP+JSON, use the
[external buyer demo](/docs/external-buyer-a2a-demo). It shows catalogue
browsing, source/freshness labels, purchase refusal, and token revocation.
It does not process a payment.

Try `Which variants of this item are available in the latest snapshot?` and `What source and timestamp support that price?`. Verify the response is merchant-scoped, source-grounded and explicit about stale or unsupported facts. Cached authority can support non-binding Q&A without routing every message through Grantex.

Do not promote stale snapshots into final price, stock, delivery, tax, return or warranty promises. Prepared purchase output is not an order confirmation or paid state.

#### Protocols and channels

The runtime includes bounded protocol-adapter payloads and web/MCP/OpenAPI/A2A/WhatsApp/Telegram bridge routes. Client configuration, provider credentials, platform/marketplace approval and merchant publishing are separate dependencies. A UCP/ACP/schema.org payload does not automatically list a merchant in ChatGPT, Gemini or another marketplace.

With Sell everywhere turned on, a published shop is listed in the AgenticOrg network: buyers reach it from ChatGPT and other MCP apps through `https://mcp.agenticorg.ai/mcp`, from the AgenticOrg shopping bot on Telegram, and on the open web through its UCP profile. That is AgenticOrg's own network, not a listing in another company's marketplace.

Current WooCommerce/ERP/PIM/OMS/WMS/custom-source configuration does not have universal runtime parity with Shopify. Treat each as an integration project until its adapter is implemented and validated; until then, a CSV or JSON upload is the supported way to bring such a catalog.

#### Commerce decisions and the ledger

Before a purchase handoff, an Offline POS handoff, a payment link or a checkout completion goes anywhere, a fixed set of rules decides it. A payment link needs valid artifacts and the merchant's own limits, including its daily maximum; agent-executed completion also needs mandate, consent and the buyer's Commerce Passport cap. The answer is allow or refuse, with the first failing rule as the reason, and it never waits for a person. An allow can be used once, for exactly that payload. Every commerce change is written to the commerce ledger, which an administrator can export and check offline. Optional human review copies a refusal into the review queue without changing it.

UCP and ACP checkout for agent platforms, the AgenticOrg network and the public UCP profile are switched off by default. Turning them on is an operator step, one at a time. Once checkout is on, a merchant that chose where buyers pay hands each ready checkout to its own payment page; see [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid). The agent-executed payment executor stays off, and refunds of completed checkouts are also decided by the same rules.

#### Payments and offline POS

**Payment hand-off.** A merchant chooses its own Shopify checkout or its own Plural account. The buyer pays on that page and authenticates the payment there. A Plural payment confirmed for the right amount, by Plural's signed webhook or the once-a-minute status check, becomes an order on the Orders page with an email to the tenant's administrators; any other payment is refused and logged for a refund. A Shopify-paid order stays in the merchant's Shopify admin.

Plural capability verification records provider-owned, non-sensitive capability evidence. It is not a completed payment or mandate. A human sets up and authorizes payment relationships with the fintech/provider under its own process.

Offline POS handoff means a bounded interaction with a physical-store/POS confirmation path; it does not mean unlimited offline financial authority. Provider/POS/merchant evidence remains authoritative. AgenticOrg does not execute OACP capture, refunds, holds, shipping or order creation merely from cached artifacts; an order is created only from a confirmed provider payment.

Public discovery remains off unless explicitly enabled through platform and merchant settings. Readiness, certification and public standardization are not implied by these routes.

Next: [BFSI merchant-services playbook](/docs/bfsi-merchant-services), [API and agent clients](/docs/api-sdk-mcp).


### External buyer and seller A2A demo

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/external-buyer-a2a-demo
Audience: Merchants, developers and partner integrators. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### See an outside buyer talk to a seller

This walkthrough uses a synthetic local merchant. The buyer is a standalone
Python process, not an AgenticOrg buyer agent. It speaks the A2A v1 HTTP+JSON
message protocol to an AgenticOrg Seller Commerce Agent. A real external
client needs merchant-issued access; knowing an Agent Card URL is not enough.

```flow
Create a local seller | Three synthetic products and their price/inventory snapshots are placed in a development database.
Add source evidence | A local catalog cache record is linked to the exact connector evidence reference.
Approve one buyer | A tenant/merchant/seller/buyer-scoped credential is issued to a separate process.
Ask over A2A | The buyer discovers the card and sends catalog and product questions over HTTP.
Respect the boundary | A purchase request is refused; no order, payment or hold is created.
Revoke and clean up | The buyer receives HTTP 401 after revocation and temporary rows are removed.
```

#### What the buyer sees

| Synthetic product | Price snapshot | Quantity snapshot |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Canvas Tote | INR 1299 | 7 |
| Ceramic Mug | INR 499 | 12 |
| Pocket Notebook | INR 249 | 20 |

The buyer asks to see this catalogue, then asks
about the tote. The seller gives a price and inventory **snapshot** with a
freshness label and says that final price needs merchant confirmation. These
are local teaching fixtures, not merchant offers.

When the buyer asks to buy two totes, the seller refuses transaction
execution. That is the correct result for this A2A question route. An answer
cannot reserve stock, collect money, or create a confirmed order. For a real
purchase, the merchant system and authorized fintech/payment rail must
confirm their own outcomes through separate approved integration steps.

#### Try it on a development stack

Apply local migrations and start the development API with local PostgreSQL
and Redis. From the repository root, with local `AGENTICORG_ENV`,
`AGENTICORG_DB_URL`, and `AGENTICORG_REDIS_URL` configured, run:

```powershell
python -m examples.a2a_commerce_demo.run_demo `
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 `
  --confirm-local-synthetic
```
