The runner rejects production or non-local targets. It keeps the buyer token
out of output, revokes it after the questions, and removes its synthetic
seller, evidence, and cache records. Read the [full local demo guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/a2a-commerce-demo.md)
for setup and expected results.

#### Taking a real merchant further

The real path uses authorized Shopify read-only sync, Grantex-issued and
verified OACP artifacts, an AgenticOrg cache, merchant-scoped buyer access,
and an external A2A client configured for the endpoint. Do not substitute
this synthetic record for signed authority. A2A interoperability is not a
promise that every vendor automatically discovers this seller. Payment and
mandate execution are owned by their fintech/provider; AgenticOrg's current
A2A seller conversation is non-binding.

Next: [Guided seller-to-buyer integration](/docs/seller-a2a-commerce-journey),
[Commerce guide](/docs/commerce), [API and A2A integration](/docs/api-sdk-mcp).


### Seller commerce with an outside A2A buyer

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/seller-a2a-commerce-journey
Audience: Merchants and third-party buyer-agent integrators. Reviewed: 2026-10-01.

#### What this journey proves

An outside buyer agent can ask an AgenticOrg Seller Commerce Agent about a merchant's products over authenticated A2A v1 HTTP+JSON. The buyer can run in a consumer app such as Muse, Instinct or Dots, or in any other service that can make this A2A request. Those names are examples of possible clients, **not** claims of a built-in plugin, vendor partnership, verified client identity or automatic discovery.

The working seller question path is **non-binding**. It can return source-labelled product and inventory snapshots, or refuse. It cannot create an order, hold stock, collect money or create a Pine Labs Plural mandate. A complete paid purchase additionally requires merchant and provider integration, human authorization where required, provider confirmation, order creation and reconciliation. Do not tell a buyer they have purchased until those authoritative confirmations exist. For a paid purchase today, use a UCP or ACP checkout with the payment hand-off instead: the buyer pays on the merchant's own Shopify checkout or Plural page; see [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid).

**Who can operate this journey.** Merchant staff provide product, source-system and payment-provider approvals. An AgenticOrg **tenant administrator** performs the protected Runtime Actions, connector credential/sync, artifact issuance, capability verification and outside-buyer access issuance described below. The `merchant` role can manage merchant configuration, but it cannot perform those admin-only actions. Arrange the administrator handoff before starting the checkpoints. On the [Sell Everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere) page a merchant can connect Shopify or upload a catalog and run the Grantex steps itself; the checkpoints below use the operator console.

```flow
Merchant | Configure the seller, source system, channel approvals and provider reference in AgenticOrg.
Shopify | Sync the merchant's products, variants, prices and inventory read-only.
Grantex | Issue scoped OACP authority artifacts; AgenticOrg validates and caches them.
Buyer app | Receive merchant-approved access and connect to the A2A v1 seller endpoint.
Seller agent | Answer product questions from fresh cached evidence; refuse purchase execution.
Plural/P3P | Verify capability, then use separately approved provider and merchant paths for real authorization and settlement.
```

#### Transaction map: from question to a real sale

The interactive map above lets you select an illustrative buyer app and inspect each message. Its selected app name changes the diagram, **not** the system integration. The same merchant-scoped A2A rules apply to any external buyer implementation. A consumer app operator must explicitly configure the seller endpoint and protect its merchant-issued credential.

| Hop | Who talks to whom | Buyer-visible outcome | Current state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Outside buyer to AgenticOrg seller | The buyer can discover a generic card and use approved seller access. | Available with merchant-scoped credential. |
| 2 | Seller to buyer, using cached Shopify/Grantex evidence | A product answer includes source and freshness; it is not a final offer. | Available, non-binding. |
| 3 | Buyer to seller: "buy this" | The seller refuses execution and can point to a separate prepared handoff. | Available refusal; no order or stock hold. |
| 4 | AgenticOrg verifier to Plural/P3P | Capability evidence says whether a provider-owned path may be available. | Available separately; not a charge or mandate. |
| 5 | Buyer to provider authorization | The buyer reviews terms and authorizes with an approved provider flow. | Requires merchant/provider integration; not wired through the current A2A seller route. |
| 6 | Provider outcome to merchant order system | The buyer sees confirmed only after payment and order/inventory evidence agree. | Requires verified callbacks, merchant execution and reconciliation. |

**Authority boundary.** The third-party buyer agent never needs to live on AgenticOrg. AgenticOrg hosts the seller and maintains the sourced cache; Shopify or the merchant's uploaded catalog owns current commercial facts, Grantex governs the canonical artifacts, and Plural/P3P owns payment execution. The diagram is an explanatory journey, not a live checkout simulator.

#### Checkpoint 1: create the seller

**Tenant-admin action.** Sign in as a tenant administrator and open [Commerce Runtime](https://app.agenticorg.ai/dashboard/commerce-runtime). In **Merchant Commerce Configuration**, set the merchant ID, seller agent ID, display name, source connector, allowed buyer channels, and payment provider type `plural_pine` where appropriate. Save the configuration, then use **Create** under Runtime Actions to create or update the seller onboarding packet. Merchant staff may supply or separately save configuration with their scoped role, but the tenant administrator must perform **Create**. Keep **Public catalog** off until both platform and merchant publishing approvals are in place. A public Agent Card does not publish a merchant catalog.

**Pass check.** Readiness and the onboarding packet show the intended merchant, seller, tenant and source. Keep separate IDs for separate merchants. The packet is not a transaction authority or provider approval.

#### Checkpoint 2: bring source facts

**Shopify and tenant-admin action.** Have the Shopify administrator approve the read-only Admin API access and webhook setup. The AgenticOrg tenant administrator then saves the credential through AgenticOrg's protected custody path in **Shopify Connector**, inspects **Status**, and runs **Sync**. Compare a small sample of product IDs, variants, image URLs, amount/currency and inventory timestamps against Shopify. A webhook signals a possible change; it does not itself prove a fresh snapshot. Other configured ERP or commerce systems need their own validated adapter and must not be treated as Shopify-equivalent by default. A CSV or JSON upload on Sell Everywhere is the other supported catalog source; it is recorded as uploaded by the merchant.

**Pass check.** The sync reports product/variant counts and a source evidence reference for the correct merchant. Prices and stock remain snapshots, not final offers or reservations. Never paste a Shopify token into an A2A message, documentation page or buyer app.

#### Checkpoint 3: establish authority

**Tenant-admin action.** After a successful source sync, select **Issue** in Runtime Actions to request Grantex OACP authority for that evidence. Confirm the returned artifacts are scoped to this tenant, merchant and seller, have source references, have valid expiry/freshness, and are held in AgenticOrg's cache. Use the [OACP commerce guide](/docs/commerce) for the trust and cache model.

**Pass check.** Buyer-facing answers cite the merchant source and freshness. If Grantex is temporarily unavailable, a still-valid cached artifact can support non-binding Q&A; expired, revoked or mismatched authority must fail closed. AgenticOrg does not send every buyer question through Grantex.

#### Checkpoint 4: admit an outside buyer

**Merchant action.** Choose one external buyer-agent integration and agree who operates it. The merchant tenant administrator issues a short-lived, merchant/seller/buyer-scoped credential via `POST /api/v1/a2a/commerce/buyer-access`. The token is shown only when created. Deliver it through a protected channel to the buyer application's secret store. Never put it in a prompt, source repository, URL, chat transcript or public Agent Card. Give each buyer agent a separate credential so it can be rotated or revoked independently.

**Buyer-app action.** Configure the AgenticOrg base URL and the A2A v1 HTTP+JSON endpoint. Fetch `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` for the generic card, then `GET /api/v1/a2a/extendedAgentCard` with `A2A-Version: 1.0` and the merchant-issued bearer credential for the seller-specific card. Discovering the generic card alone grants no merchant access. The buyer app must explicitly configure the endpoint and credential; AgenticOrg cannot make every consumer app route shoppers here automatically.

```http
POST /api/v1/a2a/commerce/buyer-access
Authorization: Bearer <tenant-admin-credential>
Content-Type: application/json

{"merchant_id":"merchant-123","seller_agent_id":"seller-123","buyer_agent_id":"outside-buyer-123","expires_days":7}
```

The `buyer_agent_id` is a merchant-assigned label. Today's server authenticates possession of the issued bearer credential, not the claimed vendor brand. A client calling itself Muse, Instinct or Dots is not automatically a verified client of that company. Consult [A2A integration details](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/a2a-interoperability.md) before making external identity claims.

#### Checkpoint 5: prove the conversation

**Buyer-app action.** Send a synchronous text question to `POST /api/v1/a2a/message:send`. The server derives tenant, merchant, seller and buyer scope from the credential. The client cannot override those values with message metadata. Inspect `sourceLabel`, `freshnessLabel`, `status`, `refusalReason`, `allowedToExecute` and `nonAuthoritativeForTransaction` in the response.

```http
POST /api/v1/a2a/message:send
Authorization: Bearer <merchant-issued-buyer-credential>
Content-Type: application/a2a+json
Accept: application/a2a+json
A2A-Version: 1.0

{"message":{"messageId":"question-123","role":"ROLE_USER","parts":[{"text":"Which canvas tote variants are in the latest snapshot?"}]}}
```

**Pass check.** The answer is sourced and time-qualified. A request to buy, hold stock or create a payment is refused. A wrong-merchant request is refused, an expired or revoked credential is rejected, and stale or unsupported facts are not promoted to final commitments. An external buyer credential must not grant catalog-admin, task or other tenant APIs. The current transport is synchronous text; streaming, push notifications, file parts and durable A2A conversations are not claimed.

Run the [local external-buyer demo](/docs/external-buyer-a2a-demo) to see a separate Python buyer process browse a synthetic seller and test purchase refusal and credential revocation. That demo proves the wire path, not a Shopify/Plural transaction.

#### Checkpoint 6: hand off payment

**Merchant, provider and tenant-admin action.** The merchant and provider set up the Plural/P3P relationship and buyer authorization under the provider's terms. The AgenticOrg tenant administrator configures the provider reference and uses **Verify** to obtain non-sensitive capability evidence. When the buyer asks to proceed, that administrator can use the separate purchase-preparation path to assemble a bounded, source-aware handoff. This is not the A2A question route and it does not create a mandate or payment.

**What a real paid journey still needs.** The approved provider path must obtain any required human mandate/payment authorization, return a verified outcome, and reconcile with the merchant's order, inventory and receipt systems. AgenticOrg may show a paid or confirmed state only after the authoritative provider and merchant outcomes agree. If capability is unavailable, consent is absent, a price or stock snapshot changed, or confirmation is missing, show a blocker or pending state rather than success. [Plural capability guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/plural-pine-p3p-capability-verifier.md) explains the current verifier boundary.

**Current boundary.** AgenticOrg ships a provider capability verifier and non-executing preparation/reconciliation contracts. It does **not** ship a completed Plural/P3P payment or mandate through this external A2A seller route. Provider approval, merchant authorization, checkout/order execution and production rollout are separate integration work. Do not use a simulated capability response as proof of a paid transaction.

**The payment hand-off, outside this route.** UCP and ACP checkout and the AgenticOrg network can end a ready checkout with a link to the merchant's own payment page: its Shopify cart, or a Plural hosted payment page under the merchant's own Plural account. The buyer pays and authenticates there; AgenticOrg never holds the money. A Plural payment confirmed for the right amount becomes an order with an email to the merchant's administrators. That path does not run through the A2A seller route, and agent-executed payment against buyer mandates stays off.

#### Operational acceptance before inviting buyer traffic

| Check | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Merchant and buyer scope | Right seller answers; wrong tenant/merchant/seller cannot read. |
| Product freshness | Source, update time and expiry visible; stale or revoked evidence is refused. |
| Buyer credential | Short expiry, per-client scope, safe storage and immediate revocation test. |
| Purchase request | Refused on A2A Q&A; no order, hold, mandate or payment. |
| Provider handoff | Capability evidence is redacted; real provider and merchant outcomes are required for paid state. |
| Distribution | Each consumer app explicitly configures the A2A endpoint, access and UX. No automatic marketplace listing is implied. |

For an external buyer client, begin with the generic card and a protected credential, then validate the scoped card, one product question, a purchase refusal and a revocation. For an actual customer purchase, do not launch until the merchant, provider and channel have completed their own integration and production checks.


### API, SDK, MCP and A2A integration

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/api-sdk-mcp
Audience: Developers and integration owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Choose an integration surface

Use REST/OpenAPI for application contracts, the repository SDKs for client access, MCP for compatible tool clients, and A2A v1 HTTP+JSON for synchronous text between agents after merchant or tenant authorization. Older AgenticOrg A2A-shaped card/task routes are proprietary; they are not the v1 wire contract. The authenticated **A2A / MCP** screen shows integration material. Public discovery does not grant access to business data or actions. See [external A2A buyer access](/docs/seller-a2a-commerce-journey).

| Surface | Suitable first task | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REST/OpenAPI | Inspect a resource with an approved credential | Deployed API/schema is the contract |
| Python/TypeScript SDK | Company-scoped read or bounded agent run | Installed client version may differ from repository source |
| MCP stdio adapter | List agents/tools in a compatible local client | Client transport support and scopes are still required |
| A2A v1 HTTP+JSON | Read generic card, obtain scoped credential, send synchronous text | Merchant buyer credential permits non-binding seller Q&A only |
| Commerce bridges | Read merchant artifacts and prepare handoffs | Channel approval and provider execution remain separate |

#### Authenticate and preserve context

Use a credential issued for the reviewed deployment and minimum scopes. Keep it in environment/secret storage. Supply authorized company context for execution paths that require it. Never accept a company ID from untrusted model content without server-side authorization.

Route scope checks apply to every credential, Grantex agent tokens included, on the route families that have a scope mapping (`SCOPE_FAMILIES` in `api/route_enforcement.py`), such as agents, chat, workflows, approvals, audit, connectors, documents, speech, transactions, lineage, spend and content; the A2A and MCP families join them only while their switch is on (see below). On a mapped family an agent token needs the family's scope (for example `agents:read` or `audit:read`) or `agenticorg:admin`, or it gets `403`. Other route families, knowledge among them, have no scope mapping yet: there, any authenticated credential of the tenant passes the scope check, API keys and agent tokens are not limited to a domain, and only the route's own checks, such as an administrator requirement, apply. Issue machine credentials with that boundary in mind. A tenant administrator signed in as a person grants an agent route scopes with `PATCH /api/v1/agents/{id}` and `{"route_scopes": [...]}`, on a shared agent registered on Grantex. Only canonical route-family scopes are accepted there, never `agenticorg:admin` (`422`). Administrator access is the exact scope `agenticorg:admin`; a look-alike such as `agenticorg:admin:full` is not an administrator.

### Obtain a workspace API key

An authorized administrator opens **Settings > API Keys**. Enter a meaningful
**Key Name**, choose **Expires In**, then select **Generate Key**. A short-lived
key is preferable for a first integration exercise. The secret is displayed
only once; place it in approved secret storage rather than a shared document.
The key table shows its prefix, status, last-used time and creation time. Use
**Revoke** for an unused or compromised key and confirm the client can no longer
authenticate.

The current form does not offer a custom per-key scope editor. A named key is
not inherently a narrowly scoped business grant. Review server-side credential
permissions and use the appropriate delegated-grant path when action-level
authority is required. Human case decisions require the named approver's
authenticated session; an admin key must not substitute for it.

The Python SDK supports an API key or delegated grant. Example of a read-oriented client:

```python
import os
from agenticorg import AgenticOrg

client = AgenticOrg(
    api_key=os.environ["AGENTICORG_API_KEY"],
    base_url=os.environ["AGENTICORG_BASE_URL"],
)
agents = client.agents.list()
```

Pin the reviewed Python `agenticorg==0.4.0` or TypeScript
`agenticorg-sdk@0.4.0` release after checking registry availability. These
versions include the runtime resources, A2A v1 seller access and machine-safe
case methods absent from `0.3.0`. The MCP adapter release target is
`agenticorg-mcp-server@5.0.0`; its execution and SOP submission tools require
`company_id`. Verify publication, installed version and backend deployment
separately; a repository merge alone does not update an installed client.

#### Connect MCP

There are two directions. The repository MCP adapter exposes AgenticOrg to external
clients. **Connectors > Remote MCP** instead lets an AgenticOrg agent consume a
tenant-owned external server through authenticated Streamable HTTP. Follow the
[remote connector setup and verification workflow](/docs/connectors); generic
connector registration does not discover remote tools. The incoming path supports
bearer authentication and reviewed read execution, not arbitrary write execution.

Use the repository MCP adapter with a client that supports its stdio transport. Configure `AGENTICORG_BASE_URL` and one accepted authentication value: `AGENTICORG_API_KEY` or `AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_TOKEN`. Use the client's secure configuration mechanism instead of committing a key in JSON.

The adapter's execution/SOP-submission tools require `company_id`. Its `run_agent` path goes through A2A. Scope checks on the A2A and MCP routes are off by default (`AGENTICORG_ROUTE_SCOPE_A2A_MCP`). While the setting is off, any authenticated credential reaches `POST /api/v1/a2a/tasks`, `GET /api/v1/a2a/tasks/{id}` and `POST /api/v1/mcp/call`; when it is on, those routes need `a2a:read`, `a2a:write` or `mcp:write` (or `agenticorg:admin`). Administrators must evaluate and configure it, not assume every discovery route is protected identically.

The `seller.*` tools read cached commerce artifacts; they do not authorize payment, orders or holds. Governed-case human decisions have no shortcut through the machine-authenticated MCP adapter.

#### Integration acceptance test

1. Pin a reviewed SDK/adapter version and endpoint.
2. Make a bounded permitted read.
3. Test missing/expired credentials and an insufficient scope.
4. Test cross-company access refusal.
5. Inspect error shapes, retry behavior and rate limits.
6. Prove any external action separately with authoritative confirmation.

A generic MCP bridge is not a universal buyer plugin or marketplace approval. Check the current client/provider documentation before enabling a production surface.

An external A2A buyer agent needs a credential issued by the merchant's tenant
admin. This is a bearer capability, not proof that the client belongs to a
named third-party vendor. Revocation, artifact freshness, and tenant/merchant
binding are checked by the server on each request. No purchase is executed by
the synchronous A2A message path.

For a working external client and a temporary synthetic seller catalog, follow
the [local A2A demo](/docs/external-buyer-a2a-demo). The buyer process imports
no AgenticOrg runtime code and exercises discovery, sourced questions, purchase
refusal, and revocation over HTTP.


### Self-hosting and deployment handoff

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/self-hosting
Audience: IT and platform teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Hosted versus institution-managed

The hosted workspace and a self-managed deployment share product concepts, but operational responsibilities differ. A bank-managed environment must own network, identities, keys, database, backups, model/provider access, workers, updates, security monitoring and recovery. Self-hosting alone does not establish regulatory compliance or data residency.

For most business users, use the approved hosted or institution-provided URL. This guide is for IT/platform teams, not a requirement before completing [Your first agent](/docs/first-agent).

#### Local learning environment

The repository provides a Docker Compose development stack and GNU Make targets. With reviewed prerequisites installed:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org.git
cd agentic-org
make dev
make seed
```

The current local quickstart binds the console to `http://127.0.0.1:3000` and API to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. It includes local data services and development verification, identity and model stubs. The default fake/scripted model responses are explicitly synthetic; this environment does not prove a real provider, bank integration or customer transaction.

Use `make ps` for service status, `make logs` for logs, `make test`/`make check` for repository checks and `make e2e` for browser tests. `make down` preserves data; `make clean` deletes development volumes. Do not run destructive cleanup against a production environment.

#### Prepare production separately

| Responsibility | Required decision/evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Named users, role/scope model, SSO/SCIM where configured |
| Network | Approved ingress/egress, TLS, provider endpoints and private access |
| Database | PostgreSQL/pgvector, tenant isolation, migrations, backup/restore proof |
| Runtime | API/UI, Redis, workers/schedulers, OCR and browser dependencies |
| Models | Allowed endpoints, credentials, retention, cost and region |
| Integrations | Bank/provider contracts, scopes, test accounts and ownership |
| Operations | Monitoring, alert ownership, capacity tests and rollback |

Do not copy development placeholder secrets, fake-model flags or seed identities into production. Air-gapped deployment has additional dependency/model/image and outbound-integration limits; review the operator guide before promising disconnected capability.

#### Feature switches that ship off

The main feature switches that default to off are listed below; `core/config.py` lists every setting. A setting that is off leaves the earlier behaviour in place. Some also have a per-tenant flag, shown in parentheses. These are authority flags managed by the platform operator, except `prompts.maker_checker`, which a tenant admin can set. Set a switch the same way on every service of the deployment, and treat turning one on as a change to plan, test and record like a release.

| Setting | What it turns on |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_MODEL_GATEWAY_ENABLED` (`model_gateway.enabled`) | Routing and access policies and per-model limits on live model calls |
| `AGENTICORG_MODEL_GATEWAY_RECORDS_ENABLED` | A signed routing record for each gateway-routed model call |
| `AGENTICORG_GUARDRAILS_HOOKS_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_GUARDRAILS_ENFORCE` (`guardrails.enforce`) | Guardrail evaluation at every stage, then enforcement instead of flag-only |
| `AGENTICORG_OPERATOR_OVERRIDE_ENABLED` (`operator_override.enabled`) | Halting or throttling a model, agent, workflow or the tool pipeline |
| `AGENTICORG_RESIDENCY_ENFORCE` (`residency.enforce`) | Refusing providers without an attestation for the tenant's data region |
| `AGENTICORG_TRACING_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_TRACING_TIMELINE_ENABLED` | OpenTelemetry spans and stored run timelines |
| `AGENTICORG_SYNTHETIC_CHECKS_ENABLED` | The scheduled synthetic-check sweep and the Observability Checks tab |
| `AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED` | Linking audit rows into a tamper-evident hash chain |
| `AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_LIMITS_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_MEMORY_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_TOOL_REGISTRY_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_RUNTIME_DEBUG_CONSOLE_ENABLED` | Per-agent run limits and loop detection, long-term memory, tool schema checks and the step-through debugger |
| `AGENTICORG_WORKFLOW_BUILDER_V2_ENABLED` | The **Build visually** tab and definition checks on save |
| `AGENTICORG_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_ENFORCED`, `AGENTICORG_CONTEXT_WINDOW_MANAGED`, `AGENTICORG_PROMPT_TYPED_PARAMETERS_ENABLED` | Checking an agent's final answer against its output schema, with escalation to a person when it stays invalid; leaving older tool results out of a conversation that does not fit the model's window; typed prompt parameters |
| `AGENTICORG_PROMPTS_MAKER_CHECKER` (`prompts.maker_checker`), `AGENTICORG_PROMPT_COMPARE_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_EVALS_V2_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_EVAL_PROMOTION_GATE_ENABLED` | Prompt maker-checker, model comparison, evaluation datasets and the promotion gate |
| `AGENTICORG_AGENT_REGISTRY_ENABLED` | Agent registry cards, lifecycle states and the Agent Catalogue |
| `AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_INVENTORY_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_MODEL_CARDS_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_RISK_TIERS_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_GOVERNANCE_POLICY_CONSOLE_ENABLED` | AI asset inventory, model cards, risk tiers and the policy console |
| `AGENTICORG_FINOPS_ATTRIBUTION_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_FINOPS_THRESHOLDS_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_FINOPS_FORECAST_ENABLED` | Use-case cost attribution, thresholds that alert, throttle or suspend runs (they need attribution on), and forecasts |
| `AGENTICORG_SPEND_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED` | [AI spend intelligence](/docs/ai-spend-intelligence) |
| `AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_HYBRID_SEARCH`, `AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_RERANK_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_QUERY_TRANSFORM_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED` | Additional knowledge retrieval stages |
| `AGENTICORG_CONVERSATION_V2_ENABLED` | Banking intents and earlier-turn context in chat, and the Conversations screen |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED` | The bank-operated [customer agent](/docs/customer-agent): customer sessions, the autonomy ladder, cards, the permissions page and the embeddable element |
| `AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_REVOCATION_CHECK=feed` | Refusing grant tokens the authority service has revoked, read from its revocation feed, before they are honoured |
| `AGENTICORG_CONTENT_SERVICES_ENABLED` | Governed drafting, summarisation and extraction APIs |
| `AGENTICORG_IDP_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_WORKBENCH_V2_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_SPEECH_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_TRANSACTION_INTELLIGENCE_ENABLED`, `AGENTICORG_LINEAGE_ENABLED` | Document processing, workbenches, call recordings, transaction findings and lineage, with their [screens](/docs/review-and-operations-screens) |
| `AGENTICORG_PERSONALISATION_ENABLED` | Consent-checked personalisation |
| `AGENTICORG_PAUSED_AGENTS_REFUSED` | Refusing runs, chats and workflow steps for paused agents |
| `AGENTICORG_ROUTE_SCOPE_A2A_MCP` | Scope checks on the A2A task and MCP call routes |

#### Release handoff

Use the repository's reviewed deployment path and migration-first process. Strict (non-local) runtimes make no schema changes at start-up and refuse to start unless the database is at the migration head the build carries, so apply migrations before the release that needs them. Verify exact commit, migration completion, API/UI revisions, traffic, health, database/Redis and required CI. Then test the institution's actual authorized flow with approved synthetic data. A successful build is not a completed deployment or provider canary.

#### User documentation domain

The public user manual is available under `/docs` in the UI build. `docs.agenticorg.ai` should be a DNS **subdomain**, not a separate nameserver delegation by default. Hosting/TLS must route that hostname to the reviewed UI/static documentation service before publishing the link. The repository's documentation-domain runbook explains the release checks and ownership; no DNS change is made by reading this guide.


### Sell through AI assistants: start here

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-start-here
Audience: Anyone new to selling through AI assistants. Reviewed: 2026-10-30.

In 30 seconds:

- AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude can now shop for people. AgenticOrg lets your shop sell to them.
- You set up once: add your products from Shopify or a spreadsheet, write your rules, set your limits and choose where you get paid.
- A buyer asks their assistant for something. It finds your shop, fills the cart and asks for a payment link.
- The buyer pays you on your own payment page. The assistant can never pay by itself.
- You get the order with the delivery address. The video below follows one order, start to finish.

#### Watch one order, start to finish

This recording was made on the live AgenticOrg service with a demo coffee shop, a demo buyer and a Plural test payment. The setup, payment and Orders screens are the real product, and every answer from the shop's side comes live from AgenticOrg. The buyer's assistant is shown as a simple console that makes the same calls an AI app makes, and the opening and closing cards were added for the video.

Video: One order, start to finish. A shop owner sets up a demo coffee shop: products from a spreadsheet (a Shopify store connects through a read-only app in its Shopify admin instead), rules, a shipping fee, limits and their own Plural account. A buyer's AI assistant finds the shop, fills the cart and gets a payment link. The buyer pays the shop, and the order reaches the shop owner with the delivery address. Narrated, with English captions. Watch it at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.mp4 (English captions at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.vtt).

Short on time? The same order in under 4 minutes: the silent stretches are left out, the key screens are shown closer, and the buyer's test screen is redrawn in large type with the same words and prices.

Video: One order, in 4 minutes. A shorter version of the same recording, 3 minutes 53 seconds long: the shop owner sets up the demo coffee shop and turns Sell everywhere on, the buyer's AI assistant finds the shop and fills the cart, the buyer pays the shop on its own Plural page with a test payment, and the order reaches the shop owner. Narrated, with English captions. Watch it at /media/docs/one-order-in-4-minutes.mp4 (English captions at /media/docs/one-order-in-4-minutes.vtt).

#### How it works, in three parts

### 1. You set up your shop once

It takes about ten minutes, on one page in AgenticOrg: **Sell everywhere** (`/dashboard/sell-everywhere`).

1. **Create your shop.** Give it a name.
2. **Add your products.** Pick the way that suits you:
   - **On Shopify?** Connect your store. In your Shopify admin, create an app that may read products and stock, then paste your store address and its access token. Shopify shows the token only once, but you do not need it again: AgenticOrg stores it encrypted, reads your products, prices and stock by itself and never changes them.
   - **Not on Shopify?** Upload a spreadsheet (a CSV file) with your products, prices and stock.
3. **Write your rules.** Your returns and delivery policy. Without Shopify, also set a shipping fee; Shopify shops use their Shopify shipping rates.
4. **Set your limits.** The biggest single order, the most per day and the most items in one order. An AI assistant can never go over them. Nothing is set for you.
5. **Choose where you get paid.** Your own Shopify checkout, or your own Plural account.
6. **Turn it on.** AgenticOrg gives your shop a web address, such as `your-shop.agenticorg.ai`, and Grantex checks your products, prices and stock. Once that address is live, usually within minutes and at most an hour, buyers' assistants can find you.

Figure: One switch, every surface. You turn it on once. AgenticOrg lists your shop and connects it to each surface. Buyers finish and pay with you.

### 2. A buyer shops through their AI assistant

- The buyer connects their assistant to AgenticOrg once: ChatGPT, Claude or another app that can add an MCP server, using `https://mcp.agenticorg.ai/mcp`. Or they open the AgenticOrg shopping bot on Telegram.
- They ask in their own words, for example: "Two packs of filter coffee, delivered to Bengaluru."
- The assistant finds your shop, picks the product, adds the delivery address and the shipping, and asks for a payment link.
- AgenticOrg checks the order against your limits and the facts Grantex checked, records the decision, and only then hands back your payment link. If something is off, for example the order is over your limit, no link is given and the reason is recorded.

### 3. The buyer pays you, and you get the order

Figure: The buyer pays on your page. When the checkout is ready, AgenticOrg checks your shop's facts and limits, then the buyer gets your payment link and pays you there. AgenticOrg never takes the money.

- The buyer pays on **your** page: your Shopify checkout, or a Plural payment page under your own Plural account (card, UPI or net banking). They confirm the payment there themselves.
- A Plural order appears on your **Orders** page (`/dashboard/orders`) with the items, the amount and the delivery address, and your administrators get an email. A Shopify order appears in your Shopify admin, like any other.
- You pack and ship it as usual.

#### Who does what

| Who | Does | Never does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| You, the shop owner | Add products, write rules, set limits, choose where you get paid, ship the order | Give up the sale: you stay the seller |
| The buyer | Asks for what they want, checks the order and pays you | Share card or UPI details with the assistant |
| The buyer's AI assistant | Finds your shop, fills the cart, asks for a payment link | Pay on its own or go over your limits |
| AgenticOrg | Lists your shop, checks every order against your limits, records every decision | Hold the buyer's money |
| Grantex | Checks and signs your products, prices and stock | Sell anything or take payments |

#### What you need

- An AgenticOrg account where you can open **Sell everywhere**.
- Your products: a Shopify store, or a spreadsheet.
- A way to get paid: your Shopify store, or a Plural account. Without one, buyers are told to finish the purchase with you directly.

#### Quick answers

**Do I need Shopify?** No. A spreadsheet works just as well. Shopify only saves you typing, and lets buyers pay in your own Shopify checkout.

**Can the AI assistant spend money without the buyer?** No. It can only ask for a payment link. The buyer opens the link and pays you themselves.

**Where does the money go?** Straight to you, through your own Shopify checkout or Plural account. AgenticOrg never touches it.

**Can I stop selling this way?** Yes. Choose **Pause** on the Sell everywhere page and your shop leaves the network at once. Your shop name and web address stay yours.

**Am I in Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot or Perplexity?** Not yet. AgenticOrg is registering with each of them for every shop on the network; the Sell everywhere page shows each one as it comes.

#### Go deeper

- [Sell everywhere: one switch for every AI surface](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere): every step of the setup page.
- [Getting paid: buyers pay on your own page](/docs/oacp-getting-paid): Shopify checkout, Plural, the Orders page and the email.
- [What OACP is and why you need it](/docs/oacp-overview): the trust layer underneath, for the curious.
- [How OACP works, end to end](/docs/oacp-how-it-works): how your facts are checked, decided and recorded.
- [Example: Nilgiri Tea House](/docs/oacp-example-nilgiri-tea): a live example shop you can try in two minutes.
- [OACP questions and answers](/docs/oacp-faq).


### What OACP is and why you need it

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-overview
Audience: Merchants and business owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-30.

In 30 seconds:

- AI shopping agents use several standards: UCP, ACP, AP2, Visa TAP, Mastercard Agent Pay, Web Bot Auth, MCP and A2A.
- Wiring each one on its own leaves you with several copies of your prices, rules and logs.
- OACP is one trust layer underneath them. You state your facts once, Grantex signs them, and AgenticOrg checks, decides and records.
- Each standard then receives the same facts in its own format. Revoke a fact once and every channel stops using it.
- OACP feeds the standards. It does not replace them, and it is not a certification.

#### Watch one order, end to end

This recording follows one order on the live service, paid with a Plural test payment, from the shop owner's setup to the buyer paying the shop. New to all this? Start with [Sell through AI assistants: start here](/docs/oacp-start-here), which explains it in plain words. The rest of this guide covers the trust layer underneath.

Video: One OACP order, end to end. Recorded on the live service with a demo shop and a Plural test payment. The shop owner adds products (a Shopify store connects through a read-only app in its Shopify admin; the demo shop uploads a spreadsheet), sets rules, limits and their own Plural account, and turns Sell everywhere on. A buyer's AI assistant finds the shop through the AgenticOrg MCP server, fills the cart and gets a payment link. The buyer pays the shop, and the order reaches the Orders page with the delivery address. Narrated, with English captions. Watch it at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.mp4 (English captions at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.vtt).

#### The short version

OACP stands for Open Agentic Commerce Protocol.

It is a safety layer for selling to AI agents. It sits under the agent standards you already hear about. It does not compete with them.

Think of it as one source of truth for your shop. Every agent channel reads from it. Every purchase passes through the same rules. Every decision lands in the same record.

Figure: Five copies versus one layer. On the left, each standard is wired on its own, so the shop keeps five sets of facts, keys and logs. On the right, the shop feeds one OACP layer, and adapters render it for every buyer agent.

#### Why sellers need it

AI agents now shop for people. One agent compares prices. Another fills a cart. A third pays.

Each of those steps has its own standard. If you connect to each standard separately, four problems appear:

- **Many sources of truth.** A price changes in one feed but not another.
- **Many trust set-ups.** Each integration has its own keys and its own checks.
- **Many logs.** Nobody can show one clean record of what happened.
- **No common off switch.** Pull a product in one place and an agent can still buy it somewhere else.

OACP fixes these by putting one layer underneath. You keep your facts in one place. Every channel reads the same signed copy.

#### The standards, in one line each

You do not need to learn these. OACP renders into them for you.

| Standard | What it answers | What OACP gives it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) | Where is the shop, what does it sell, how do I check out? | Your business profile, catalog, checkout and orders |
| ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol) | Which products can an agent buy, and how? | A product feed and agent checkout sessions |
| AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) | What did the buyer allow the agent to spend? | Intent, Cart and Payment mandates, mapped to AP2 field names |
| Visa TAP and Web Bot Auth | Which agent is calling, and is it really that agent? | Signature checks on agent requests |
| Mastercard Agent Pay | Which card-network agent id does this agent have? | The scheme label, recorded from the registry (its wire details are not public) |
| MCP and A2A | How do agents and tools talk to each other? | Checkout tools for MCP clients and a seller agent for A2A |

Figure: Each standard answers one question. Discovery, checkout, payment permission and agent identity each have their own standard. OACP sits underneath and feeds all of them from the same signed facts.

#### What OACP actually is

OACP is three things working together:

1. **Signed facts.** Your catalog, prices, stock and policies become small signed records. Grantex signs them. Each one has an expiry date and a revocation slot.
2. **One decision before money moves.** A fixed rule set, called the arbiter, says allow or refuse. No allow, no payment link and no payment.
3. **One record.** Every decision and every commerce write is recorded in a signed ledger you can export and check.

Adapters then render those facts into each standard's own format.

#### Who does what

```flow
Your shop | Stays the source of truth for products, prices, stock and orders. Shopify, or a CSV or JSON catalog you upload, is the source today.
Grantex | Signs your facts, publishes the signing keys, runs the revocation list and countersigns decisions. It can also issue buyer mandates, for agent-executed payment, which is switched off.
AgenticOrg | Checks every signature, decides each purchase with fixed rules, records it and speaks each standard.
Your payment page | The buyer pays on your own Shopify checkout or your own Plural account, and gets the link only after an allow decision. AgenticOrg never holds the money.
```

#### What OACP is not

Honesty matters here, so here is the plain list.

- **Not a replacement.** OACP renders into UCP, ACP and AP2. Buyer agents still speak those standards.
- **Not a certification.** The groups behind UCP, ACP, AP2 and TAP have not certified or endorsed OACP.
- **Not regulatory approval.** OACP helps you keep evidence. It does not establish regulatory compliance on its own.
- **Not AP2's own format.** Mandates are signed JWTs that use AP2 field names, not AP2's SD-JWT format. Passkey signing of the cart is a Grantex extension.
- **Not switched on by default.** Checkout, the AgenticOrg network, mandates, agent-executed payment and public discovery each sit behind a switch that starts off. Where buyers pay is each merchant's own choice. See [feature switches](/docs/oacp-feature-switches).
- **Not a payment collector.** AgenticOrg never takes the buyer's money. The buyer pays the merchant on the merchant's own payment page.

- [A purchase, step by step](/docs/oacp-buyer-journey)

### Example: Nilgiri Tea House, end to end

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-example-nilgiri-tea
Audience: Merchants, agent platform teams and anyone new to OACP. Reviewed: 2026-10-22.

In 30 seconds:

- Nilgiri Tea House is a live example shop on AgenticOrg. Buyer agents can find it at nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai today.
- It is a made-up tea shop in Ooty with 10 products in rupees. Every product, price and address is synthetic demo data.
- This page follows it from an empty account to a published shop, then shows a buyer agent shopping there.
- You can try it yourself in two minutes: open the shop's profile and search its catalog. No account is needed.
- Each step ends with what to do for your own shop, so you can copy the path one step at a time.

#### Meet Nilgiri Tea House

Nilgiri Tea House is the example merchant we run in production so that you can see OACP working end to end. It sells loose-leaf teas, a gift sampler and a few tea accessories from a (made-up) store in Ooty, in the Nilgiri hills.

Figure: Nilgiri Tea House, from shop to sale. The shop's catalog and limits go into AgenticOrg. Grantex signs those facts. The shop proves its own address with a DNS record. Buyer agents find it and search it, and the arbiter decides every checkout.

Here is what is switched on for it today.

| What | Status | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shop profile for buyer agents (UCP) | Live | `https://nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai/.well-known/ucp` |
| Catalog search and lookup | Live, no key needed | `https://nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai/ucp/catalog/search` |
| Facts signed by Grantex | 11 signed artifacts, all verified | Refreshed automatically when they expire |
| Checkout, cart and order (UCP), ACP feed and checkout | On | Needs a platform API key issued by the merchant |
| Shopping from ChatGPT and other MCP apps | Live, no sign-in, no payment tools | `https://mcp.agenticorg.ai/mcp` ([how to connect](#chatgpt-through-the-hosted-agenticorg-mcp-server)) |
| Payments | Off: no payment method chosen, and agent-executed payment is off | No money can move in this demo |

#### Try it yourself in two minutes

You need no account. Any computer with `curl`, or just a web browser for the first step, will do.

```flow
Open the shop's profile | Visit https://nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai/.well-known/ucp in your browser. This is the file every buyer agent reads first. It names the UCP version, where to send requests and what the shop can do.
Search the catalog | Send the search below with the word chai. The shop answers with its Masala Chai Blend, its price in paise and whether it is in stock.
Search for something else | Try green, kettle or an empty query for all 10 products. One tea, the Blue Mountain Oolong, is sold out on purpose, so you can see how stock is shown.
```

The profile, shortened:

```bash
curl -s https://nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai/.well-known/ucp
```

```json
{
  "ucp": {
    "version": "2026-04-08",
    "services": {
      "dev.ucp.shopping": [
        { "transport": "rest", "endpoint": "https://nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai/ucp" }
      ]
    },
    "capabilities": {
      "dev.ucp.shopping.catalog.search": [ ... ],
      "dev.ucp.shopping.checkout": [ ... ],
      "dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate": [ ... ]
    }
  },
  "signing_keys": [ { "kty": "EC", "crv": "P-256", ... } ]
}
```

The search:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai/ucp/catalog/search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"chai","context":{"currency":"INR"}}'
```

```json
{
  "products": [
    {
      "title": "Masala Chai Blend",
      "description": { "plain": "Synthetic demo product. Black tea with cardamom, ginger, clove and cinnamon." },
      "variants": [
        {
          "sku": "NTH-MASALA-250",
          "title": "250 g",
          "price": { "amount": 44900, "currency": "INR" },
          "availability": { "available": true, "status": "in_stock" }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "pagination": { "has_next_page": false, "total_count": 1 }
}
```

Prices are in the smallest unit of the currency, so `44900` means ₹449.00. The whole shelf looks like this:

Figure: What a buyer agent sees. The 10 products the shop serves, with prices and stock. Every answer comes from facts that Grantex signed and AgenticOrg verified. If those facts expire and cannot be renewed, the shop stops answering instead of guessing.

#### Part 1. How the shop was set up

These are the steps behind Nilgiri Tea House, in order. For the demo, a setup script runs them in one go, calling the same AgenticOrg functions the dashboard uses. For your shop, the **Sell Everywhere** page (`/dashboard/sell-everywhere`) takes you through the same steps and runs the Grantex and publishing steps itself; see [Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere). The detail of each step is in the [Merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup).

```flow start=1
Create the merchant | The shop got its own tenant, an administrator and a merchant record: merchant ID nilgiri_tea_house and seller agent seller_agent_nilgiri_tea. For you: sign up, then type a shop name on Sell Everywhere and select Create shop; the id is generated. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: You need the administrator or merchant role.
Load the catalog | Its 10 products, prices and stock went in, plus one store with opening hours. A real shop connects Shopify read-only, or uploads a CSV or JSON file, on Sell Everywhere. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: A missing Shopify credential, a wrong store domain or a bad file row stops the read and says why.
Set purchase limits | The largest order, the allowed currency (INR) and the most items per order. For you: the Order limits step on Sell Everywhere, which also asks for your daily maximum. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Without limits, Sell everywhere stays off for your shop.
Get the facts signed | The operator added the shop to the Grantex allowlist. AgenticOrg then asked Grantex to sign the catalog, prices, stock, policies and capabilities, and got 11 signed artifacts back. For you: turning on Sell everywhere enrols you with Grantex and asks for the signatures, with no allowlist edit for your shop. | Owner: Platform operator for the demo; AgenticOrg for you | If blocked: The Grantex enrolment row says Waiting while your deployment's Grantex cannot enrol tenants yet.
Check every signature | AgenticOrg checked each artifact's signature, key, expiry and revocation status before keeping it. All 11 passed. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: A refusal names the reason, for example revocation_status_unavailable; nothing from that batch is kept.
Create the signing key | One signing key for the shop. Its public half is published in the profile, so agents can check the shop's own answers. For you: Sell everywhere creates it if it is missing. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Publishing is refused with signing_key_missing until the key exists.
```

#### Part 2. Its own address

Buyer agents need a web address to find a shop. Nilgiri Tea House uses `nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai`, connected by hand with the two records below, the way you would connect a domain of your own. Your shop can get `<your-shop>.agenticorg.ai` from Sell everywhere with no DNS work (while fewer than 20 shops have one), or use a subdomain you own, such as `agent.your-store.example`.

Figure: Nilgiri Tea House's two DNS records. A CNAME routes the address to AgenticOrg. A TXT record with a one-time code proves the shop controls the address. With both in place, the address was attested and the profile went live.

```flow start=7
Ask for the challenge | AgenticOrg issued a one-time code for nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai and showed the TXT record to create. On Custom Domains you see the same thing, with copy buttons. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: An IP address or a one-word host is not accepted.
Add the two DNS records | A CNAME from nilgiritea to ghs.googlehosted.com, and the TXT record _agenticorg-ucp.nilgiritea with the code. Your own domain also needs one Search Console owner; see the custom domain guide. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: DNS changes can take up to an hour to show; check again later.
Verify and publish | AgenticOrg looked the TXT record up, matched the code and linked the address to the shop. The shop opted in to public discovery, Grantex allowed it, and the profile went live. | Owner: AgenticOrg and Grantex | If blocked: The page lists each failed check with its fix, for example serving_host_not_attested.
Certificate | Google issued the HTTPS certificate for the address. That usually takes 15 minutes and at most 24 hours. | Owner: Google | If blocked: After 48 hours without a certificate, check CAA records and that the CNAME is DNS only.
```

Full instructions for your own domain, including every check and its fix, are in [Your own domain for buyer agents](/docs/oacp-custom-domains).

#### Part 3. A buyer agent shops

This is what happens when an AI shopping agent buys tea for someone.

Figure: A buyer agent shops at Nilgiri Tea House. The agent reads the profile, searches, and opens a checkout with its API key. The mandate step belongs to agent-executed payment, which is switched off. The arbiter allows or refuses and records the decision. This demo has no payment method, so it stops before payment.

```flow start=11
Discover | The agent reads /.well-known/ucp and learns the address of the shop's API and which UCP features it supports. | Owner: Buyer agent | If blocked: A 404 means the profile is not published, or its signed facts have lapsed and could not be renewed.
Search | The agent searches for chai and gets the Masala Chai Blend at ₹449, in stock. The answer comes only from verified facts. | Owner: Buyer agent | If blocked: A catalog_unavailable message means the verified facts lapsed and could not be renewed; nothing is guessed. Try again shortly.
Open a checkout | The agent creates a checkout for NTH-MASALA-250, quantity 1, using the API key the merchant issued to its platform. The shop prices it from the same verified facts. | Owner: Buyer agent | If blocked: Without a valid key the shop answers 401.
Mandates, switched off | On the agent-executed path, Grantex would issue three signed mandates: what the buyer allowed (Intent), this exact cart (Cart) and the amount and payment rail (Payment). That path is off, so no mandate is issued here. | Owner: Grantex | If blocked: A mandate is refused when it goes beyond what the buyer allowed.
Decide | For a shop with a payment method, the arbiter checks its signed facts and its limits before any payment link exists, and answers allow or refuse. The decision is sealed in the ledger. | Owner: AgenticOrg arbiter | If blocked: A refusal names the first rule that failed; no link is issued and nothing is charged.
Pay | Nilgiri Tea House has no payment method, so there is no payment step: once pickup is chosen the checkout is ready, and completing it answers payment_failed, "A payment instrument is required to complete." Nothing is charged. A shop that chose where buyers pay answers requires_escalation with continue_url instead: the link to its own Shopify checkout or Plural page, where the buyer pays. | Owner: The shop's payment page | If blocked: Without a payment method, buyers get no payment link.
```

For an agent platform, the checkout request looks like this. The key and the platform profile are your own.

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai/ucp/checkout-sessions \
  -H "X-API-Key: $PLATFORM_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H 'UCP-Agent: profile="https://your-agent-platform.example/.well-known/ucp"' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"line_items":[{"item":{"id":"NTH-MASALA-250"},"quantity":1}]}'
```

How a payment link is issued, and how the switched-off mandate path works, is in [A purchase, step by step](/docs/oacp-buyer-journey).

#### See it with real agents

These are real runs against the live shop on 22 and 25 October 2026, not mock-ups. Each one
searches the catalog, opens a checkout and stops at the payment step. Nothing was charged.

### ChatGPT, through the hosted AgenticOrg MCP server

ChatGPT connects straight to AgenticOrg's hosted MCP server at `https://mcp.agenticorg.ai/mcp`. The
server needs no sign-in and offers shop tools only: search, product lookup, and opening or updating a
checkout. It has no tool that pays, and each caller is rate-limited.

For these runs the server served Nilgiri Tea House alone. For Sell everywhere the same address serves
every shop on the AgenticOrg network and adds two tools: `list_shops`, and `complete_checkout`, which
returns the shop's payment link for a ready checkout. It still has no tool that pays. See
[Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere).

Connect it once:

```flow
Add the server | In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins, choose Add, then Add custom MCP server.
Fill in three fields | Name it Nilgiri Tea House, set Server URL to https://mcp.agenticorg.ai/mcp and set Authentication to No authentication.
Create it | Tick that you trust the server, then choose Create as a plugin.
Shop | In any chat, type @Nil, pick the plugin and ask in plain words.
```

The run below used a free ChatGPT account on 25 October 2026. ChatGPT's menu names may change over
time.

![ChatGPT's message box with @Nil typed; the picker offers the plugin Nilgiri Tea House (AgenticOrg demo).](/screenshots/nilgiri-chatgpt-picker.webp)

1. **Pick the plugin.** Type `@Nil` in the message box and choose Nilgiri Tea House.

![The buyer's message, sent with the Nilgiri Tea House plugin: find masala chai, tell me the price, open a checkout for 1 pack for store pickup in INR, and stop before any payment. ChatGPT worked for 24 seconds and shows Masala Chai Blend from Nilgiri Tea House, a 250 g pack at Rs 449.00, in stock, black tea blended with cardamom, ginger, clove and cinnamon.](/screenshots/nilgiri-chatgpt-request.webp)

2. **Ask in plain words.** Ask it to find masala chai, open a checkout for one pack for store pickup,
   and stop before paying. In 24 seconds ChatGPT searched the catalog and found Masala Chai Blend
   (250 g, in stock, ₹449.00).

![ChatGPT's checkout card: checkout created successfully, store pickup selected at Nilgiri Tea House, Ooty, India (demo store). Item 1 at Rs 449.00, pickup fee Rs 0.00, total Rs 449.00, checkout status Ready for completion, payment: no payment made. Checkout ID chk_b874442731f24f9f8308752406904b57. What this means: the checkout is ready for the next step with one 250 g pack and store pickup configured; it stopped before payment, no payment instrument was added and no charge was made.](/screenshots/nilgiri-chatgpt-checkout.webp)

3. **Checkout, then stop at payment.** ChatGPT opened the checkout and chose pickup at the Ooty
   store, which costs nothing. The checkout is ready for completion with a total of ₹449.00, and no
   payment was added or charged. A shop that has chosen where buyers pay would give the buyer a link
   to its own payment page here, only after the arbiter allows it.

ChatGPT may show a product photo it found on its own. The shop's catalog has no real photos, so any
picture you see there does not come from Nilgiri Tea House.

### Gemini, through the AgenticOrg MCP server

Gemini CLI was connected to the `agenticorg-mcp-server` UCP tools, pointed at the shop's profile.
Gemini asked before every tool call, and each call was approved by hand.

![Gemini summarises its run: it found Masala Chai Blend, NTH-MASALA-250, at Rs 449 in stock, opened checkout chk_b07d…f2d for one 250 g pack with a total of Rs 449, and the shop answered that the order still needs a fulfilment choice, shipping or pickup.](/screenshots/nilgiri-gemini-summary.webp)

1. **Search and checkout.** Gemini found Masala Chai Blend (NTH-MASALA-250) at ₹449, in stock,
   and opened a checkout for one pack. The shop priced it at ₹449 and marked it `incomplete`: it
   still needed to know how the tea reaches the buyer.

![Gemini updates the checkout to in-store pickup at Nilgiri Tea House, Ooty, with a pickup fee of Rs 0; the session moves to ready_for_complete with totals of 44900 subtotal, 0 fulfilment and 44900 total.](/screenshots/nilgiri-gemini-pickup.webp)

2. **Pickup chosen.** Gemini chose in-store pickup at the Ooty store, which costs nothing. The
   checkout moved to `ready_for_complete` with a total of ₹449.

![The shop's answer to completing the checkout: an error message with code payment_failed, "A payment instrument is required to complete.", severity recoverable, path $.payment.](/screenshots/nilgiri-gemini-payment-stop.webp)

3. **Stop at payment.** Asked to complete, the shop answered `payment_failed`: "A payment
   instrument is required to complete." That is the payment layer. A shop that has chosen where
   buyers pay would answer with a link to its own payment page here, only after the arbiter allows it.

### Telegram, through an AgenticOrg agent

An AgenticOrg agent with the `ucp_buyer` connector answers in a Telegram bot. It may search, read
and open checkouts at sandbox shops, and it has no tool that pays. Asked "Find masala chai at
Nilgiri Tea House and open a checkout for one", it replied:

![In Telegram, the buyer asks "Find masala chai at Nilgiri Tea House and open a checkout for one." The bot replies: Item found: Masala Chai Blend, 250 g, Rs 449, in stock. Checkout ID: chk_de0b0a92da6446259b4147662d72c60f. Status: incomplete. Total: Rs 449. Behind that one message the agent searched the catalog, opened the checkout at the shop (HTTP 201)
and answered, in about 30 seconds. To give your own agent these tools, see the

#### Do the same for your shop

| Nilgiri Tea House did | You do | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Created its merchant and seller agent | Sign up and create your shop | Sell Everywhere |
| Loaded 10 synthetic products | Connect Shopify read-only, or upload a CSV or JSON file | Sell Everywhere |
| Had no shipping fee | Write your policies, and set a shipping fee if you have no Shopify | Sell Everywhere |
| Set limits in INR | Set your order limits, daily maximum and currency | Sell Everywhere |
| Had no payment method | Choose your Shopify checkout or your Plural account | Sell Everywhere, Payments |
| Got 11 artifacts signed and verified | Turn on Sell everywhere; it enrols you with Grantex and asks for the signatures | Sell Everywhere |
| Proved nilgiritea.agenticorg.ai | Take the address Sell everywhere gives you, or add your own subdomain and its records | Sell Everywhere, or Custom Domains |
| Published its profile | Nothing: Sell everywhere creates the key and publishes, and Publish shows why if it waits | Sell Everywhere |
| Opened checkout and the ACP feed | Issue each agent platform its own API key | Settings, API keys |

Most steps take a few minutes. Waiting for DNS and the certificate usually takes the longest.

#### What this demo does not do

- **No real products or customers.** Every product, price, store and address is synthetic, and each product description starts with "Synthetic demo product".
- **No money moves.** The demo has no payment method, so no checkout gets a payment link, and agent-executed payment is off.
- **No shipping rates.** The demo sets no shipping fee, so buyers choose store pickup. A real shop gets its rates from Shopify, or sets a flat fee on Sell Everywhere. The demo is for discovery, search and checkout decisions.
- **No store-location search yet.** Store locations are part of UCP 2026-08-25. The shop serves UCP 2026-04-08, so a location search answers that the feature is not served.
