### How OACP works, end to end

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-how-it-works
Audience: Merchants, product and platform teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-30.

In 30 seconds:

- Your shop's facts travel through seven steps before an agent sees them.
- The shop states the facts. Grantex signs them. AgenticOrg checks every signature before it keeps a copy.
- When an agent wants to buy, the arbiter applies fixed rules and answers allow or refuse at once. Nobody waits for a person.
- Every decision is recorded in the commerce ledger. Adapters then speak each standard, so every agent gets the same answer.
- A buyer gets a link to your own payment page only after an allow decision, and AgenticOrg never holds the money.

#### The whole flow on one page

Figure: From your shop to every buyer agent. Seven steps: the shop states its facts, Grantex signs them, AgenticOrg verifies and keeps them, the arbiter decides allow or refuse, the ledger records the decision, adapters speak each standard, and buyer agents receive the same answer.

Each step has one owner. The next sections explain them one at a time.

#### See the flow in one order

The recording below runs the whole flow once on the live service: the shop states its facts, Grantex verifies them, the arbiter checks the order against the shop's limits, and the buyer gets the merchant's payment link.

Video: One OACP order, end to end. Recorded on the live service with a demo shop and a Plural test payment. The shop owner adds products (a Shopify store connects through a read-only app in its Shopify admin; the demo shop uploads a spreadsheet), sets rules, limits and their own Plural account, and turns Sell everywhere on. A buyer's AI assistant finds the shop through the AgenticOrg MCP server, fills the cart and gets a payment link. The buyer pays the shop, and the order reaches the Orders page with the delivery address. Narrated, with English captions. Watch it at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.mp4 (English captions at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.vtt).

#### Step 1. Your shop states its facts

Your shop already knows its products, prices, stock and policies. AgenticOrg reads them. It does not invent them.

- Shopify is read with read-only access, through a custom app in your own store. A shop without Shopify uploads its catalog as a CSV or JSON file instead, recorded as uploaded by you.
- Your merchant settings add the rest: order limits, your shipping fee, stores, where buyers pay and your policies.
- Other systems (WooCommerce, ERP, PIM and others) can be saved as settings. They stay "pending adapter" and are never called.

#### Step 2. Grantex signs each fact

AgenticOrg sends the facts to Grantex and asks for authority. Grantex turns each fact into a signed record, called an artifact.

Every artifact carries:

- a signature (ES256) over the exact content;
- an expiry time, so old facts stop counting;
- a slot on a public revocation list, so a fact can be withdrawn.

Grantex publishes the keys that check these signatures, and the revocation list. Anyone can check an artifact with those two public things.

#### Step 3. AgenticOrg checks before it keeps anything

AgenticOrg verifies every artifact before it stores a copy. This is the most important safety step.

Figure: Four checks before a fact is kept. Each artifact must pass the signature check, come from a published Grantex key, be in scope and unexpired, and be valid on the revocation list. Passing artifacts are kept with source and freshness labels. A failure keeps nothing from that batch.

In production, staging and preview, one failed artifact means nothing from that batch is kept. This is called strict mode, and it is on by default there.

#### Step 4. The arbiter decides

When an agent wants to buy, the arbiter decides. It is a fixed set of rules, not a person.

- It answers **allow** or **refuse**. It never answers "pending".
- An allow is single use. It is bound to the exact cart, price and quantity, and it expires after 10 minutes.
- A refusal names the first rule that failed, so you know exactly why.

Today the decision comes before the payment link: the arbiter checks your signed facts and your order limits, including the daily maximum, and only an allow gives the buyer a link to your own Shopify checkout or Plural page. The rules are listed in plain words in [Safety and trust](/docs/oacp-safety-and-trust#what-the-arbiter-checks).

#### Step 5. The ledger records it

Every commerce write and every decision is written to the commerce ledger in the same database transaction.

- Each row is signed.
- When audit-chain sealing is on, rows are also linked into a hash chain, so a removed or edited row shows up.
- You can export the ledger and check it on your own computer with `scripts/verify_ledger.py`.

Sealing and outside witnessing are separate switches. Both start off.

#### Step 6. Adapters speak each standard

The same verified facts are rendered into each standard's own shape:

- a UCP business profile at `/.well-known/ucp`, with catalog, checkout and orders;
- an ACP product feed and ACP checkout sessions;
- Intent, Cart and Payment mandates with AP2 field names, for agent-executed payment, which is switched off;
- checkout tools for MCP clients, the AgenticOrg shopping bot on Telegram, and a seller agent for A2A.

Each surface has its own switch, so you can turn on one channel at a time.

#### Step 7. Buyer agents get the same answer

Because every channel reads the same signed facts, agents see the same price, the same stock and the same refusals. Once you have chosen where buyers pay, every channel ends a ready checkout the same way: a link to your own payment page, where the buyer pays. AgenticOrg never holds the money.

#### Who does what, at a glance

```flow
States the facts | Products, prices, stock and policies come from your shop. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Reconnect Shopify or upload your catalog again, fix the merchant settings, then read the catalog again.
Signs the facts | Each fact becomes a signed, expiring, revocable artifact. | Owner: Grantex | If blocked: AgenticOrg keeps nothing new and asks for a fresh request.
Verifies and keeps | Signature, key, scope, expiry and revocation are checked before storing. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: The batch is refused with the exact refusal code.
Decides | Fixed rules answer allow or refuse at once. | Owner: AgenticOrg arbiter | If blocked: The refusal names the first failing rule.
Records | The decision and every commerce write go to the ledger. | Owner: AgenticOrg ledger | If blocked: A write route that skips its ledger row is answered as an error.
Hands over the payment link | After a consumed allow, the buyer gets a link to your own Shopify checkout or Plural page and pays there. A confirmed Plural payment becomes an order. | Owner: AgenticOrg, then your payment page | If blocked: Without a payment method, the buyer gets no link and is told to pay with you directly.
```

#### Where to go deeper

- [A purchase, step by step](/docs/oacp-buyer-journey)
- [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid)
- [Safety and trust](/docs/oacp-safety-and-trust)
- Technical references: [artifact cache guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/artifact-cache-guide.md) and [arbiter and ledger](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/arbiter-ledger.md)


### A purchase, step by step

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-buyer-journey
Audience: Merchants and agent platform teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-30.

In 30 seconds:

- A buyer's agent finds a product, opens a checkout and asks to complete it.
- Today the buyer pays on your own page: the arbiter checks your signed facts and your limits, then the buyer gets a link to your Shopify checkout or Plural payment page.
- The buyer authenticates and pays there, for example with 3-D Secure or their UPI PIN. AgenticOrg never holds the money.
- Agent-executed payment is built but switched off: Grantex Intent, Cart and Payment mandates, the buyer's passkey and RBI AFA for UPI AutoPay.
- Every decision lands in the ledger, whichever way the buyer pays.

#### A purchase today: the buyer pays on your page

The example uses a synthetic shop, Merchant Example, that has chosen where its buyers pay on the Sell Everywhere page.

Figure: The buyer pays on your page. The buyer's checkout is ready. The arbiter checks the shop's signed facts and limits and records its decision. The buyer gets a link to the shop's own Shopify cart or Plural payment page and pays there. The shop gets the order.

```flow
Find the product | The buyer's agent searches your catalog through UCP, the ACP feed, the AgenticOrg MCP server or the AgenticOrg bot on Telegram. Prices and stock come from verified facts. | Owner: Buyer agent | If blocked: Without fresh verified facts the catalog answers with no products.
Open a checkout | The agent opens a checkout and chooses shipping, or store pickup where your shop has store locations. AgenticOrg prices it from the verified catalog and your shipping rates and moves it to ready_for_complete. | Owner: Buyer agent and AgenticOrg | If blocked: An unknown or out-of-stock item, or no shipping option for the buyer's country, keeps the session incomplete.
Arbiter decides | Before any link exists, the arbiter checks your signed facts and your order limits, including the daily maximum. The allow is used once, for exactly this checkout. | Owner: AgenticOrg arbiter | If blocked: A refusal names the rule and the reason, for example daily_amount_cap_exceeded, and no link is issued.
Payment link | Complete answers requires_escalation with continue_url: your Shopify cart with the items in it, or a Plural payment page under your own Plural account. Asking again returns the same link while it is valid. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: payment_setup_incomplete means your payment method is not fully set up; payment_handoff_unavailable means the shop has no payment link for this channel, or that the items cannot be paid in its Shopify checkout: an item that is not from its Shopify store, an item sold by a unit such as weight, or more than 9,999 of one item.
Buyer pays | The buyer opens the link and pays on your page by card, UPI or net banking, authenticating with 3-D Secure or their UPI PIN. | Owner: Buyer and your payment page | If blocked: A Plural link lasts 30 minutes; after that the buyer asks for a new one.
Order | Plural confirms the payment through its signed webhook or the check AgenticOrg runs every minute, and the checkout becomes an order on your Orders page, with the delivery address the buyer gave and an email to your administrators. A Shopify order is in your Shopify admin. | Owner: Your payment provider and AgenticOrg | If blocked: A payment for the wrong amount never becomes an order; it is logged so you can refund it in Plural.
```

No mandate, passkey or spending cap is asked for on this path. The agent holds no payment credential and moves no money, and the buyer authenticates on the payment page. See [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid) to set it up.

#### Agent-executed payment with mandates (switched off)

AgenticOrg also has a path where the purchase completes without leaving the chat: the payment provider charges against signed buyer mandates. It is built but switched off. Payment execution stays off until a payment-provider sandbox run has passed, and a shop that chose where buyers pay always gets a payment link instead. The rest of this page explains how that path works.

The example uses Merchant Example and a buyer who allows up to ₹2,000.

Figure: A purchase with mandates. The buyer agent opens a checkout. Grantex issues the Intent, Cart and Payment mandates, the buyer's passkey signs the cart when the buyer is present, and AgenticOrg verifies all three. The arbiter decides; on allow the payment provider charges once and the order is confirmed; everything is recorded. This path is switched off.

### The three mandates, in plain words

A mandate is a signed note of what the buyer allowed. Grantex issues all three. Each lives at most 10 minutes.

| Mandate | Plain meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intent | "My agent may spend up to this much, at these shops." | Up to ₹2,000 at Merchant Example |
| Cart | "This exact cart, and nothing else." | One office tote, ₹1,499, by its hash |
| Payment | "Charge this amount, on this rail, to this token." | ₹1,499 by card token on Plural |

The Cart mandate binds the cart by a hash. Change one item or one price and the hash changes, so the mandate no longer matches.

The Payment mandate never holds the card or UPI token itself. It holds a fingerprint of it.

### Step by step: who does what

```flow
Find the product | The buyer agent reads the shop's catalog through UCP or the ACP feed. Prices and stock come from verified facts. | Owner: Buyer agent | If blocked: Without fresh verified facts the catalog answers with no products.
Open a checkout | The agent creates a checkout session. AgenticOrg prices it from the synced catalog and moves it to ready_for_complete. | Owner: Buyer agent and AgenticOrg | If blocked: An unknown or out-of-stock item keeps the session incomplete.
Intent mandate | Grantex records what the buyer allowed: the description, the spending cap and the shops. | Owner: Grantex | If blocked: Grantex refuses when the buyer's passport cap or consent does not allow it.
Cart mandate and passkey | Grantex binds the exact cart. When the buyer is present, the buyer's passkey on their own device signs the cart hash. | Owner: Buyer and Grantex | If blocked: A missing, wrong or replayed passkey signature refuses the cart.
Payment mandate | Grantex binds the amount, the currency, the rail and a fingerprint of the payment token. | Owner: Grantex | If blocked: Card data in the request, or an unknown rail, is refused.
AgenticOrg verifies | AgenticOrg checks all three signatures, the revocation list and that the chain links to this exact checkout. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: Any failed check stops the purchase with its refusal code.
Arbiter decides | Eight fixed rules run in order. The answer is allow or refuse, at once. | Owner: AgenticOrg arbiter | If blocked: The first failing rule is the reason, and it is recorded.
RBI AFA, India only | A UPI AutoPay payment needs the buyer to approve with their UPI PIN in their own UPI app. AgenticOrg returns that step and waits for nothing. | Owner: Buyer and their bank | If blocked: Completion is refused until verified AFA evidence arrives from the provider.
Payment | The payment provider charges once, against the consumed allow decision. The three mandate hashes travel with the order. | Owner: Payment provider | If blocked: With payment execution off, as it is today, checkout stops at executor_unavailable and nothing is charged.
Order and receipt | The order is created and a signed order update goes to the agent platform. The ledger holds the mandates, the decision and every payment call. | Owner: AgenticOrg and the merchant | If blocked: A failed payment returns the session to ready_for_complete.
```

### What the decision can say

Figure: Three possible answers. On the mandate path the arbiter allows, and the payment runs once; or it refuses and names the first failing rule, and nothing is charged; or, for UPI AutoPay, it asks for the buyer's AFA step, and the next attempt gets a fresh decision.

### When the buyer is not present

Sometimes an agent buys while the person is away. This is called "human not present".

- There is no passkey step, because nobody is there to touch it.
- The shop must set stricter limits for these purchases, for example a lower amount cap. Without them, every not-present purchase is refused.
- The Intent mandate's cap must cover the total.
- For UPI AutoPay, the AFA exemption never applies.

### RBI AFA for India, in plain words

RBI rules ask for an additional factor of authentication (AFA) on some UPI AutoPay payments.

| Payment | AFA needed? |
| --- | --- |
| Setting up the mandate, and the first debit with it | Always |
| A later debit up to ₹15,000 | No |
| A later debit up to ₹1,00,000 for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions or credit-card bills | No |
| A later debit above those amounts | Yes |
| Amount, currency or debit type unknown | Yes, to stay safe |

A checkout is always a set-up plus a first debit, so AFA always applies there. The limits are settings, so a future RBI change is a configuration change.

On today's path a buyer who pays by UPI on your Plural page approves the payment with their UPI PIN there, as with any online payment.

#### What is on by default

> The checkout routes, the AgenticOrg network, mandates and payment execution each start switched off. Once checkout is on and you have chosen where buyers pay, a ready checkout gives the buyer a link to your own payment page. Agent-executed payment stays off, so no money moves without the buyer paying on that page. See [feature switches](/docs/oacp-feature-switches).

- [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid)
- [Safety and trust](/docs/oacp-safety-and-trust)
- [Merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup)
- Technical references: [payment hand-off](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/payment-handoff.md), [mandates, UPI AutoPay and RBI AFA](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/mandates.md) and [UCP checkout](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/ucp-checkout.md)


### Merchant setup checklist

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-merchant-setup
Audience: Merchants and platform operators. Reviewed: 2026-10-29.

In 30 seconds:

- Setup has five phases: connect your shop, connect to Grantex, publish your UCP profile, open sales channels, and agent-executed payment.
- For a merchant, phases 1 to 3 are one page, Sell Everywhere, with no step for your platform operator.
- Your UCP profile goes live on an address you control: a platform address AgenticOrg gives you, or your own subdomain proved with a DNS TXT record.
- Buyers pay on your own Shopify checkout or Plural page, which you choose on the Sell Everywhere page. AgenticOrg never holds the money.
- Agent-executed payment with buyer mandates stays off until a payment-provider sandbox run has passed.

#### The five phases

Want to see the result first? [Nilgiri Tea House](/docs/oacp-example-nilgiri-tea) is a live example shop that went through phases 1 to 4 without a payment method.

Figure: Five phases from shop to sales. Connect your shop, connect to Grantex, publish your UCP profile and open sales channels. The fifth phase, agent-executed payment, stays off until a payment-provider sandbox run has passed. Buyers already pay on your own page once checkout is open.

Phases 1 to 3 are one page for a merchant: **Sell Everywhere** (`/dashboard/sell-everywhere`) takes you from a new shop to a published profile, with no step for your platform operator; see [Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere). The **Commerce Runtime** page at `/dashboard/commerce-runtime` is the operator console for the same runtime. You need the administrator role or the merchant role. A few steps are done by your platform operator, the person who runs your AgenticOrg deployment. Those steps say so.

#### Phase 1. Connect your shop

```flow start=1
Create your shop | On Sell Everywhere, choose your shop, or type a shop name and select Create shop. AgenticOrg creates the merchant and its id; you never type one. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Check that you have the merchant or administrator role.
Connect your catalog | Connect Shopify with the Admin API token of a custom app in your own store (read_products, read_inventory), or upload a CSV or JSON catalog. AgenticOrg encrypts the token and never shows it again. Then compare a few products, prices and stock levels with your store or file. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Every sync uses your own stored token; without one it stops with blocked_missing_shopify_credentials. A wrong store address or a bad file row stops the read and says which.
Write your policies | Write your returns and shipping terms, and store pickup if you offer it. Without Shopify, also set one shipping fee per order, its currency and the countries you ship to; 0 ships free. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: A shop without Shopify and without a shipping fee can offer buyers no shipping, so Sell everywhere stays off until it is set.
Set your order limits | Set the largest single order, the most per day, the most items per order and your currency. Nothing is set for you, and the daily maximum must be at least the per-order maximum. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Without limits, Sell everywhere stays off.
```

Where buyers pay is the next step on the same page; the checklist covers it in phase 4, where checkouts end.

#### Phase 2. Connect to Grantex

```flow start=5
Turn on Sell everywhere | Choose your shop name, accept the network terms and turn it on. AgenticOrg enrols your tenant, merchant and catalog source with Grantex itself; nobody edits a list for your shop. | Owner: Merchant, then AgenticOrg | If blocked: The switch stays off until your catalog, policies, shipping fee and limits are done (setup_incomplete names what is missing). Waiting means your deployment's Grantex cannot enrol tenants yet.
Request authority | Going live sends the Grantex authority request once by itself, and Grantex signs your catalog, prices, stock and policies. Your operator can also send it from Commerce Runtime. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: A 202 answer means connector evidence is missing; read your catalog again first.
Verify and keep the facts | AgenticOrg checks every signature, key, expiry and revocation slot before it keeps anything. The Verified catalog row then shows Done. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: Verified catalog shows To do; select Publish to try again. A 422 artifact_verification_refused lists each refusal code, and nothing from that batch is kept.
Ask a test question | Ask your seller agent "Which variants are in stock?" and check that the answer shows its source and freshness. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: A missing answer means catalog, price or stock facts are missing; refresh them.
```

#### Phase 3. Publish your UCP profile

Your UCP profile tells buyer agents where your shop is and what it offers. It is served at `https://<your shop host>/.well-known/ucp`.

With Sell everywhere this phase runs by itself:

- A shop with no address gets `<your-shop>.agenticorg.ai`. It needs no TXT record, because AgenticOrg owns that domain. At most 20 shops get one.
- A missing signing key is created, and the profile is published as soon as nothing stands in the way.
- The **Shop profile** row shows the exact reason when it waits. Select **Publish** to run the steps again.

For a host of your own, ownership is proved with a DNS TXT record. The **Custom Domains** page runs these steps for you:

Figure: The DNS TXT step. AgenticOrg gives you a TXT record name and value. You add it at your DNS provider. AgenticOrg looks it up and, on a match, records that you control the host.

```flow start=9
Choose your shop host | Ask AgenticOrg for a challenge for your host, for example shop.merchant.example. It returns a TXT record name and value. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: An IP address or a single-word host is not accepted.
Add the DNS TXT record | At your DNS provider, add the TXT record _agenticorg-ucp.shop.merchant.example with the value AgenticOrg gave you. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: DNS changes can take time to spread; wait and try the check again.
Verify the host | Ask AgenticOrg to check the record. On a match it stores the proof and links the host to your merchant. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: A host already linked to another tenant is refused.
Create your signing key | AgenticOrg creates one signing key for your shop. Your profile publishes its public half. Rotated keys stay published for at least 7 days. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Publishing is refused with signing_key_missing until a key exists; Publish on Sell Everywhere creates it.
Publish | Record your opt-in to public discovery. The next Grantex authority request asks Grantex to allow discovery for this host. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Refusals name the reason, such as serving_host_not_attested.
Profile goes live | When the UCP profile switch is on and Grantex has issued an allowing discovery artifact, the profile is served. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: The profile answers 404 until every condition holds; the UCP status view shows which one is missing.
```

Your host must also reach the AgenticOrg service with the original host name intact. The easiest way is the **Custom Domains** page. It runs the TXT step above for you, adds the CNAME record that routes the host, and follows the domain until its certificate is live. See [Your own domain for buyer agents](/docs/oacp-custom-domains).

#### Phase 4. Open your sales channels

Each channel has its own switch. Turn on one, test it, then the next.

```flow start=15
UCP checkout | The operator turns on UCP checkout and you issue each agent platform its own API key. Agents can then open checkouts at your /ucp address. | Owner: Platform operator and merchant | If blocked: With the switch off, every checkout route answers 404, the network included.
ACP product feed | The operator turns on the ACP feed. You export it as JSON, JSON Lines or CSV and upload the files where the agent platform asks. | Owner: Platform operator and merchant | If blocked: The feed is refused until the catalog's verified facts are fresh.
ACP checkout | The operator turns on ACP checkout, you opt your shop in, and you issue the platform a key with ACP write access. | Owner: Platform operator and merchant | If blocked: Without your opt-in your ACP routes answer 404.
MCP checkout tools | Sell everywhere shops are served by the AgenticOrg server at https://mcp.agenticorg.ai/mcp, with nothing to set. For an MCP server of your own, set the address of your UCP profile on each install; its checkout tools appear only while your profile lists checkout. | Owner: AgenticOrg, or the platform operator for your own install | If blocked: No profile address, or checkout off, means no tools are registered.
Choose where buyers pay | In the Payments step of Sell Everywhere, choose your own Shopify checkout, or your own Plural account (client ID, client secret and webhook secret, Sandbox or Production, then Test). On every channel above, a ready checkout then answers requires_escalation with continue_url, the link to that page. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Shopify checkout needs a connected store; Plural needs saved credentials with a webhook secret. Without a method, buyers get no payment link.
```

See [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid) for what the buyer sees, the Orders page and the email for each order.

#### Phase 5. Agent-executed payment: off until a sandbox run passes

> Agent-executed payment, where AgenticOrg charges through a payment provider against verified buyer mandates, stays off. It is turned on only after a full run against the payment provider's sandbox has passed in staging, and then one merchant at a time. A shop that chose where buyers pay always hands the buyer a link instead. A shop with neither gives no payment link, its checkouts stop before payment, and no buyer is charged.

```flow start=20
Grantex mandates | The operator turns on mandates and you name your Grantex commerce tenant and merchant in your settings. | Owner: Platform operator and merchant | If blocked: Without mandates, production refuses agent-executed decisions as buyer_authority_verified.
Sandbox credentials | The operator stores the provider's sandbox credentials in the secret manager. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Without credentials the sandbox tests are skipped, not passed.
Staging run | In staging, turn on payment execution for one test merchant and run the sandbox tests and the checkout smoke test. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Any failure keeps payments off.
Check the ledger | Confirm each payment call comes after a consumed allow decision. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: A payment row without a consumed decision is an irregularity; stop and investigate.
Production, one merchant at a time | After owner approval, name the executor for one merchant whose payment method is off, and watch its first orders. A shop with a payment method keeps getting links. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Remove the merchant's executor setting to stop it at once.
```

Mandates matter only for agent-executed payment. A payment link needs none: the buyer authenticates and pays on your own page.

#### Quick test before you go live

- Ask a buyer question and check the source and freshness label.
- Open a test checkout and confirm it reaches ready_for_complete.
- Complete it and confirm the answer is `requires_escalation` with a `continue_url` to your payment page. With Plural in Sandbox, pay the link and check the order on the Orders page and the email.
- Export the ledger and run `scripts/verify_ledger.py` on it.

- [Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere)
- [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid)
- [Feature switches reference](/docs/oacp-feature-switches)
- [Commerce runtime and Shopify](/docs/commerce)
- Technical references: [UCP profile](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/ucp-profile.md), [ACP feed and sessions](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/acp-feed-and-sessions.md), [payment hand-off](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/payment-handoff.md) and the [launch and rollback runbook](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/explainers/launch-rollback-runbook.md)


### Sell everywhere: one switch for every AI surface

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere
Audience: Merchants and business owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-30.

In 30 seconds:

- Sell everywhere puts your shop on every AI surface the AgenticOrg network reaches, with one switch.
- Buyers then find you in ChatGPT, Claude and other AI apps, in the AgenticOrg shopping bot on Telegram, and on the open web.
- You do no setup on each surface: AgenticOrg connects to them once, for every shop on the network.
- If you have no web address for buyer agents yet, AgenticOrg gives you one, such as your-shop.agenticorg.ai.
- You stay the seller. Buyers pay on your own Shopify checkout or Plural page, and you can pause it at any time.

#### One switch, every surface

Figure: One switch, every surface. You turn it on once. AgenticOrg lists your shop and connects it to each surface. Buyers finish and pay with you.

| Surface | How buyers reach you | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ChatGPT, Claude and other AI apps | They add AgenticOrg's server, `https://mcp.agenticorg.ai/mcp`, once as a custom MCP server. They can then list the network's shops, search them, open or update a checkout and get the payment link | Nothing |
| Telegram | They tap your link, `t.me/<bot>?start=<your-shop>`, or search across shops in the AgenticOrg shopping bot. The page shows your exact link | Share your link if you like |
| The open web | AI search engines and agents read your shop's profile at your web address | Nothing |
| Google Gemini and AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity | Coming: AgenticOrg is registering with each program for the whole network | Nothing yet |
| Payment | When the checkout is ready, buyers get a link to your own payment page and pay you there; see [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid) | Choose Shopify checkout or Plural once |

#### Watch it end to end

The recording below shows each step on this page for a demo coffee shop. It then follows a buyer's AI agent as it shops there and the buyer pays on the shop's Plural page.

Video: A real OACP order, end to end. Recorded on the live service with a demo shop and a Plural test payment. The shop owner adds products (a Shopify store connects through a read-only app in its Shopify admin; the demo shop uploads a spreadsheet), sets rules, limits and their own Plural account, and turns Sell everywhere on. A buyer's AI assistant finds the shop through the AgenticOrg MCP server, fills the cart and gets a payment link. The buyer pays the shop, and the order reaches the Orders page with the delivery address. Narrated, with English captions. Watch it at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.mp4 (English captions at /media/docs/oacp-commerce-walkthrough.vtt).

#### Set up and turn it on

Everything happens on one page: **Sell Everywhere** (`/dashboard/sell-everywhere`). It takes about ten minutes.
Steps 1 to 4 show **Done** or **To do**; the catalog step can also show **Read your catalog** (your Shopify
store is connected but not read yet) or **Changed in your store**. Payments has no badge, and step 6 shows
**Live** once your shop is on. The switch stays off until your catalog, your policies, your shipping
fee (for a shop without Shopify) and your order limits are done; the page names whatever is missing.
Payments is not needed to turn it on, but until you choose a method buyers get no payment link and are told
to pay you directly.

```flow
Your shop | Choose your shop, or type a shop name and select Create shop. AgenticOrg gives it an id; you never type one.
Your catalog | Connect Shopify, or upload a CSV or JSON file. This is what buyers will search.
Your policies | Write your returns and shipping terms, and store pickup if you offer it. Without Shopify, also set your shipping fee, its currency and the countries you ship to. Buyer agents read your policies before they buy.
Order limits | Set the largest single order, the most per day, the most items per order and your currency. Nothing is set for you.
Payments | Choose where buyers pay: your own Shopify checkout or your own Plural account. See Getting paid.
Turn on Sell everywhere | Choose your shop name, accept the network terms and turn it on. AgenticOrg enrols you with Grantex, gives you a web address, publishes your shop and has your catalog facts signed.
```

### Connect Shopify

AgenticOrg reads your products with a custom app you create in your own store. It only reads products,
prices and stock.

1. In your Shopify admin, open **Settings**, then **Apps and sales channels**, then **Develop apps**.
2. Create an app, open **Configuration** and allow the Admin API scopes `read_products` and `read_inventory`.
3. Install the app, open **API credentials** and reveal the Admin API access token. Shopify shows it once.
4. On the Sell Everywhere page, enter your store address (`your-store.myshopify.com`) and the token, then
   select **Connect Shopify**. AgenticOrg checks the token with one read, stores it encrypted and reads your
   catalog.

To keep products current, the page shows your own webhook address once you are connected. In Shopify,
open **Settings**, **Notifications**, **Webhooks**, create a **Product update** webhook in JSON to that
address, then paste the signing secret Shopify shows there and select **Connect Shopify** again. Leave the
access token blank to keep the one you saved: Shopify shows a token only once. AgenticOrg checks every
delivery with your secret; a changed product shows **Changed in your store** until the catalog is read
again.

### Upload a file instead

One product per row, one currency, up to 2,000 products:

| Column | Required | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sku` | Yes | `TEA-1` (letters, digits, dots, hyphens, underscores) |
| `title` | Yes | `Nilgiri green tea` |
| `description` | No | `Loose leaf, 100 g` |
| `price` | Yes | `499.00` |
| `currency` | Yes | `INR` |
| `quantity` | Yes | `12` (stock you have) |
| `image_url` | No | `https://cdn.merchant.example/tea-1.png` |
| `url` | No | `https://merchant.example/tea-1` |

A JSON file is a list of objects with the same keys. If a row has a problem, nothing is stored and the
page lists each row and column to fix. Your catalog is recorded as uploaded by you, never as coming from
a store system. Upload again whenever your products change.

### Shipping fee

A shop that uploads its catalog sets one shipping fee per order in the policies step, with its currency and
the countries it ships to (two-letter codes such as `IN`; leave them empty to ship everywhere). Enter 0 to
ship free. Buyers are offered this fee at checkout, and Sell everywhere stays off until it is set. A
Shopify shop uses the shipping rates of its Shopify delivery profiles instead.

### Store pickup

The pickup text is part of your policies: buyer agents read it as wording. Checkout offers store pickup
only when your shop also has a store location in its merchant settings, which the Commerce Runtime page
sets. Sell Everywhere does not add store locations, so a shop that only uploads a catalog offers shipping
and no pickup.

### Order limits

AI agents can only start orders within your limits: the largest single order, the most per day and the
most items per order, in your currency. The daily maximum must be at least the per-order maximum.

Before a buyer gets a payment link, the arbiter checks the order against these limits. The daily maximum
counts, in that currency: the payments confirmed today (by the UTC day), the payment links still open
whichever day they were issued, and every payment link issued today, even after it lapses or its checkout
is canceled, because the buyer can still pay it. A link stops counting when its payment becomes an order
(the order then counts as paid) or when Plural reports the payment failed. Shopify does not tell AgenticOrg when a buyer
pays, so a Shopify link counts all the day it was issued. An order that would go over the daily maximum
gets no link.

#### After you turn it on

The page shows how going live is progressing:

| Row | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grantex enrolment | Enrolled | Grantex signs your catalog facts. No operator edit is needed for your shop. |
| Grantex enrolment | Waiting | Your deployment's Grantex is not ready for enrolment yet; nothing to do. |
| Grantex enrolment | Needs attention | Grantex refused or revoked the enrolment, or could not be reached. The message says whether to retry or contact your platform administrator. |
| Shop profile | Published | Your profile is published on your web address. Buyer agents can read it once the **Your web address** row shows **Live**. |
| Shop profile | Not published | The page says exactly why, for example that your web address is still being set up. |
| Verified catalog | Done | Grantex has verified your catalog, prices and stock. |
| Verified catalog | To do | Grantex has not verified your catalog yet. Select Publish to try again. |

Grantex's signed facts for your prices and stock last only minutes. AgenticOrg renews them whenever a buyer's agent reads your shop, and each time you open this page, so **Done** means Grantex verifies your catalog now, not only when you turned the shop on.

Select **Publish** (or **Refresh listing** once your profile is published) to run the steps again at any
time: Grantex enrolment, your web address, publication and the signed catalog facts. Each row then shows
the exact reason if something still waits.

Your shop name is the short name buyers see in AI apps and in your Telegram link, such as `nilgiritea`. Use 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. It cannot change later, so choose it with care.

The network terms say that AgenticOrg lists your shop and opens checkouts for buyers who find it, and that you remain the seller and take payment yourself.

#### Your web address

Buyer agents read your shop's profile at `https://<your address>/.well-known/ucp`.

- **You already have an address.** If you connected your own domain in Custom Domains, or your profile is already published, the network uses it.
- **You have no address yet.** AgenticOrg gives you `<your-shop>.agenticorg.ai` and sets it up for you, certificate included. It usually goes live within an hour.

AgenticOrg can give out 20 of these addresses in all, and the page shows how many are in use. If they are taken, you can still turn on Sell everywhere and connect your own domain instead; see [Your own domain for buyer agents](/docs/oacp-custom-domains).

Your shop appears on the network only once its profile is published at that address and the address is live, certificate included. Buyer agents read your profile and search your catalog there, so a shop whose address is still being set up would only give them errors. While the profile is published but the address is still being set up, the AI apps and Telegram rows show **Waiting for your web address**. Before the profile is published, the AI apps row shows **Waiting for publication** and the Telegram row shows **Coming soon**. A new `agenticorg.ai` address usually takes a few minutes, and at most an hour.

#### Where buyers can find you

The page lists each surface and where it stands:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Live | Buyers can reach you there now. For Payments: you chose where buyers pay. |
| Waiting for DNS, Setting up, Issuing certificate | Your web address is being connected. Check back in a few minutes. |
| Waiting for your web address | You are on the network and your profile is published, but your web address is still being set up. AI apps and the Telegram bot offer your shop as soon as it is live. |
| Waiting for publication | You are on the network, but your profile is not published yet. |
| Coming soon | Telegram only: the shopping bot is not reachable for your shop yet, for example because your profile is not published. |
| Coming: registration in progress | AgenticOrg is still registering with that program. |
| Off | Sell everywhere is paused or not turned on. For Payments: you have not chosen where buyers pay. |

To see what buyers see in ChatGPT, follow [the ChatGPT run in the Nilgiri Tea House example](/docs/oacp-example-nilgiri-tea).

#### Pause or resume

Choose **Pause** on the page. New network checkouts are refused at once, and your shop leaves the directory: AI apps and the Telegram bot stop offering it within about two minutes, as their short-lived lists refresh. Your web address and your shop name stay yours. Choose **Resume Sell everywhere** to come back.

#### What stays with you

- **Payment.** AgenticOrg never takes the buyer's money. A buyer opens a checkout in the chat; when it is ready, the buyer gets a link to your own Shopify checkout or Plural payment page and pays you there. See [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid).
- **Your rules.** Every network checkout goes through the same checks as any other: your signed facts, your limits and the arbiter's fixed rules, recorded in your ledger.
- **Your data.** The directory shows your shop name, display name, categories, web address, profile address and Telegram link, nothing else.

Agents never pay on a buyer's behalf here. The AI apps and the Telegram bot have no tool that pays, and a
network Complete that carries a payment instrument, decision or mandate is refused.

#### Read next

- [Getting paid: buyers pay on your own page](/docs/oacp-getting-paid)
- [Merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup)
- [Your own domain for buyer agents](/docs/oacp-custom-domains)
- [Example: Nilgiri Tea House, end to end](/docs/oacp-example-nilgiri-tea)
- [Feature switches](/docs/oacp-feature-switches)


### Getting paid: buyers pay on your own page

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-getting-paid
Audience: Merchants and business owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-30.

In 30 seconds:

- When a buyer's checkout is ready, the buyer gets a link to your own payment page and pays you there.
- AgenticOrg never takes your buyers' money and never sees their card or UPI details.
- Shopify stores send buyers to their own Shopify cart. Stores with a Plural account send buyers to a Plural payment page.
- Plural payments become orders on the Orders page, and every administrator gets an email.
- You choose the method once, in the Payments step of Sell Everywhere, and can switch it off at any time.

#### Choose where buyers pay

Figure: The buyer pays on your page. When the checkout is ready, the arbiter checks your shop's facts and limits, then the buyer gets your payment link and pays you there. AgenticOrg never takes the money.

| Method | What the buyer sees | Where the order appears |
| --- | --- | --- |
| My Shopify checkout | A link to your store's own cart with the items already in it. They pay in your Shopify checkout. | Your Shopify admin, as with any other Shopify order |
| My Plural account | A link to a Plural payment page for your Plural account. They pay by card, UPI or net banking. | The Orders page here, with an email to your administrators |
| Off | No payment link. On the AgenticOrg network the buyer is told to pay with you directly. | Wherever you take the order |

The buyer always authenticates the payment themselves on that page, for example with 3-D Secure or their UPI PIN. Nothing is charged in the chat, and no agent pays on the buyer's behalf.

#### Set it up

```flow
Open Payments | On the Sell Everywhere page (/dashboard/sell-everywhere), choose your shop and go to step 5, Payments. It holds the Getting paid settings.
Shopify | Choose My Shopify checkout. Your Shopify store must already be connected in step 2; the page shows the store it will use.
Plural | Under Your Plural account, choose Sandbox or Production, enter your Plural client ID, client secret and webhook secret, and select Save Plural credentials. Then select Test, which only asks Plural for an access token.
Webhook | Copy the webhook URL the page shows into your Plural dashboard, or send it to Plural support if your account has no webhook setting, so payments are confirmed the moment they happen.
Save | Choose My Plural account or My Shopify checkout and select Save payment method. New checkouts use it at once.
```

My Plural account can be saved only once your Plural credentials, including the webhook secret, are saved. My Shopify checkout can be saved only once your Shopify store is connected.

Your Plural secrets are stored encrypted and are never shown again. To change one, enter your client ID again with the new value and save; leave a secret field blank to keep the saved one. Use Sandbox until a test payment has gone through, then switch to Production with your live credentials.

You do not need a payment method to turn on Sell everywhere, but until you save one, buyers get no payment link.

#### Before a link is issued

When the buyer asks to complete a ready checkout, the arbiter decides first, and the buyer gets a link only on an allow. It checks two things:

- **Your facts are still valid.** The catalog, price, stock and policy facts Grantex signed are fresh and not revoked.
- **The order is within your limits.** The largest single order, the currency, the most items per order and the daily maximum you set in step 4. The daily maximum counts, in that currency: the payments confirmed today (by the UTC day), the payment links still open whichever day they were issued, and every payment link issued today, even after it lapses or its checkout is canceled, because the buyer can still pay it. A link stops counting when its payment becomes an order (the order then counts as paid) or when Plural reports the payment failed. Shopify does not tell AgenticOrg when a buyer pays, so a Shopify link counts all the day it was issued.

No buyer mandate is asked for, because the agent holds no payment credential and the buyer pays on your page. The decision is used once and recorded in your ledger. A refusal names the rule that failed and its reason, for example `daily_amount_cap_exceeded`, and no link is issued.

#### What the buyer sees

1. The buyer asks for a product in ChatGPT or another AI app, in the AgenticOrg bot on Telegram, or on another agent platform, and opens a checkout.
2. When the checkout is ready, the buyer gets your payment link and the total.
3. They open the link and pay on your page. Asking again gives the same link while it is valid.
4. With Plural, they return to a short page that says whether the payment went through. If it did not, they ask for a new link.

A Plural link is valid for 30 minutes, or until the checkout expires if that is sooner: asking to complete the checkout again gives the same link while it is valid, or a fresh one after it lapses. A Shopify link stays the same for the life of the checkout. Once either link has been issued, the checkout's items cannot be changed, even after a Plural link lapses, because the buyer can still pay it; the buyer starts a new checkout to change the items. The one exception: once Plural reports that every link the checkout gave out failed, the checkout can be changed and completed again.

#### Your orders

Open **Orders** (`/dashboard/orders`) to see every order buyers paid for through a Plural link, newest first: the total, the items, where to deliver it, the buyer's contact details, the payment status and where they shopped (Telegram, an AI app, or another platform). Each order also sends the same details in an email to every active administrator of your workspace.

The delivery column shows how the buyer chose to receive the order: shipping with the delivery option they chose, or store pickup with the store. For shipping it also shows the address they gave their agent at checkout, line by line, with the recipient's name and phone when the buyer gave them. The shipping fee is shown once for the whole order, even when it ships to more than one place. The Plural payment page does not ask for an address, so ship to the one shown here. The address and contact details appear exactly as the buyer gave them; AgenticOrg does not check or correct them.

AgenticOrg creates an order only when Plural confirms the full amount, through its signed webhook or the check AgenticOrg runs every minute. If Plural reports a payment that does not match the checkout, for example a different amount, no order is created and the payment is logged so you can refund it in Plural. A payment that is only authorised, not captured, stays pending.

Orders paid in your Shopify checkout appear in your Shopify admin, not on the Orders page.

#### If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Connect your Shopify store first | Connect your store in step 2, then save My Shopify checkout again. |
| Save your Plural credentials first, or add your Plural webhook secret | Save the client ID, client secret and webhook secret, then save My Plural account again. |
| The buyer is told the shop's payment page is not set up | Save your Plural credentials, or connect your Shopify store, then save the payment method again. |
| The buyer is told payment links are not available here | Your platform operator has not set the public web address of the AgenticOrg service, which Plural links need. |
| The buyer is told the commerce arbiter refused | The order is over one of your limits, or a signed fact has lapsed. The message names the rule; the decision in your ledger gives the exact reason. |
| Test fails | Check the client ID and secret and that the environment matches them (Sandbox or Production). |
| Paid in Plural but no order here | Check the webhook URL in your Plural dashboard. Payments are also checked every minute, so the order appears shortly. |
| These items cannot be paid for in the shop's Shopify checkout | An item did not come from your Shopify store, is sold by a unit such as weight, or was ordered more than 9,999 at a time. Use My Plural account for these orders. |


### Your own domain for buyer agents

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-custom-domains
Audience: Merchants and platform operators. Reviewed: 2026-10-21.

In 30 seconds:

- Buyer agents can find your shop on a subdomain you own, such as agent.your-store.example, instead of an AgenticOrg address such as your-shop.agenticorg.ai.
- You add two DNS records. AgenticOrg checks them, tells you exactly what to fix, and connects the domain itself.
- Google issues the certificate, usually within the hour. You do not wait for anyone or share any account.
- Only the agent addresses are served on your domain; nothing else of AgenticOrg is reachable there.
- Your main domain (your-store.example) can answer too, through a pass-through rule. A redirect is not allowed there.

#### What you get

Your UCP profile is the file buyer agents read first. It says where your shop is and what it offers. With a custom domain it is served at `https://agent.your-store.example/.well-known/ucp`, together with your catalog and store locations under `/ucp`.

Figure: Your own domain, step by step. You add a subdomain and publish two DNS records. AgenticOrg checks them, connects the domain and follows the certificate until the domain is live.

**Do you need one?** Not to get started. When you turn on Sell everywhere and your shop has no address yet, AgenticOrg gives it `<your-shop>.agenticorg.ai` and sets it up for you, certificate included, with no DNS records on your side. Only 20 of these addresses can be given out in all. Connect your own subdomain when you want your own name, or when they are taken; the network then uses your domain. A shop holds one domain at a time, so a shop already on a platform address removes it here before adding its own. See [Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere).

You will use the **Custom Domains** page at `/dashboard/custom-domains`. You need the administrator role or the merchant role. Enter your merchant ID, and your seller agent ID if your shop has more than one, then press **Load**.

#### Before you start

- **A subdomain you control.** Use a name such as `agent.your-store.example` or `shop-agent.your-store.example`. It can be at most 64 characters long. Your main domain cannot be used directly, because a CNAME record is not allowed at the top of a domain. The [apex section](#your-main-domain) below shows how to make your main domain answer as well.
- **Access to your DNS provider**, to add two records.

#### Connect your domain

```flow start=1
Add the subdomain | On Custom Domains, type the subdomain and press Add domain. AgenticOrg shows the two records to publish, each with a copy button. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: "This name is the apex of its DNS zone" means you entered your main domain; use a subdomain.
Publish the CNAME record | At your DNS provider, point the subdomain at the address shown, which ends in .web.app. Keep it DNS only: switch off any proxy, CDN or CNAME flattening for this record. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Some providers add your domain to the end of the name for you; enter only the first part if so.
Publish the TXT record | Add the TXT record named _agenticorg-ucp.<your subdomain> with the value shown. It ties the subdomain to your AgenticOrg account, so nobody else can claim it. It has its own name, so it never clashes with the CNAME. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: Copy the value exactly; DNS changes can take up to an hour to be seen.
Verify records | Press Verify records. AgenticOrg checks both records and lists every problem with its fix. | Owner: Merchant | If blocked: See "If a check fails" below, fix the record and press Verify records again.
Connect the domain | AgenticOrg connects the domain by itself within a few minutes. Nobody needs to act. | Owner: AgenticOrg | If blocked: A connection problem shows "Needs attention" with the reason and a Retry button.
Certificate, then live | Google issues the certificate, usually within the hour and at most 24 hours. AgenticOrg checks every few minutes and marks the domain Live. | Owner: Google and AgenticOrg | If blocked: After 48 hours without a certificate the domain shows a failure; check that the CNAME is DNS only.
```

The progress bar on the page shows the same five stages: publish DNS records, verify ownership, connect domain, issue certificate, live. Each stage is marked done, current or failed.

Your profile is served on the domain once it is published. That means your signing key exists, you pressed publish, and Grantex allows public discovery for the host. If Sell everywhere is on, select **Publish** on the Sell Everywhere page once the domain is live: it creates a missing signing key, publishes your profile on the domain and shows the exact reason if anything still waits. See [Merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup), phase 3.

**If the page also asks for a Search Console owner,** your deployment still connects domains through Cloud Run domain mappings. In that case:
- The CNAME points at `ghs.googlehosted.com`.
- Google connects the domain only for an account that owns it in Search Console, so add the account shown on the page under Settings, Users and permissions, Verified owners, Add an owner, then tick the box on the page.
- Your platform operator then connects the domain with one command.

#### The records

| Type | Name | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CNAME` | `agent.your-store.example` | the address shown, ending in `.web.app.` | Sends traffic for the subdomain to AgenticOrg, and lets Google issue its certificate. |
| `TXT` | `_agenticorg-ucp.agent.your-store.example` | `agenticorg-ucp-verify=<code shown>` | Ties the subdomain to your AgenticOrg account. Keep it while the domain is connected. |

Two more rules keep the certificate working:

- **Keep the CNAME DNS only.** On Cloudflare that means the grey cloud. Also turn off **Always Use HTTPS** for it, so the certificate checks get through.
- **Check your CAA records.** If your domain has CAA records, they must allow the certificate authorities Google uses: `pki.goog` and `letsencrypt.org`.

#### If a check fails

| Message | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The TXT ownership record was not found | The TXT record is missing or holds another value | Publish the exact value shown and check again in a few minutes |
| No CNAME record was found | The subdomain has no CNAME, or a proxy hides it | Add the CNAME and set it to DNS only |
| The CNAME record points somewhere else | The found target is shown | Point it at the target on the page |
| DNS did not answer in time | A temporary lookup problem | Check again in a few minutes |
| Confirm that you added the mapping account | Only on deployments using domain mappings: the records are right but the Search Console box is not ticked | Add the owner, tick the box, check again |
| Already connected to another organization | Another AgenticOrg customer proved control of this host first | Remove it there first |
| Already connected to another merchant | Another merchant in your organization holds the host | Remove it there first |
| AgenticOrg could not connect the domain | The connection was refused; the reason is shown, for example that the domain is connected to another Firebase project | Fix the cause and press Retry |
| Google is issuing the certificate | Nothing is wrong; it takes up to 24 hours | Wait |

**Retry and check status.** The button on the page always does the right thing for the domain's current state. It verifies records, checks the certificate, or retries a failed domain. A failed domain keeps its subdomain reserved for you until you remove it.

**Change or remove.** To use a different subdomain, remove the current one first with the bin button. Removing it stops your profile being served there at once. AgenticOrg asks your platform operator to disconnect it, and that request stays in the operator queue until it is done.

#### Your main domain

Many agents look for `https://your-store.example/.well-known/ucp`. Keep your website where it is, and let your web server pass three paths through to your connected subdomain:

| Path | Match |
| --- | --- |
| `/.well-known/ucp` | exact |
| `/.well-known/ucp/` | everything under it (older UCP releases) |
| `/ucp/` | everything under it (catalog, locations, checkout) |

The rules for these paths:

- **Never redirect.** UCP does not allow a redirect for the profile, and agents will not follow one.
- **Send the request to the subdomain with `Host` set to the subdomain.** AgenticOrg recognises your shop by that name.
- **Keep the method, body and headers.**
- **Use HTTPS on your main domain.**

Agents that sign their requests should call the address your profile names, which is your subdomain. A signed request forwarded from your main domain no longer matches the name it was signed for.

On **Cloudflare**, use a Worker. Workers are available on every Cloudflare account; check Cloudflare's current request limits for yours. Bind it to the routes `your-store.example/.well-known/ucp*` and `your-store.example/ucp/*`:

```js
const AGENT_HOST = "agent.your-store.example";
export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    url.hostname = AGENT_HOST;
    return fetch(new Request(url, request), { redirect: "manual" });
  },
};
```

On **nginx**, add three locations to the server block for your main domain:

```nginx
resolver 1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8 valid=300s;
set $agent_host agent.your-store.example;
location = /.well-known/ucp { include snippets/ucp-pass.conf; }
location ^~ /.well-known/ucp/ { include snippets/ucp-pass.conf; }
location ^~ /ucp/ { include snippets/ucp-pass.conf; }
```

And the shared `snippets/ucp-pass.conf`:

```nginx
proxy_pass https://$agent_host;
proxy_set_header Host $agent_host;
proxy_ssl_server_name on;
proxy_ssl_name $agent_host;
proxy_ssl_verify on;
proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt;
proxy_redirect off;
```

Check it with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n" https://your-store.example/.well-known/ucp`. It must print `200` and no redirect address. The full guide is in the repository at `docs/oacp/merchant-apex-domain.md`.

#### For platform operators

### How domains reach AgenticOrg

The recommended setup puts a Firebase Hosting site in front of the API service:
- Each merchant subdomain is a custom domain on that site, which AgenticOrg creates and removes through the Firebase Hosting API.
- The site sends only the agent paths to the API: `/.well-known/ucp`, `/ucp/`, `/acp/` and the host check. Every other path on a merchant domain is a plain 404.
- Firebase passes the merchant's domain to the API in `X-Forwarded-Host`. AgenticOrg accepts it only for domains it connected itself, and only on those paths.

The older setup maps each domain to the API service with a Cloud Run domain mapping. Google then requires a Search Console owner and an operator command for every merchant.

### Turn it on

Firebase mode needs the `v6z91` and `v6z93` database migrations, which the normal deploy runs with `--with-migrations`. Then, once:

```flow start=1
Add Firebase to the project | Enable the Firebase and Firebase Hosting APIs and add Firebase to the Google Cloud project of the API service. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Adding Firebase needs the project owner's account.
Create the merchant domains site | Create one Firebase Hosting site, for example agenticorg-merchant-domains. Its address, <site>.web.app, is the CNAME target merchants publish. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Site ids are global; pick another if the name is taken.
Release the agent-only configuration | Run python scripts/release_merchant_domain_site.py --project <project> --site <site>. It sends the agent paths to the API and nothing else. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Run it with your own Google account signed in to gcloud.
Allow AgenticOrg to manage the site | Grant the API's service account the Firebase Hosting Admin role (roles/firebasehosting.admin) on the project. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Without it, every domain fails with a permission message.
Set the settings | Set the settings below on the API and worker services, then move traffic to the new revisions. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: The exact commands are in the repository at docs/oacp/merchant-custom-domains.md.
```

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAINS_ENABLED` | `true`. Off, the Custom Domains routes answer 404 and the status checks stop. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FIREBASE_ENABLED` | `true`, to connect new domains through Firebase Hosting. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FIREBASE_SITE` | The site id, for example `agenticorg-merchant-domains`. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_CLOUD_RUN_PROJECT` | The Google Cloud project, also the Firebase project. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_OPERATOR_TENANT_ID` | Your own AgenticOrg organization's id, for the operator queue. Your browser shows it at `/api/v1/auth/me` while you are signed in. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_OPERATOR_EMAIL` | The inbox for domains that need attention under the older setup. |

The deploy script adds to the existing settings rather than replacing them, so they survive later deploys.

### Work the queue

With Firebase Hosting, AgenticOrg connects and disconnects domains by itself. A Firebase domain appears in the **Operator queue** only when it fails, for example because the domain is connected to another Firebase project. It shows the reason and needs no command.

Domains on the older domain-mapping setup still need you:

```flow start=1
Connect a new domain | Copy the command from the queue item or the email and run it signed in as the mapping account. It looks like gcloud beta run domain-mappings create --service=agenticorg-api --domain=<host> --project=<project> --region=asia-southeast1. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: "Domain not verified" means the merchant has not added your account in Search Console; press Mark failed with that reason.
Mark it mapped | Press Mark mapped. AgenticOrg then watches for the certificate and marks the domain live by itself. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: If you forget, AgenticOrg still finds the live certificate on its next check.
Disconnect a removed domain | When a merchant removes a connected domain, a "Delete mapping" item appears. Run its gcloud beta run domain-mappings delete command, then press Mark deleted. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: If the item says another domain now uses the host, keep the mapping and press Mark done.
```

Every operator action is written to the merchant's commerce ledger with you as the actor.

### Platform addresses for Sell everywhere

Shops that turn on Sell everywhere without an address of their own get `<shop>.<apex>`, for example `tea-corner.agenticorg.ai`. AgenticOrg owns the apex, so the address is attested without a TXT record; it is created as a Firebase Hosting custom domain and followed to a live certificate like any other.

- It needs the Firebase setup above and one wildcard record in the apex's DNS zone: `*.<apex> CNAME <site>.web.app.`
- `AGENTICORG_PLATFORM_SUBDOMAIN_APEX` names the apex (`agenticorg.ai` by default).
- `AGENTICORG_PLATFORM_SUBDOMAIN_CAP` (20 by default) caps how many are given out, because Firebase connects at most 20 custom domains per domain. Past the cap, a shop can still turn on Sell everywhere and is asked to connect its own domain.

### Limits and when to change approach

**Firebase Hosting:**
- Each merchant domain can have at most 20 subdomains connected. The platform addresses all sit under one apex, so they share that limit.
- A request can take at most 60 seconds.
- Responses that do not set their own caching are marked not to be cached, so Firebase never serves a stale answer.
- Hosting meters storage and data transfer beyond its monthly allowance. The site stores no files, and agent responses are small.

**Cloud Run domain mappings** (older setup) are still a Google preview:
- Google warns of extra latency.
- A connected host reaches the whole API service.
- Google allows 50 certificates for each top domain in a week.

A load balancer with managed certificates would replace either setup when a paying merchant needs a service level or traffic must be filtered per host. It is not needed today. At list prices checked on 2026-10-21, it costs about $19 a month for 10 to 100 merchants and about $199 a month for 1,000.

### Turn it off

Set `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAINS_ENABLED=false`. The Custom Domains pages, routes and checks stop at once. Turning only `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FIREBASE_ENABLED` off sends new domains to the older setup, and makes domains already connected through Firebase answer 404 until it is on again. Remove those domains first if you are leaving Firebase for good.


### Safety and trust

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-safety-and-trust
Audience: Merchants, risk and audit teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-21.

In 30 seconds:

- Revoke a fact once and every channel stops using it. If the revocation list cannot be reached, everything refuses.
- The arbiter decides before money can move: your signed facts and your limits before a buyer gets a payment link, up to eight rules when an agent would pay itself. The first rule that fails is the reason, and it is recorded.
- Every decision is in the commerce ledger. You can export it and check it on your own computer, with no database and no network.
- Agent requests can carry a signature (Visa TAP or Web Bot Auth). AgenticOrg checks and logs them today; refusing unsigned calls is a separate switch.
- A refusal is never a mystery: it names the rule, the reason and how to fix it.

#### Revocation everywhere

Sometimes a fact must stop counting at once. A price was wrong. A product was recalled. A buyer withdrew consent.

With OACP you revoke it once. Grantex marks its slot on a public revocation list as invalid. Every place that relies on it checks that list.

Figure: One revoke, every channel. The merchant or operator revokes one fact. Grantex marks it invalid on the status list. AgenticOrg refuses the cached fact, the UCP profile stops offering what relied on it, the arbiter refuses new purchases, and revoking a mandate revokes the mandates built on it. If the list cannot be reached, everything refuses.

Good to know:

- AgenticOrg keeps a copy of the list only briefly: never longer than the list itself allows, and never more than 10 minutes.
- Revoking a mandate also revokes the mandates built on it.
- A revocation stops new decisions. It does not undo a payment that already ran.

#### What the arbiter checks

Every rule runs, in a fixed order. The first one that fails decides the refusal.

### Before a payment link

Today a buyer pays on your own Shopify checkout or Plural page. Before the buyer gets that link, the arbiter checks two rules:

| Rule | In plain words | Example refusal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Facts still valid | Your catalog, price, stock, policy and protocol facts are signed, fresh, unexpired and not revoked. | artifact_revoked:price |
| Merchant limits | The order is within your per-order amount, currency and items per order, and within your daily maximum. The daily maximum counts, in that currency: the payments confirmed today (by the UTC day), the payment links still open whichever day they were issued, and every payment link issued today, even after it lapses or its checkout is canceled, because the buyer can still pay it. A link stops counting when its payment becomes an order (the order then counts as paid) or when Plural reports the payment failed. Shopify does not tell AgenticOrg when a buyer pays, so a Shopify link counts all the day it was issued. | daily_amount_cap_exceeded |

Mandate, consent, spending cap, verified buyer authority and RBI AFA are not checked here. The agent holds no payment credential and moves no money, and the buyer authenticates on the payment page, for example with 3-D Secure or their UPI PIN. In production the allow still needs the Grantex countersignature, and it is used up before the link exists.

### When an agent would pay itself (switched off)

Agent-executed payment, where the payment provider charges against buyer mandates, is built but switched off. When it is on, the arbiter runs these eight rules before a checkout completes:

Figure: Eight rules, one answer. An agent-executed purchase passes eight gates in order: mandate, consent, spending cap, verified buyer authority, valid facts, merchant limits, not-present limits and RBI AFA. Passing all gives allow. The first failure gives refuse, with that rule as the reason.

| # | Rule | In plain words | Example refusal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Mandate present | There is a buyer mandate, and it has not expired. | mandate_expired |
| 2 | Consent active | The buyer's consent is still active. | consent_missing |
| 3 | Spending cap | The buyer's Commerce Passport allows this amount, in this currency. | passport_amount_cap_exceeded |
| 4 | Verified buyer authority | AgenticOrg verified the mandates itself. A claim in the request is not enough in production. | buyer_authority_caller_asserted |
| 5 | Facts still valid | Catalog, price, stock, policy and other facts are signed, fresh, unexpired and not revoked. | artifact_revoked:price |
| 6 | Merchant limits | The order is within your amount, currency and quantity limits, and your daily maximum when you set one. | order_amount_cap_exceeded |
| 7 | Not-present limits | If the buyer is away, your stricter limits and the Intent cap cover the order. | not_present_limits_missing |
| 8 | RBI AFA | A UPI AutoPay payment has verified AFA evidence when RBI rules need it. | afa_evidence_missing |

A refund has its own single rule: the refund must be positive, in the order's currency, and within what was captured.

#### Nobody waits for a person

The arbiter never answers "pending". It decides at once.

- An allow is single use, bound to the exact cart, and expires after 10 minutes.
- In production an allow is usable only with a Grantex countersignature. If that is missing, ask for a new decision.
- You can choose to copy refusals into your review queue. That copy never changes or delays the decision.
- An operator's note on a decision is only a note. It can never turn a refusal into an allow.

#### The ledger and offline checks

Every commerce write and every decision is recorded in the commerce ledger, in the same transaction as the change itself.

Figure: Check the record yourself. Export the ledger, run the verifier on your own computer, and read one of two answers: verified, or the first break, such as a missing, reordered, edited or truncated row.

```flow
Export | A tenant administrator downloads the ledger export from the ledger routes. | Owner: Tenant administrator | If blocked: Only administrators of that tenant can export.
Verify offline | Run python scripts/verify_ledger.py export.json. It uses no database and no network. | Owner: Anyone holding the file | If blocked: Exit code 2 means the file is not a readable export.
Read the answer | Exit code 0 means verified. Exit code 1 reports the first break, such as sequence_gap or link_hash. | Owner: Auditor or merchant | If blocked: Treat a break as an irregularity, re-export and compare.
```

Three honest details:

- Rows are signed with a platform secret (HMAC). The offline check verifies the chain links and the witnessed heads. It checks row signatures only when you supply the secret.
- Rows are chained only for tenants where audit-chain sealing is on. That switch starts off.
- To catch someone who rewrites the whole file, compare with a head kept outside it: a Grantex witness (its own switch, off by default) or a head you saved yourself with --expected-head.

#### Request signing: which agent is calling?

Agents can sign their HTTP requests (RFC 9421). AgenticOrg understands two public profiles:

- **Visa Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP):** browsing and payment tags, a short window and a one-time nonce.
- **Web Bot Auth:** the agent's key is found through its published signature agent.

Figure: Log mode and enforce mode. In log mode, the default, every request is answered and its signature status is logged. In enforce mode, unsigned or invalid requests to the commerce API get 401. Public pages are never refused in either mode.

| Mode | Unsigned or bad signature | Good signature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| log (default) | Answered, and the status is logged | Answered, logged, and recorded on write routes |
| enforce | Refused with 401 on the commerce API surfaces | Answered, logged, and recorded on write routes |

Enforce mode covers only the catalog and product JSON reads and the A2A routes. Your public pages, structured data, sitemap and llms.txt are never refused for a missing signature.

#### What a refusal looks like

A refusal always tells you what failed and why. Here is a shortened, synthetic example for a purchase over the buyer's cap:

```json
{
  "code": "arbiter_refused",
  "failing_rule": "passport_amount_cap",
  "reason": "passport_amount_cap_exceeded",
  "decision_id": "arbdec_5b0e1c7d2a9f",
  "action": "The commerce arbiter refused: passport_amount_cap (passport_amount_cap_exceeded).",
  "required_config": "buyer_authority.passport_ref, passport_max_amount_minor_units, passport_currency, passport_expires_at"
}
```

Read it like this:

1. **failing_rule** is the rule from the table above.
2. **reason** is the exact cause.
3. **decision_id** finds the sealed decision in the ledger.
4. **required_config** says what must change before a new attempt.

A refused payment link reads the same way, for example `failing_rule` `handoff_merchant_limits` with the reason `daily_amount_cap_exceeded`.

In a UCP or ACP checkout the decision comes back inside the checkout answer, as a business message. Nothing is charged, and no payment link is issued.

#### Related guides

- [Feature switches reference](/docs/oacp-feature-switches)
- [OACP FAQ](/docs/oacp-faq)
- Technical references: [arbiter and ledger](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/arbiter-ledger.md), [agent request signing](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/agent-request-signing.md) and [OACP troubleshooting](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/troubleshooting.md)


### Feature switches reference

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-feature-switches
Audience: Platform operators and merchants. Reviewed: 2026-10-21.

In 30 seconds:

- Every OACP surface that could expose your shop or move money starts switched off. Where buyers pay is each merchant's own choice, not a switch.
- The safety checks start switched on in production: signature checks, verified buyer authority and the Grantex countersignature.
- Request signatures start in log mode: checked and logged, never refused, until someone chooses enforce.
- Switches are settings on the AgenticOrg service. They are read at start-up, so a change needs a restart.
- Turn them on one at a time, in the order below, and write down how to turn each one back off first.

#### Three kinds of switch

Figure: Safe by default. Safety checks start on in production. Every surface that publishes or moves money starts off. Request signatures start in log mode and move to enforce only by choice.

"Strict runtimes" are production, staging, preview and any unknown environment name. Local, dev, development, test and ci are not strict.

#### Safety checks (on in production)

| Switch | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_OACP_VERIFY_STRICT` | On in strict runtimes; log-only elsewhere | Refuses to keep any fact whose signature, key, scope, expiry or revocation check fails. |
| `AGENTICORG_ARBITER_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_AUTHORITY` | On in strict runtimes | Refuses buyer authority that AgenticOrg did not verify itself (rule 4). |
