| `AGENTICORG_ARBITER_REQUIRE_GRANTEX_GRANT` | On in strict runtimes | An allow decision can be used only with a verified Grantex countersignature. |
| `AGENTICORG_ARBITER_GRANTEX_POST_ENABLED` | Follows the switch above | Sends each decision to Grantex for its countersignature. |
| `AGENTICORG_ROUTE_ENFORCEMENT_MODE` | `enforce` | A commerce write that skips its ledger row is answered as an error. `log` only logs it. |

Turning a safety check off weakens the shop's protection. Do it only as a recorded decision, for a short window.

#### Ledger extras (off by default)

| Switch | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_DEFAULT_ON` | Off | Links the ledger rows of every commerce tenant into a hash chain (the global `AGENTICORG_AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED` does it for all tenants). |
| `AGENTICORG_AUDIT_WITNESS_ENABLED` | Off | Sends each sealed chain head to Grantex, which countersigns it as an outside witness. |
| `AGENTICORG_OACP_RETENTION_APPLY_ENABLED` | Off | Lets the daily task delete review manifests whose stored retention decision has come due. |

#### Selling surfaces (off by default)

| Switch | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_UCP_PROFILE_ENABLED` | Off | Serves your UCP profile, catalog and store locations. Off, they answer 404. |
| `AGENTICORG_UCP_VERSIONS` | `2026-04-08` | Which UCP releases are served. Add `2026-08-25` when platforms read it. |
| `AGENTICORG_UCP_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_DAYS` | `7` (minimum 7) | How long a rotated-out signing key stays published. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAINS_ENABLED` | Off | Lets you connect your own subdomain (for example `agent.your-store.example`) for your UCP profile under Commerce > Custom Domains. Off, those pages and routes answer 404. See [Your own domain for buyer agents](/docs/oacp-custom-domains). |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FIREBASE_ENABLED` | Off | Connects new custom domains through a Firebase Hosting site: merchants publish two DNS records and AgenticOrg does the rest. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FIREBASE_SITE` | Empty | The Firebase Hosting site id; merchants point their CNAME at `<site>.web.app`. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_MAPPING_ACCOUNT` | Empty | The Google account that connects domains. Merchants add it as an owner in Search Console. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_OPERATOR_TENANT_ID` | Empty | Your own organization's id. Only its administrators see the operator queue. Empty, nobody does. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_OPERATOR_EMAIL` | Empty | Where each new operator queue item is emailed, with its command. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_CLOUD_RUN_PROJECT` | Empty | The project the queue's commands name. Region (`asia-southeast1`), service (`agenticorg-api`) and CNAME target (`ghs.googlehosted.com`) have their own settings with these defaults. |
| `AGENTICORG_CUSTOM_DOMAIN_CLOUD_RUN_AUTOMAP_ENABLED` | Off | Lets AgenticOrg connect and disconnect domains itself. Keep it off: Google names a very broad role for it. |
| `AGENTICORG_UCP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED` | Off | Serves UCP checkout, cart and order routes. Off, they answer 404. The network checkout gateway needs it too, and the once-a-minute Plural payment check runs only while UCP or ACP checkout is on. |
| `AGENTICORG_ACP_FEED_ENABLED` | Off | Lets you export the ACP product feed. |
| `AGENTICORG_ACP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED` | Off | Serves ACP checkout sessions (your shop must also opt in). |
| `AGENTICORG_ACP_SIGNATURE_MODE` | `log` | Keep `log`. ACP publishes no signing method yet, so `enforce` would refuse every request. |
| `OACP_PUBLIC_CATALOG_PLATFORM_DISABLED` | Unset | An operator override that withdraws the public catalog pages for every merchant. |

#### Sell everywhere network (off by default)

| Switch | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_ENABLED` | Off | Serves the network directory, the network checkout gateway and the Turn on Sell everywhere step. Off, they answer 404 and the page says Sell everywhere is not enabled; the setup steps before it still work. |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_SERVICE_TOKEN` | Empty | The credential the hosted MCP server presents to the network checkout gateway (at least 32 characters, from the secret manager). Empty, the gateway refuses every call. |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_AGENT_PROFILE` | `https://agenticorg.ai/ucp/platforms/agenticorg-network/profile.json` | The platform profile network checkouts are opened for. |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_TERMS_VERSION` | `2026-10-25` | The network terms version a merchant accepts when turning Sell everywhere on. |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_TELEGRAM_ENABLED` | Off | Serves the webhook of the public AgenticOrg shopping bot on Telegram. Off, it answers 404. |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME` | Empty | The bot's username, for each shop's `t.me/<bot>?start=<shop>` link. Empty, no Telegram link is shown. |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Empty | The bot's token and webhook secret, from the secret manager. |
| `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_TELEGRAM_CHAT_LIMIT_PER_HOUR`, `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_TELEGRAM_GLOBAL_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `20` and `60` | How many messages one chat may send in an hour, and the whole bot in a minute. |
| `AGENTICORG_PLATFORM_SUBDOMAIN_APEX` | `agenticorg.ai` | Shops without an address of their own get `<shop>.<apex>`. Needs custom domains through Firebase and one wildcard CNAME for the apex. |
| `AGENTICORG_PLATFORM_SUBDOMAIN_CAP` | `20` | How many platform addresses may be given out, Firebase's limit per domain. Past it, a shop is asked to connect its own domain. |
| `AGENTICORG_SHOPIFY_ENV_OPERATOR_TENANT_ID` | Empty | The only tenant that may read the deployment's own `SHOPIFY_*` store settings. Every other shop uses the token it stored itself. |

#### Payment links

The payment hand-off has no switch of its own: each merchant chooses where buyers pay on the Sell Everywhere page. It needs UCP or ACP checkout on and, for Plural, a public address:

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` | Empty | The public `https://` address of the AgenticOrg API. Plural payment links, the buyer's return page and the merchant's webhook URL are built on it, or on `AGENTICORG_APP_URL` when it is empty. Without either, Plural links are not offered. |

#### Agent-executed payment and mandates (off by default)

These switches belong to the path where AgenticOrg charges through a payment provider against buyer mandates. It stays off until a payment-provider sandbox run has passed. A merchant that chose where buyers pay keeps getting payment links whatever these say.

| Switch | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_MANDATES_ENABLED` | Off | A checkout Complete gets Intent, Cart and Payment mandates from Grantex and verifies them. |
| `AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_MANDATE_CAPABILITY_EVIDENCE_ENABLED` | Off | Sends your payment-capability check result to Grantex with the authority request. |
| `PLURAL_PINE_LIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED` | Off | Registers the Plural executor, so an allowed checkout or refund can actually charge or pay back. |
| `AGENTICORG_RBI_EMANDATE_AFA_LIMIT_MINOR_UNITS` | `1500000` (₹15,000) | Later UPI AutoPay debits above this need RBI AFA. |
| `AGENTICORG_RBI_EMANDATE_AFA_HIGHER_LIMIT_MINOR_UNITS` | `10000000` (₹1,00,000) | The higher limit for insurance, mutual fund and credit-card bill debits. |

#### Agent request signatures

| Switch | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_VERIFY_MODE` | `log` | `log` checks and logs signatures and refuses nothing. `enforce` answers 401 to unsigned calls on the commerce API. |
| `AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_AUTHORITIES` | Empty | The public host names a signature must cover. Set before `enforce`. |
| `AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_TAP_KEY_STORE_URLS` | Empty | Where Visa TAP keys are looked up. Empty means no TAP key is found. |
| `AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_SIGNATURE_AGENT_ORIGINS` | Empty | Which Web Bot Auth signature agents are trusted. |
| `AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_REGISTRY_LOOKUP_ENABLED` | Off | Records a verified agent's DID and scheme ids from the Grantex registry. |
| `AGENTICORG_HTTPSIG_SIGN_OUTBOUND` | Off | Makes AgenticOrg's own buyer agent sign its requests. |
| `AGENTICORG_A2A_SCHEME_AGENT_IDS` | Empty | AgenticOrg's own scheme agent ids, shown in its A2A agent card. |

#### MCP server and merchant settings

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP server `AGENTICORG_UCP_PROFILE_URL` and `AGENTICORG_UCP_AGENT_PROFILE` | Unset | Point an MCP install at your UCP profile. Unset, no checkout tools appear. |
| MCP server `MCP_NETWORK_DIRECTORY_URL` and `AGENTICORG_NETWORK_SERVICE_TOKEN` | Unset | Network mode: one hosted server serves every listed shop, with list, search, checkout and payment-link tools and no tool that pays. |
| Merchant `provider_policy.payments` | None | Where buyers pay: `shopify_cart` or `plural_hosted`, set in the Payments step of Sell Everywhere. None means no payment link. |
| Merchant `provider_policy.arbiter` | None | Your order limits: per order, per day, items per order and currency, set in the Order limits step. |
| Merchant `provider_policy.ucp.fulfillment.flat_rates` | None | Your flat shipping fee, for a shop without Shopify, set in the policies step. |
| Merchant `provider_policy.ucp.executor` | None | Names the payment executor for agent-executed payment. None means no charge. It is not used while `provider_policy.payments` is set. |
| Merchant `provider_policy.ucp.grantex_mandates` | None | Names your Grantex commerce tenant and merchant for mandates. |
| Merchant `provider_policy.acp.checkout_enabled` | False | Your opt-in to ACP checkout. |
| Merchant `provider_policy.arbiter.escalate_to_human` | False | Copies refusals into your review queue. It never changes or delays a decision. |

#### The order to turn things on

First run the release in staging with route enforcement and signatures in `log`, and UCP checkout and payments off. Then change one switch at a time, each followed by its smoke test.

```flow
Staging run | Route enforcement log, signatures log, UCP checkout off, payments off. Check the ledger has no missing rows. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Fix every missing ledger row before production.
Route enforcement | Keep enforce in production, the default. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Use log only for a short, recorded window.
Request signatures | Start in log. Move to enforce only when the expected callers show as verified and the owner records the decision. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Set log again; requests are answered again.
UCP profile and checkout | Turn on for a published merchant and run the UCP smoke test. Merchants that chose where buyers pay now get payment links. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Set false; routes answer 404 and stored sessions are kept.
Sell everywhere network | Set the service token on the API and the hosted MCP server, turn on the network, then the Telegram bot. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Set false; the directory and gateway answer 404 and listings are kept.
Grantex mandates | Turn on before agent-executed payments, merchant by merchant. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Set false; production refuses agent-executed decisions again.
Agent-executed payments | Only after the sandbox run passes, one merchant at a time. | Owner: Platform operator | If blocked: Unset and restart; checkout answers executor_unavailable.
```

The ACP feed and checkout, mandate-capability evidence, witnessing, retention and audit-chain sealing follow the same pattern, one at a time.

#### Turning something back off

Set the switch back and restart the service. For worker tasks (witness, retention, sealing), change the worker and scheduler too.

- Data already written is kept: decisions, ledger rows, sessions, orders and payment records.
- To stop one merchant only, use its merchant setting instead, for example set its payment method to Off or remove its executor.

The full table, with the exact turn-on condition and rollback for each switch, is in the [launch and rollback runbook](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/explainers/launch-rollback-runbook.md).

#### Related guides

- [Merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup)
- [Safety and trust](/docs/oacp-safety-and-trust)


### OACP FAQ

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/oacp-faq
Audience: Merchants. Reviewed: 2026-10-30.

In 30 seconds:

- Short answers to the questions sellers ask most about OACP.
- OACP is a trust layer under UCP, ACP and AP2. It feeds them and does not replace them.
- Your shop stays the source of truth. Grantex signs. AgenticOrg checks, decides and records. Buyers pay on your own payment page.
- Nothing that publishes your shop or moves money is on by default.
- For the full picture, start with the overview and the merchant setup checklist.

#### Who does what

Figure: Four roles, clear limits. Your shop owns the facts and orders. Grantex signs facts, runs the revocation list and issues mandates, and never moves money. AgenticOrg verifies, decides and records. The payment provider charges on your own payment page, and only after an allow decision.

#### Do I have to choose between UCP, ACP and OACP?

No. OACP sits underneath. It renders your facts into UCP and ACP, and maps mandates to AP2 field names. Buyer agents keep using the standard they already speak.

#### Is OACP certified or endorsed by the UCP, ACP or AP2 groups?

No. OACP is not a certification, and those groups have not endorsed it. It also does not establish regulatory compliance on its own.

#### What do I need to start?

A Shopify store, or a CSV or JSON file of your products, and the merchant or administrator role in AgenticOrg. Everything else is on one page, Sell Everywhere: your catalog, policies, order limits, where buyers pay and the switch. Turning it on enrols you with Grantex; your platform operator only connects the deployment to Grantex once. Follow [Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere) or the [merchant setup checklist](/docs/oacp-merchant-setup).

#### How do I get paid?

Buyers pay on your own page: your Shopify checkout, or a Plural payment page under your own Plural account. When a checkout is ready, the buyer gets the link, pays there and authenticates the payment themselves. AgenticOrg never holds the money. Plural payments show on the Orders page, with the delivery address the buyer gave, and in an email to your administrators; Shopify orders are in your Shopify admin. See [Getting paid](/docs/oacp-getting-paid).

#### Can an agent pay for the buyer without them?

Not today. Agent-executed payment with buyer mandates is built but switched off, so every purchase ends with the buyer paying on your page. No AI app or bot on the AgenticOrg network has a tool that pays.

#### Does every buyer question go through Grantex?

No. AgenticOrg answers questions from its own verified copy of your facts. Grantex takes part in purchases: it countersigns the decision, and on the agent-executed path it would also issue the mandates. It never moves money.

#### Can an agent buy something at the wrong price?

OACP is built to refuse it. A decision is bound to the exact cart, price and quantity. Change any of them and the decision no longer matches. Stale, expired or revoked prices are refused, and no payment link is issued.

#### Does a person at my shop approve each order?

No. The arbiter decides at once with fixed rules, including your order limits and daily maximum. You can copy refusals into a review queue, but that never changes or delays a decision.

#### What happens if Grantex is unreachable?

Plain questions can still be answered from facts that are still valid. In production, anything that commits money, including a new payment link, is refused until Grantex is back. If the revocation list cannot be read, facts are refused.

#### How do I stop selling a product to agents at once?

Revoke the fact that covers it. Grantex marks it invalid, and every channel stops using it. For one channel only, turn that channel's switch off. To leave the AgenticOrg network, pause Sell everywhere.

#### Does this work with UPI in India?

Yes. A buyer can pay by UPI on your Plural payment page and approves it with their UPI PIN there. Agents paying through UPI AutoPay mandates, with RBI AFA as the buyer's own step in their UPI app, is built but switched off: it has not yet run against the Plural sandbox.

#### What if the buyer is not present when the agent buys?

Today the buyer always pays on your page, so a payment needs the buyer. On the agent-executed path, which is off, there is no passkey step, your stricter not-present limits apply, and without them the purchase is refused.

#### Can I check the records myself?

Yes. Export the ledger and run `scripts/verify_ledger.py` on your own computer. It needs no database and no network. See [Safety and trust](/docs/oacp-safety-and-trust#the-ledger-and-offline-checks).

#### What is switched on today?

The safety checks are on in production. Every surface that publishes your shop starts off: the UCP profile and checkout, the ACP feed and checkout, and the AgenticOrg network. Once checkout is on and you have chosen where buyers pay, a ready checkout gives the buyer a link to your own payment page. Mandates and agent-executed payment stay off. See [feature switches](/docs/oacp-feature-switches).

#### Where can I read more?

- [What OACP is](/docs/oacp-overview) and [how it works](/docs/oacp-how-it-works)
- The blog post [OACP explained: one trust layer under UCP, ACP and AP2](https://agenticorg.ai/blog/oacp-one-trust-layer-under-ucp-acp-ap2)
- The technical [OACP runtime docs](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/oacp/README.md)


### BFSI: business onboarding and KYB review

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/bfsi-business-onboarding
Audience: Banks, NBFCs and fintech operations. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### Scenario and boundary

Example Bank wants analysts to spend less time assembling a business-onboarding file and more time reviewing exceptions. This playbook uses AgenticOrg's governed-case path for read-only investigation, cited memo preparation, screening proposals, deterministic policy evaluation and a human decision.

It does not automate account opening, sanctions clearance, loan approval or regulatory reporting. Provider availability, country coverage, bank policy and system-of-record integration are institution-specific. Use fictional businesses until the institution approves real data.

#### Prepare the pilot

Assign an onboarding owner, screening analyst, authorized approver, provider integration owner and platform/security owner. Configure the tenant-gated case runtime, one active shared agent per required case role, reviewed provider manifest/read tools, exact local purpose controls, Grantex grants and a reviewed policy. Configure the decision issuer and signed handoff destination separately.

The institution's application/LOS system submits cases through the reviewed API/workflow. The approvals console is for queue and review, not a universal business-intake form.

#### Process map

This map assigns each handoff in the configured case path. A missing source or
unresolved review is a stop, not an implied clearance.

```flow
Application | A fictional business submits details through the bank's approved intake. | Owner: Bank intake team | If blocked: Incomplete intake stays with the bank; no case outcome is inferred.
Investigation | Configured agents read approved registry, ownership and screening sources. | Owner: Configured case agents | If blocked: Missing grant, provider error or absent record remains missing evidence, not a clear result.
Memo and policy | The case shows cited findings, missing items and the reviewed policy tier. | Owner: AgenticOrg case runtime | If blocked: Unsupported citations or incomplete evidence require investigation before decision.
Screening review | The analyst checks each proposed disposition against the cited record. | Owner: Screening analyst | Human decision: Accept the proposal or override it with a written reason. | If blocked: An unresolved hit stays open for human review; the proposal does not clear it.
Decision request | The exact case version and action go to the configured approval issuer. | Owner: Authorized case operator and approval issuer | Human decision: A designated approver decides on the issuer page; a distinct second approver participates where required. | If blocked: Missing, expired or superseded approval cannot record a decision; request a new decision on the current case.
Bank handoff | The signed outcome is delivered for the bank system to interpret and act on. | Owner: Bank system-of-record team | If blocked: Delivery failure or duplicate evidence needs reconciliation; do not infer account opening.
```

#### Follow one fictional application

1. Open **Approvals > governed cases** at `/dashboard/approvals/cases`.
2. Find the fictional case and inspect investigation state.
3. Read identity, registry, ownership, screening, activity and missing evidence.
4. Open retained source passages where available; confirm provider record and retrieval time.
5. Inspect policy ID/version and fired rules. Do not treat missing evidence as passing.
6. Review screening proposals. Override only with a documented reason; the agent's proposal does not clear the hit.
7. Request a decision for the current case. The named approver authenticates on the issuer's page, including distinct second approval where required.
8. Record the verified decision and inspect signed handoff delivery. Confirm what the bank system did with it.

#### What a successful trial proves

It proves the configured evidence/review/decision/handoff path for that test. It does not prove universal registry coverage, calibrated model accuracy, case-bound pooled grants or regulatory approval. The rollout review must keep visible that AgenticOrg's Grantex SDK call passes no case id or purpose, so token-level case purpose and per-case caps are not checked on that path.

#### Negative cases to demonstrate

Try a unavailable provider capability, unresolved screening hit, missing grant, cross-company request, machine-credential human decision, changed memo after approval request and duplicate handoff. Expected outcomes are visible missing evidence/refusals or safe idempotent handling, never a manufactured approval.

#### Measure adoption

Compare manual file-assembly time, missing-information rate, analyst overrides, re-investigation, review age and delivery failures on a reviewed sample. Track reopening causes. Do not publish a numerical accuracy claim from a few happy-path examples.

Next: [Capability status and gaps](/docs/bfsi-capability-status), [Governed cases](/docs/governed-cases), [Approvals](/docs/approvals), [Adoption checklist](/docs/adoption-checklist).


### BFSI: reconciliation and finance exceptions

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/bfsi-reconciliation
Audience: Finance and treasury operations. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### Scenario and boundary

Example Bank's finance team wants a daily exception pack comparing a reviewed ledger export with bank/settlement statements. AgenticOrg assists with evidence extraction, comparison, break classification and a reviewable summary. Posting entries, releasing money and certifying balances remain the finance team's authorized process.

This is a configurable reference workflow, not a universally pre-integrated bank reconciliation product. The actual ledger/bank connector contract, matching logic and accounting policy must be implemented/reviewed for the institution.

#### Prepare the sources

Use synthetic CSV/XLSX statements with transaction reference, date, amount, currency and relevant account mapping. Define timezone, date boundaries, sign conventions, duplicates and tolerances. Avoid real account numbers in training examples.

Upload the reconciliation procedure to Knowledge Base and verify search. Configure read-only exports/connectors with the correct company binding. Make sure the agent's selected tools actually read the required data; a finance template alone does not do so.

#### Configure and run

For a small reproducible exercise, prepare these two **synthetic** datasets
using the schema expected by your reviewed read tool. Do not infer that uploading
CSV to Knowledge Base automatically connects the reconciliation agent to it.

```csv
source,reference,date,amount,currency
bank,DEMO-001,2026-09-28,1000.00,INR
bank,DEMO-002,2026-09-28,2500.00,INR
bank,DEMO-003,2026-09-28,750.00,INR
```

```csv
source,reference,date,amount,currency
ledger,DEMO-001,2026-09-28,1000.00,INR
ledger,DEMO-002,2026-09-28,2400.00,INR
ledger,DEMO-004,2026-09-28,500.00,INR
```

The reviewed expected result is one exact match (`DEMO-001`), an INR 100
amount difference (`DEMO-002`), one bank-only entry (`DEMO-003`) and one
ledger-only entry (`DEMO-004`). Bank total is INR 4,250; ledger total is INR
3,900. These figures are teaching assertions, not reconciled customer balances.
Require source-row references and validated calculations in the exception pack.

1. Review the available reconciliation agent or create a bounded finance candidate.
2. Specify output: matched items, unmatched items, reason, evidence reference and proposed follow-up.
3. For exact financial totals, require deterministic calculations/validated tool results; do not ask an LLM to invent or approximate amounts.
4. Build a manual workflow: read sources, validate schema, compare, prepare exception pack, human review.
5. Run a synthetic day with known expected matches and deliberate breaks.
6. Inspect source freshness, totals, duplicate handling and every exception.
7. Hand approved corrections to the accounting system through a separately authorized process.

#### Process map

The comparison below assumes a reviewed read tool, mappings and deterministic
calculation. It does not imply an automatic ledger posting connector.

```flow
Read-only sources | Collect reviewed statement and ledger exports for one business period. | Owner: Finance data owner and approved read tool | If blocked: A late, partial or inaccessible source makes the period incomplete.
Validate and compare | Apply reviewed schema, currency, duplicate and matching rules with validated calculations. | Owner: Configured comparison and finance operator | If blocked: Corrupt rows, mismatched currencies or totals become exceptions, not forced matches.
Exception pack | List matched pairs and each break with source-row evidence and proposed follow-up. | Owner: Finance assistant | If blocked: Missing provenance or uncertain arithmetic must be checked before review.
Finance review | Recheck ambiguous matches and proposed corrections against the source records. | Owner: Authorized finance reviewer | Human decision: Approve, revise or reject each proposed correction through the institution's controls. | If blocked: Unresolved breaks remain open and cannot be reported as balanced.
Authoritative posting | Send approved corrections through a separately authorized accounting process. | Owner: Institution finance and accounting system | If blocked: A prepared pack is neither a posted entry nor a verified balance.
```

#### Sample acceptance cases

| Input | Expected evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Same reference and amount | A documented matched pair |
| Missing ledger item | Unmatched source entry, not a guessed posting |
| Same amount in different currencies | No unsupported cross-currency match |
| Duplicate reference | Explicit duplicate exception |
| Corrupt/partial source | Failed validation or incomplete evidence, not balanced totals |

#### Scheduling and operations

Schedule only after a manual run is reproducible. Confirm timezone, statement arrival, worker availability, rate limits and retry/idempotency. A late source must not be represented as a complete daily reconciliation.

Measure correctly identified breaks, false matches, review effort, source delays and reopened corrections. Compare against an independently reviewed ledger sample. Retest mappings after upstream changes.

Next: [Capability status and gaps](/docs/bfsi-capability-status), [Connectors](/docs/connectors), [Workflows](/docs/workflows), [Audit and monitoring](/docs/audit-and-monitoring).


### BFSI: customer service across chat and voice

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/bfsi-customer-service
Audience: Contact-center and service teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### Scenario and boundary

Example Bank wants a service assistant that explains approved procedures, triages complaints and prepares staff responses through chat and configured voice. Start with general information and synthetic cases. Do not expose account details or perform account/card/payment actions without the bank's approved authentication and integration path.

A phone number, claimed name or free-text account identifier is not identity verification. AgenticOrg's voice/runtime controls do not themselves establish bank-customer authentication.

#### Prepare a reviewed knowledge set

Upload current product FAQs, branch directory, complaint procedure and escalation policy. Assign effective dates and an owner. Search known answers and confirm citations. Remove or clearly supersede conflicting old procedures. Do not load unapproved financial advice as an operational policy.

#### Build the service agent

Use a reviewed support-triage candidate or custom operations agent. Define categories, urgency, response-draft structure and escalation. Grant read-only knowledge/approved ticket tools first. Explicitly refuse PIN/OTP collection, balance invention, account changes and payment instructions outside the authorized bank workflow.

1. Run a general question through the agent detail/chat path.
2. Test a complaint with missing information.
3. Test a suspected fraud/card-loss scenario requiring urgent human routing.
4. Ask for a private account balance and confirm refusal/referral.
5. Verify any configured ticket write/email action separately before enabling it.

#### Process map

This is a response-preparation path. The bank's authenticated channel and staff
remain responsible for private account servicing and final communication.

```flow
Question or complaint | Receive the request through a configured general-information or authenticated channel. | Owner: Bank channel owner | If blocked: A claimed name or phone number alone does not establish customer identity.
Knowledge check | Retrieve the current approved procedure and inspect its cited source. | Owner: Service agent and knowledge owner | If blocked: Missing, conflicting or outdated guidance goes to staff; do not invent an answer.
Response draft | Prepare a bounded answer or complaint summary from supported facts. | Owner: Service agent | If blocked: Private account data or an unsupported action is refused or referred to the bank's authorized path.
Human escalation | Review sensitive, urgent or unresolved requests before any staff response. | Owner: Authorized service staff | Human decision: Staff decide whether to send, revise or escalate the prepared response. | If blocked: Suspected fraud or a failed voice/ticket path follows the bank's urgent human process.
Confirmed outcome | Record communication and resolution in the bank's approved system. | Owner: Bank service team and system of record | If blocked: A prepared draft is not a sent message or completed account action.
```

#### Add voice only after chat is correct

Configure signed Twilio calls using [Voice setup](/docs/voice). Test with an approved number/window. Check speech recognition, spoken clarity, interruption/silence, safe failure wording and actual provider status. A passing text simulation does not prove acoustic or telephone quality.

Document provider recording/retention and customer-facing disclosures under the institution's process. AgenticOrg's call-history masking does not control the provider's own storage settings.

#### What to measure

Track correct routing, unsupported-answer rate, unresolved questions, escalation time, call failures and human overrides. Validate different accents/languages and noisy conditions where they are in scope. Do not claim a language is ready merely because it appears in a selector.

Roll out a narrow task population before sensitive account servicing. Re-test whenever the bank procedure, provider number/callback, model or ticketing contract changes.

Next: [Capability status and gaps](/docs/bfsi-capability-status), [Run and chat](/docs/run-and-chat), [Knowledge and OCR](/docs/knowledge-and-ocr), [Approvals](/docs/approvals).


### BFSI: insurance document and claims assistance

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/bfsi-insurance
Audience: Insurers and claims operations. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### Scenario and boundary

Example Insurer needs help preparing claim files for manual review. An assistant can extract document text, compare it with an approved checklist, summarize missing items and prepare reviewer notes. It must not decide coverage, reject a claim, determine liability or release a payout.

This is a configurable document/workflow example, not a shipped universal claims-system adapter. The insurer owns the policy wording, adjudication rules, data permissions and integration.

#### Prepare the exercise

Use a fictional claim, synthetic identity/receipt documents and a reviewed sample checklist. Keep medical or real customer data out of initial testing. Upload the checklist and policy reference to Knowledge Base; verify retrieval against known clauses and effective dates.

For scans, use supported PDF/image formats and inspect extraction method, OCR confidence and page provenance. Manually verify dates, policy numbers, currency, totals and negatives. A confidence value is not permission to accept an amount.

#### Configure the assistant

Create a custom operations/document-review agent with output fields for document type, cited facts, missing items, unreadable fields and reviewer questions. Require it to quote/cite only available evidence and explicitly mark uncertainty. Limit tools to approved reads during the first pilot.

#### Process map

The map stops at reviewer preparation. Coverage, liability and payout stay with
the insurer's authorized process.

```flow
Approved claim file | Authorized intake supplies synthetic file references and the current checklist. | Owner: Insurer intake team | If blocked: Missing documents stay on the request list; no completeness claim is made.
Extraction check | Native parsing or OCR supplies page-linked text for inspection. | Owner: Document-review operator | If blocked: Unreadable dates, amounts or identifiers are flagged for manual verification, never guessed.
Checklist comparison | The assistant prepares cited present, missing and uncertain items. | Owner: Configured document-review agent | If blocked: Conflicting policy versions or absent sources go to the checklist owner.
Claims review | Staff compare the prepared notes with source documents and insurer policy. | Owner: Authorized claims reviewer | Human decision: The reviewer requests more evidence or makes the insurer's coverage determination outside the assistant. | If blocked: Ambiguous or incomplete evidence remains in review; no rejection or payout is automated.
System handoff | The claims platform records the insurer's own authorized outcome. | Owner: Insurer claims-system team | If blocked: A prepared note is not a customer notification, coverage decision or paid claim.
```

#### Run a complete test

Give the fictional file reference `DEMO-CLAIM-001` a checklist that requires an
application, receipt and incident statement. Supply only the first two documents.
The expected reviewer output should contain:

```text
File: DEMO-CLAIM-001
Application: present, with source/page reference
Receipt: present, with source/page reference; amount needs manual verification
Incident statement: missing
Next step: ask the authorized claims team to obtain the missing statement
Coverage decision: not made
Payout: not initiated
```

This is an expected-result example, not an API schema. Match it to your configured
workflow's actual fields and compare its sources against the original file.

1. Submit a complete synthetic file and compare findings against a human checklist.
2. Remove one required document and verify the assistant requests it.
3. Use a blurry amount/date and confirm it is unreadable, not guessed.
4. Provide conflicting policy versions and confirm escalation.
5. Ask the agent to approve or pay the claim and confirm refusal.
6. Inspect run history, sources and reviewer handoff.

If a claims-platform write or customer notification is needed, build/approve that connector contract separately. A prepared missing-document list is not proof that a message was sent.

#### Operate the process

Assign a checklist owner, claims reviewer, data/privacy owner and integration owner. Define retention for uploaded files, extracted text, run evidence and provider copies. Track document-quality failures, missing-item accuracy, review effort and reopened files rather than a single generalized "AI accuracy" number.

Next: [Capability status and gaps](/docs/bfsi-capability-status), [Knowledge and OCR](/docs/knowledge-and-ocr), [Workflows](/docs/workflows), [Security and data](/docs/security-and-data).


### BFSI: merchant enablement and agentic commerce

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/bfsi-merchant-services
Audience: Acquiring banks and merchant-service teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### Scenario and ownership

This is a reference example for an acquiring bank's merchant-enablement pilot,
not an already integrated banking product or a claim of live payment execution.

In this synthetic example, an acquiring bank wants to help a fictional Shopify
merchant become usable by agentic buyer interfaces. The bank can offer an
institution-managed or reviewed hosted AgenticOrg workspace, but
merchant/provider/platform contracts still determine actual availability.

AgenticOrg owns seller/buyer runtime. Grantex owns trust/policy/canonical artifacts. Shopify owns merchant catalog/inventory/order truth. The bank/fintech/provider owns payment/mandate execution and customer authorization. OACP is not a reason to make Grantex the engine for every buyer message.

#### Build one synthetic merchant path

1. Assign a merchant owner, bank integration owner, provider contact and channel owner.
2. Configure merchant-scoped Seller Commerce Agent onboarding and source/channel settings.
3. Obtain read-only access to a sandbox Shopify store with a fictional catalog through the merchant's approved process, or prepare a CSV or JSON file of fictional products to upload on the Sell Everywhere page.
4. Sync synthetic products/variants/images/price/inventory and compare samples with the sandbox store.
5. Send the bounded Grantex authority request and verify/cache issued artifacts.
6. Ask product questions about the fictional catalog through the configured web or agent bridge.
7. Inspect source, freshness, supported facts and refusal behavior.
8. Prepare a provider/POS handoff and confirm that no order/payment state is fabricated.
9. If the pilot includes payment, have the merchant choose its own Plural account in Sandbox on the Sell Everywhere page, and confirm a ready checkout returns a link to that payment page and a paid sandbox order appears on the Orders page.

#### Process map

This is a bank-led reference pilot with configured merchant, channel and
provider paths. A prepared handoff is never a completed transaction.

```flow
Bank and merchant setup | Agree identities, read scopes, provider contract and publishing state. | Owner: Bank integration owner and merchant owner | Human decision: Owners approve the pilot scope and any channel publication under their own processes. | If blocked: Unapproved access or publishing state keeps the channel off.
Merchant-source evidence | Read-only sync supplies product, price and inventory snapshots for sample checks. | Owner: Merchant source owner and configured AgenticOrg sync | If blocked: Missing scopes or stale source facts stop unsupported buyer promises.
Trust artifacts | The bounded authority request and cache retain scope, source and freshness. | Owner: Grantex authority and AgenticOrg runtime | If blocked: Invalid or stale artifacts cannot support commitment-bound requests.
Buyer channel | A configured bridge answers from supported merchant artifacts. | Owner: Channel owner and AgenticOrg buyer runtime | If blocked: Unsupported channels or facts are refused until the integration is approved.
Provider capability | A configured provider path checks non-sensitive capability evidence. | Owner: Bank/provider integration team | Human decision: The customer and provider complete any required authorization outside this map. | If blocked: Capability evidence alone does not prove a mandate or payment.
Authoritative handoff | A prepared packet awaits provider, POS or merchant confirmation. | Owner: Provider, POS or merchant system | If blocked: Absent or failed confirmation stays pending or failed; no paid or placed state is fabricated.
```

#### Plural payments and mandates

Arrange the provider onboarding contact, merchant account, sandbox/live access, allowed capability contract and human authorization journey. AgenticOrg can verify provider-owned capability evidence directly through its configured path. Store non-sensitive references, not raw mandate/payment credentials.

**What runs today: the payment hand-off.** A merchant saves its own Plural client ID, client secret and webhook secret (Sandbox or Production), which AgenticOrg encrypts and never shows again. When a buyer's checkout is ready and the arbiter allows it, the buyer gets a link to a Plural hosted payment page under the merchant's own account, pays there and authenticates the payment, for example with 3-D Secure or a UPI PIN. AgenticOrg never holds the money. A payment confirmed for the right amount, by Plural's signed webhook or the once-a-minute status check, becomes an order with an email to the merchant's administrators; any other payment is refused and logged so the merchant can refund it. Settlement, refunds and disputes stay with the merchant's Plural account.

A credential/token capability check is not proof of a completed mandate or an allowed payment in every geography. Agent-executed payment, where AgenticOrg charges against buyer mandates, needs the provider's real contract, authorization, settlement/error/refund handling and institution approval. It stays switched off; for mandates the OACP runtime remains prepared/non-executing.

#### Channels and protocol payloads

UCP/ACP/schema.org/AP2/A2A/MCP-style payloads and bridges are not automatic marketplace placement. Agree each target's supported contract, authentication, publication/approval requirements and actual customer journey. WhatsApp/Telegram need configured credentials and channel rollout; ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/Perplexity need appropriate client/platform setup.

A merchant that turns on Sell everywhere is listed in AgenticOrg's own network once its profile is published: buyers reach it from ChatGPT and other MCP apps through the AgenticOrg MCP server, from the AgenticOrg shopping bot on Telegram, and on the open web through its UCP profile. Google, Microsoft Copilot and Perplexity are shown as registration pending. See [Sell everywhere](/docs/oacp-sell-everywhere).

#### Physical-store POS

An offline POS bridge prepares a store-linked handoff and reconciles authoritative provider/POS confirmation. It must preserve merchant/store context, expiry, source, reference and duplicate handling. Do not call a paid receipt successful because an agent displayed a prepared packet.

#### Pilot success criteria

Verify accurate catalog facts, stale-source refusal, cross-merchant isolation, invalid webhook rejection, channel authentication and non-fabricated transaction state. Keep public discovery off until the publishing path is approved and validated. Measure the complete buyer journey rather than counting adapter names.

Next: [Capability status and gaps](/docs/bfsi-capability-status), [Commerce guide](/docs/commerce), [API and agent clients](/docs/api-sdk-mcp), [Team adoption](/docs/adoption-checklist).


### BFSI capability status and open work

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/bfsi-capability-status
Audience: BFSI sponsors, operators and integration owners. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### What this status means

AgenticOrg can be configured for evidence-led BFSI workflows, but a process map
is not proof that a bank's systems, providers, controls or staff are connected.
The current repository assessment has **150 functional capabilities**: **24
covered, 97 partial and 29 gaps**. A covered component may still need a
tenant setting, approved provider, external system or human reviewer. No full
BFSI journey has end-to-end acceptance on the strength of these counts alone.

Services built behind default-off settings after this baseline was last refreshed
are not yet reflected in these counts; where the table below names one, it is
marked (built, off by default). They are document processing, speech and call
intelligence, transaction intelligence, conversational services and the
supervisor view, workbenches, lineage, content services, personalisation, the
agent registry, model cards, and FinOps thresholds and forecast. Each is
unavailable until its setting is turned on; see
[feature switches that ship off](/docs/self-hosting#feature-switches-that-ship-off)
and [the six screens that ship switched off](/docs/review-and-operations-screens).
The Banking Pack can be installed without a setting, but it is not counted
either.

This page describes functional software coverage, not infrastructure location,
regulatory approval, certification or permission to process customer data. A
feature behind a disabled flag is unavailable in the default installation.

#### Where the work stands

| Area | Working foundation | Still needs implementation, enabling or validation |
|---|---|---|
| Agent governance | Agent execution, scoped grants, human review and case evidence paths | Registry-grade discoverability, dependency mapping and model cards (built, off by default) and cross-service lifecycle proof |
| Knowledge and documents | Ingestion, OCR and source-aware answers on configured paths | Mixed bundles, page-region review and document comparison (built, off by default), hybrid-ranking rollout (off by default) and cited refusal across every tenant path |
| Conversation and speech | Web chat and configured voice runtime | Banking intents, speaker separation, spoken sensitive-data redaction and supervised takeover (built, off by default), and channel parity |
| Transactions and commerce | Read-only source evidence and prepared agent handoffs | Human disposition of transaction findings (built, off by default), bank-owned source connections, provider-owned execution and reconciliation evidence |
| Operations | Logging, approval controls and evaluation hooks | Budget thresholds and synthetic checks (built, off by default), complete trace coverage, measured SLOs, rollback and production-grade recovery |

The detailed [functional assessment](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/bfsi/functional-coverage.md)
and [capability matrix](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/bfsi/coverage-matrix.md)
identify individual gaps. The [product status](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/PRODUCT_STATUS.md)
records other release boundaries. These files describe the current repository
assessment; verify your deployed version and configuration separately.

#### What to prove in a pilot

1. Select one narrow use case and name its business owner, system-of-record
   owner, integration owner, reviewer and support owner.
2. Use fictional or institution-approved data. Connect each required system
   through its reviewed API or file contract; a diagram is not a connector.
3. Run normal, missing, stale, conflicting, unauthorized and cross-company
   cases. Inspect citations, grants, reviewer decisions and external receipts.
4. Demonstrate restart, replay, revocation, duplicate events and recovery with
   the same users and roles that will operate the pilot.
5. Confirm what the external system actually did. An agent draft, signed
   handoff or payment-capability reference is not an account change, payment,
   settlement or regulatory filing.

For a concrete teaching path, open the [business onboarding](/docs/bfsi-business-onboarding),
[reconciliation](/docs/bfsi-reconciliation), [customer service](/docs/bfsi-customer-service),
[insurance](/docs/bfsi-insurance) or [merchant services](/docs/bfsi-merchant-services)
playbook. Each is a fictional, configured example and carries its own blocked
paths and human ownership.


### Team adoption and launch checklist

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/adoption-checklist
Audience: Sponsors and rollout leads. Reviewed: 2026-10-02.

#### Choose the first useful problem

Select one repeatable task with a measurable outcome, manageable data and a human owner. Good first tasks include procedure Q&A, document completeness review, reconciliation exception preparation and complaint triage. Avoid a first rollout that simultaneously requires new voice, payments, core banking and marketplace integrations.

This is a rollout checklist, not an instruction to remain in an endless audit phase. Build the actual authorized path, test it with representative evidence and train the people who will use it.

#### Assign accountable owners

| Owner | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Business sponsor | Outcome, budget and scope |
| Process owner | Current procedure, expected output and exceptions |
| Administrator | Workspace, roles, models and configuration |
| Integration owner | Provider contract, credentials, tool behavior and recovery |
| Reviewer | Human approvals, coverage and escalation |
| Security/data owner | Permitted information, retention and incident handling |
| Operator/support owner | Daily monitoring, user help and rollback |

#### Before inviting the team

1. Complete [Your first agent](/docs/first-agent) with synthetic data.
2. Verify every required knowledge/model/connector path separately.
3. Test normal, missing, conflicting, stale and forbidden requests.
4. Confirm a non-admin operator can reproduce the exact task.
5. Confirm the reviewer can find evidence and make only authorized decisions.
6. Inspect external system confirmations separately from prepared outputs.
7. Document failure recovery, support contact and a pause/rollback trigger.

#### Training session

Walk users through sign-in, company selection, task input, source inspection, run status and escalation. Show one successful task and one intentional refusal. Train reviewers to check evidence, not trust fluent wording. Let each user reproduce the path with their own role.

Use the BFSI playbooks as teaching examples, then replace fictional inputs and procedures only after the institution approves real data and integrations. Bank-specific connectivity and regulated authority must remain explicit.

#### Follow one complete pilot

```flow
Choose the task | Pick document Q&A, invoice review, a service case or a seller catalogue question. Record the current process and expected answer. | Owner: Business sponsor | If blocked: Do not begin with an unbounded promise to automate everything.
Connect approved sources | Upload reviewed knowledge and configure the model and required read-only tools using your own provider credentials. | Owner: Administrator and integration owner | If blocked: Missing credentials or unsupported tools are configuration gaps, not successful integrations.
Run and inspect | Send a representative request, inspect citations and task status, and repeat with missing, stale and conflicting inputs. | Owner: Process owner | If blocked: An unsupported answer or partial run is reviewed, not described as completed work.
Review the handoff | Check the prepared output and any required human approval. Verify external writes or messages in their owning system. | Owner: Authorized reviewer | Human decision: Approve only the scoped action supported by evidence. | If blocked: A draft, catalogue artifact or approval packet is not a posted invoice, completed order or executed payment.
Measure and expand | Compare the same cases against the baseline, train users and add the next authorized capability only when its dependency works. | Owner: Sponsor and support owner | If blocked: Pause on unacceptable error, cost, latency or reopened cases; retain a recovery path.
```

For banks, use [Customer service](/docs/bfsi-customer-service) and
[Capability status](/docs/bfsi-capability-status). For fintech/platform teams,
use [API, SDK and MCP](/docs/api-sdk-mcp). For merchants, follow the
[External buyer journey](/docs/seller-a2a-commerce-journey).

#### Operating across countries

Agree on data location, retention, access, supported language, provider coverage,
currency and applicable approval requirements for the actual deployment. A
deployment option or provider connector does not establish residency, regulatory
approval or support in every jurisdiction. Start with approved samples; never put
customer records, API keys or passwords in a public demo enquiry.

Discuss a specific pilot at [sanjeev@orchestrum.in](mailto:sanjeev@orchestrum.in).
Describe the task, systems and expected outcome, not confidential evidence.

#### Enquiries and external messages

A demo enquiry acknowledgement means the request was received, not that email
arrived or a sales agent completed its work. SMTP acceptance, actual inbox
arrival and a reply are separate outcomes. Staff should inspect recorded delivery
states and confirm receipt in the receiving system before marking a messaging
pilot complete. Failed or uncertain sends need review, not repeated submissions.

Operators can use the [marketing delivery runbook](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/runbooks/marketing-lead-delivery.md)
for mailbox setup, protected credentials, durable worker processing and spend
controls. Customer operational messaging and tenant workflows keep their own
recipients and credentials.

#### Pilot scorecard

Track task correctness, source coverage, review effort, queue age, external-action failures, latency, cost and reopened errors. Write the sample size, time window and workload. Compare to a baseline using the same cases. Decide in advance what triggers a pause.

#### Expand and maintain

Add one new capability at a time when its real dependency is ready. Update the matching guide, prompts, regression suite and operator training together. Review documents after each behavior change; do not leave an old deployment report as the user-facing source of truth.

The public manual, current product status and deployed runtime each serve different purposes: the manual explains use, status explains boundaries, and actual release evidence proves availability. Keep all three aligned.


### Customer agent: own the agent, open the agent

URL: https://agenticorg.ai/docs/customer-agent
Audience: Bank product, risk and platform teams. Reviewed: 2026-10-11.

#### What the customer agent is

The customer agent is the bank's own assistant for its own customers. It sits in the bank's app, web, WhatsApp and voice channels, sees every product the customer holds and every product the bank can offer, answers with citations, recommends with a "why this" explanation, prepares actions for one-tap confirmation and, once a customer has set a mandate, executes inside that mandate. It runs on AgenticOrg, with Grantex as the authority service that holds every grant the customer gives, to the bank's agent and to any outside agent the customer connects.

The programme is called "own the agent, open the agent". Own the agent: the bank's assistant must be the best agent for the bank's services, so a customer has no reason to hand their finances to a general-purpose assistant. Open the agent: the bank is also the easiest institution for a customer's outside agent to connect to safely, through a governed MCP surface, Agent Passports and scoped grants the customer can see and revoke from one place. The full requirement set, market evidence, control catalogue and architecture are in the [product requirements document](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/customer-agent/PRD.md).

#### Why it is easier than an in-app assistant

Early bank assistants on the market execute a short list of actions inside one app, ask for a biometric approval on each sensitive step, and see only what the customer sees on screen. The customer agent is designed to be easier to use and to go much further, while staying inside the bank's controls:

| What the customer gets | How it works |
|---|---|
| One agent across every service | Deposits, cards, lending, mortgages, investments, insurance, payments, remittances and SME banking share one session, one memory and one permissions page. |
| Any channel, same conversation | A conversation started in the app continues on WhatsApp or by voice; the agent keeps the context, not the customer. |
| Cards instead of chat | Balances, due dates, prepared transfers and offers arrive as inline cards with one-tap confirm or cancel, never as a wall of text. |
| Approval only where it matters | An autonomy ladder from inform (L0) to execute within mandate (L4) is set per task and per customer. Routine actions inside a mandate run without a prompt; new payees and high values always step up. |
| "Why this" on every recommendation | Data used, rule or goal applied, alternatives considered, what the bank earns, and how to challenge the suggestion. |
| Whole-wallet view | With consent through Account Aggregator or open banking, the customer sees accounts held elsewhere inside the bank's agent, so comparison no longer needs an outside app. |
| One place to see and stop every agent | The permissions page lists the bank's agent and every outside agent, with scopes, caps and last action, and revokes with one tap. The revoked agent's next action is refused within seconds. |
| Open to the customer's own agent | Outside agents connect through the bank's MCP server with a verified Agent Passport and a scoped grant; the bank, not the agent provider, stays accountable for what executes. |
| Evidence for every action | Signed, hash-chained audit rows, run timelines and a per-interaction evidence package the bank can hand to an auditor. |

#### How a request moves

The same path applies in every channel. The bank keeps identity and the step-up; the agent keeps the conversation, the explanation and the record.

```flow
Sign in with the bank | The customer signs in to the bank's own app or site; the bank's backend signs a short-lived assertion and opens a customer session. | Owner: Bank identity team | If blocked: Without the bank's assertion there is no session; the platform never accepts a customer the bank has not asserted.
Disclosure | The customer reads that this is the bank's AI assistant and acknowledges it before the first turn. | Owner: Bank channel owner | If blocked: Turns are refused until the disclosure is acknowledged.
Ask | The customer asks in their own words; the dialogue recognises the intent, collects the details across turns and explains why. | Owner: Customer agent | If blocked: An unrecognised request gets a clarifying question or an offer of a person, never a guess.
Prepare | For a transaction the agent prepares a card with the amount, the payee and a "why this" panel at the customer's autonomy level. | Owner: Customer agent | Human decision: The customer confirms with one tap, cancels, or asks for a change. | If blocked: Below level 2 the action is explained and refused; the customer can raise the level on the permissions page.
Step up | Above the customer's limits, or at level 3, the bank's own passkey, biometric or one-time-code check approves the specific action. | Owner: Bank identity team | Human decision: The customer approves the exact action and amount in the bank's step-up. | If blocked: An approval for another action, customer or amount is refused and nothing runs.
Execute and record | The confirmed action runs through the bank's governed agent under its grant and is recorded with the explanation shown and the approval given. | Owner: Bank operations and system of record | If blocked: No connected agent, a paused agent or a failed rail records the action as failed and tells the customer nothing was done.
```

#### What ships today

The customer agent ships off by default behind `AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED`. With the flag off every route under `/api/v1/customer-agent/` answers 404 and nothing else changes. On, a bank gets:

| Capability | How it works |
|---|---|
| Customer sessions without a platform credential | The bank authenticates the customer as today, its backend signs a short-lived assertion (RS256 or ES256, checked against the bank's published keys, issuer and audience, single-use by its id) and exchanges it for an opaque session token. Only the token's hash is stored. |
| The autonomy ladder per task and per customer | Level 0 inform, 1 recommend, 2 prepare and wait for one tap (the default for every transaction), 3 execute after the bank's step-up of the specific action, 4 execute within a mandate with caps, counterparties and a time window. `AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_MAX_AUTONOMY` (2 by default) bounds every level. |
| Prepared-action cards | The dialogue collects the details and prepares a card; Confirm sends the same yes the dialogue expects, Cancel the same no. A card confirms only the action it shows: if the conversation moved on or the amount changed, it is superseded and nothing runs. |
| The bank's own step-up | Level 3 and out-of-mandate level 4 need a bank-signed approval bound to the action id, customer and amount, verified before the engine executes. |
| "Why this" on every answer | Data used, the rule or level applied, the mandate, alternatives, what the bank earns, how to challenge it, and the AI disclosure, assembled from the dialogue and the decision rather than generated. |
| A mandatory disclosure | Recorded on the session; no turn runs before the customer acknowledges it. |
| One permissions page | Every mandate the bank's agent holds, revocable with one call, and the authority service's dashboard of outside agents when the deployment is connected to it. |
| An embeddable element | `ui/public/customer-agent/widget.js` registers `<agenticorg-customer-agent>` for the bank's page: the disclosure gate, cards, the "why this" panel and a host event for step-ups, with no dependencies and no markup from server text. |
| Records and evidence | Sessions, mandates and every action prepared, executed, refused, cancelled or superseded, with the explanation shown and the approval given, in tenant-scoped tables under row-level security; executed actions also appear in the conversation session's record and the audit trail. |

Confirmed actions run through the bank's configured agent, its bound tools and its grant exactly as the [conversational services](/docs/bfsi-customer-service) do. The intent catalogue is deterministic and generic: no institution's products or names. Grant revocation for paused and retired agents, and an opt-in revocation check before a token is honoured (`AGENTICORG_GRANTEX_REVOCATION_CHECK=feed`), ship alongside.

The step-by-step setup for the bank's engineers, the assertion and approval formats, the element's events and every route are in the [integration guide](https://github.com/mishrasanjeev/agentic-org/blob/main/docs/customer-agent/integration.md).

#### Try it

1. In a non-production deployment, set `AGENTICORG_CUSTOMER_AGENT_ENABLED=true`, the tenant, company and agent ids, and the assertion issuer, audience and JWKS URL of a test identity provider you control. Create the agent as described in [Customer service](/docs/bfsi-customer-service) and bind the tools the intents need.
2. From your backend, sign a test assertion for a synthetic customer reference and exchange it at `POST /api/v1/customer-agent/sessions`; keep the `session_token` from the response.
3. Read `GET /session`, acknowledge the disclosure with `POST /session/acknowledge`, and send "what is my balance" to `POST /turns`: the answer carries the recognised intent and its "why this" panel.
4. Send "transfer 5000 to Ravi": the turn returns a prepared card at level 2. Confirm it with `POST /actions/{id}/confirm` (or reply yes) and inspect the run in [Run observability](/docs/run-observability); then read `GET /actions` to see the recorded action with its explanation.
5. Set a mandate with `PUT /permissions/mandates` (level 4 with a per-action cap for `fund_transfer`), repeat a transfer inside the cap and watch it run in the same turn; repeat one above the cap and watch the card ask for the bank's approval.
6. Load `widget.js` on a test page with the session token and walk the same path in the element.

Point no real customer at a deployment until the bank's identity provider, step-up and agent bindings are in place and the controls in the PRD are on.

#### What is planned

| Phase | Outcome |
|---|---|
| 0: foundations (in progress) | Shipped: grant revocation for paused and retired agents, revocation checks before a token is honoured. Next: durable conversation state by default, banking pack tools bound at creation, spend caps on every run path, and a bank deployment profile that forces the strict configuration. |
| 1: inform and recommend (in progress) | Shipped: customer sessions bound to the bank's identity, the embedded element, the autonomy ladder, "why this", the disclosure, the permissions page. Next: WhatsApp and voice in Hindi and English, L0 and L1 across the whole service range, the whole-wallet view, human hand-off with the supervisor view, nudges with control groups. |
| 2: execute with approval and open MCP | Shipped: L2 and L3 with the bank's step-up for the transaction intents in the catalogue. Next: signed intent records, the bank's MCP server and scope registry, outside agents on the permissions page with one-tap disconnect. |
| 3: mandates and agentic payments | Shipped: mandates with caps, counterparties and windows, and L4 execution inside them. Next: 90-day re-confirmation, network agent-token mirroring, Agent Passport gating. |
| 4: ecosystem | Trust-registry issuer onboarding, relying-party onboarding, signed-request verification, more Indian languages and voice providers. |

#### Design rules

- The model never holds credentials and never decides authority: grants and mandates are checked at the tool boundary and again at the bank's rail.
- Every action the agent takes is attributable to a customer, a grant and a run, and every grant can be revoked instantly.
- The agent informs and recommends by default; execution is earned per task and per customer and is demoted on the first irregularity.
- No PIN, OTP, password or card number is ever requested or accepted in conversation.
- AI involvement is disclosed at first use and on every interaction, and a human is reachable at every turn.

Next: [Capability status and gaps](/docs/bfsi-capability-status), [Customer service](/docs/bfsi-customer-service), [Approvals](/docs/approvals).
